Where resolved keys are cached, how long they live and how they rotate remain unresolved.
subsystems.dropout_logging: Accumulates diagnostic context and counters for interruptions in audio delivery. Events include group-role or stream-context changes, presentation-time conditions, missed or late frames, underflows, stream resets, silence and concealment intervals. Records also retain input type, satellite-channel information and clock validity so a report can relate an interruption to the stream and group state. Storage is bounded: an occupied slot or a full list can prevent a new entry. These measurements support dropout diagnosis, but do not guarantee that every audible interruption produces a complete record.
subsystems.dsp_config: Loads structured DSP configuration from the home-theater configuration files. It reads model-specific bonded gains and volume-to-gain breakpoint tables, checks matching array lengths and capacity limits, and converts the decoded data into runtime parameters. When bonded breakpoints are absent, the documented fallback uses the default table; a missing default table, invalid lengths, an empty file or a decoding failure is reported separately. Some numbered configuration fields still lack semantic names, so the complete configuration schema remains under investigation.
subsystems.dsp_files: Identifies the files used to configure audio processing, including equalization data, persistent EQ, default and satellite presets, and default or satellite processing binaries. The loader checks that files can be opened and sized, that output buffers are valid, and that channel maps, channel counts and version strings are acceptable. A separate gated DSP console provides live configuration and meters. This inventory establishes the available file families and loader checks; it does not mean every file is loaded in every playback mode.
subsystems.dsp_params: Exposes audio-processing settings for dynamic-range boost, speaker geometry, virtualizer mode, bass extraction and related filters and calibration blocks. Speaker angles feed the virtualizer, while dynamic parameters feed the bass-extraction and decoder processing paths. A missing named configuration can fall back to the default configuration, and invalid mode values produce parsing errors. The exact accepted numeric range of every parameter remains unresolved, so the names alone do not establish safe tuning limits.
subsystems.dts_decoder: Parses DTS audio frames and reports the detected profile, bit depth, bitrate, channel layout and dialogue-normalization gain. It checks input synchronization, frame size, sample size and supported audio modes; an invalid mode yields an empty speaker layout. The status vocabulary includes HD-MA and other extended profiles, but recognizing a profile name does not establish full decoding support. In this model-9 image, the recovered decoder path provides the shared DTS core rather than a separate HD-MA decoder, so an HD-MA status should not be read as proof of lossless HD-MA playback.
subsystems.effective_settings: Effective-settings resolution: it computes the setting value actually in force after layering defaults, household values, group values, and device overrides. This is the machinery behind the effectiveSettings API surface.
subsystems.enet_stats: Reports each Ethernet port's link state and speed, plus packet, byte, drop, multicast, collision and error counters read from the network driver. Detailed errors distinguish CRC and framing faults, FIFO and overflow problems, missed receives and transmit failures. The enetports and ethportstatistics status pages display these readings. They show the wired link's condition and accumulated traffic or faults; packet and byte totals are counters rather than a direct measurement of current throughput.
subsystems.error_codes: The error-code machinery: the tables and translation logic that turn internal failures into the numeric fault codes commands return. It's the numeric vocabulary for failures inside the program, mapped to the error codes sent over the wire.
subsystems.event_loop: Runs queued work on a pool of threads, with named execution scopes for ordinary work, mutexes, condition variables and HTTP clients. It tracks watchdog timestamps and elapsed time, records startup and failure, and shuts down when no work remains, cancelling its watchdog. The scope selected by each individual caller is still under investigation. This is one work-queue mechanism in the player; the evidence does not establish that every timer, socket or message in the process runs through it.
subsystems.eventloop_perf: Measures how much work the player's internal event delivery creates: how many events fail to queue, their sizes, time spent waiting, and time spent in each receiving handler. A handler taking more than 100 milliseconds produces a slow-callback diagnostic report; the handler still runs to completion. Repeated warning messages for the same observer are limited to roughly one every ten minutes, but that log limit does not suppress the per-occurrence diagnostic reports. Displayed durations are rounded down to whole milliseconds, so a barely-over-limit callback can appear in the log as 100ms > 100ms.
subsystems.exec_pages: Provides diagnostic pages that run predefined system commands and return their textual output. The commands list debug files, disk and memory use, loaded modules, processes, routes, sockets, clock sources, wireless scan results and bridge information. Other pages expose named log and configuration files. These outputs help inspect the player's current operating-system state; they are command output or file contents rather than a single normalized diagnostic schema.
subsystems.expat: Contains Expat 2.5.0 for parsing XML documents, including namespaces, attributes and entity references. The parser detects malformed markup, invalid encodings, duplicate attributes, undefined or recursive entities and incorrect parser-state transitions. It also includes accounting for entity-expansion amplification and optional debugging controls for that accounting, entities and entropy. This establishes a bundled XML parser and its safeguards, rather than proving that every XML consumer in the player uses this library or enables every optional feature.
subsystems.fcs_detail: Internals of an internal component abbreviated 'fcs' in build metadata: the filesystem-config-storage path in detail, recovered structurally as part of the settings persistence machinery.
subsystems.fd_event: Waits for readiness events on registered file descriptors using Linux epoll. Callers can add or remove descriptors, wait for events, and signal or reset the waiter through its internal wakeup mechanism. The object has space for 24 monitored descriptors; adding an already monitored descriptor, exceeding that capacity or supplying unsupported flags produces an error. The constructor's name identifies the instance in logs and does not configure its capacity. This allows an owner to wait for several I/O sources without polling each separately.
subsystems.fdevent: Documents the same descriptor-readiness mechanism as fd_event. Each instance registers descriptors with Linux epoll and uses an internal signal/reset path to wake a waiting thread. Its fixed storage holds 24 descriptors. Duplicate registrations, capacity exhaustion and epoll failures are reported, and unexpected events for descriptors absent from the registry are detected. This is a bounded I/O-waiting primitive; the record does not establish that every event system in the player uses it.
subsystems.feature_config: Fetches a cloud feature-configuration document over HTTPS using the player's software and hardware versions, then copies selected values into the replicated feature store. The configuration includes streaming choices, Spotify availability, telemetry, power-saving behavior, home-theater options and network settings; zone experiments can supply further overrides. Individual code paths read the stored values through getters. The registry and read sites are mapped, but the exact effect of every flag still requires its own consumer trace, so a flag name alone is not a complete feature specification.
subsystems.feature_flags: Catalogs the switches read by the player to enable or disable selected behavior. Some values are read from local settings during initialization; others arrive through cloud feature configuration and the replicated feature store. Consumers read a value and branch on it, including checks that affect whether a feature or interface is available. The flag names and read sites are known, while the full behavior controlled by each switch remains separate work. This record does not establish a universal precedence rule in which a cloud value always overrides a build default.
subsystems.fileio: Opens content as an HTTP stream, an SMB file or directory, or an in-memory stream. Cached content can avoid a new HTTP open, while directory listings use a separate path from file reads. Sonos service-reference URIs must be resolved to a concrete resource before opening; content types then select a matching parser. The layer supports prebuffering, asynchronous notifications and HTTP reopen requests with byte-offset resume information. Open failures and unsupported content types are reported, and this stream-opening record does not itself establish atomic persistence of state files.
subsystems.fmp4_parser: Extracts audio samples and metadata from fragmented MP4 streams. It checks fragment sequence and required box order, reads sample sizes and byte offsets, and verifies that sample tables fit within the available data. Track metadata supplies codec, sample rate, bit depth, channels, bitrate and loudness information; encoder delay, padding and seek offsets determine which samples are usable. Encrypted fragments require parseable initialization vectors, and sub-entry encryption is explicitly unsupported. A malformed fragment or unsupported track format can therefore fail before decoding begins.
subsystems.healthcheck: Maintains a diagnostic-check deadline, initially one day ahead. Update scheduling can request a deadline 30 minutes before an update check, and a group change can request one 45 seconds later. In this firmware the background worker waits, handles rescheduling and shutdown, and logs when the deadline has expired. It does not perform a self-test, fetch server instructions or submit diagnostics. The name can therefore be misleading: the recovered timer is deadline bookkeeping rather than proof that the player periodically tests its own health.
subsystems.healthcheck_contact: Contains a separate compiled helper for reading a server's diagnostic-submission permission. It requests a household-specific XML file with a two-minute deadline, requires a known body length below 1,024 bytes and an exact read, then accepts nested SubmitPermission text beginning with yes. A successful parse updates the remembered permission; a download or parsing failure leaves its previous value intact. No caller of this helper was found in this binary, and the health-check timer does not invoke it. The response is a permission value, rather than a general channel for executing remote maintenance commands.
subsystems.hhsettings_rest: The household-settings API inside the device: public keys readable by anyone, restricted keys needing permissions, and admin keys needing admin rights. Errors are specific, so clients can distinguish 'doesn't exist' from 'can't write'. When a component needs to read or write shared household configuration, this is the client that makes the call.
subsystems.hls_audio: Plays audio described by HLS playlists, fetching segments and tracking their playback times, byte offsets and metadata. Seeking selects a suitable segment and advances within the usable time range; a playlist containing different codec variants can force a source change. The player handles AES-128 and SAMPLE-AES key information, uses the segment sequence number when an IV is absent, and reports missing key data or undefined encryption methods. Invalid playlists, backwards sequence numbers, missing target durations and seeks beyond the end can fail. This describes the HLS path without claiming that it serves most internet-radio playback.
subsystems.hls_player: Tracks whether an HLS stream is live or static, selects bitrate variants and maps playback positions to segments. It can raise or lower bitrate, rejects unusable rendition entries and switches source when codec variants require it. Segment maps and byte ranges determine where reads start; encrypted tracks require key data and compatible decryption setup. Status reports expose playlist version, target duration, encryption and current bitrate. A failed key fetch, invalid rendition or inconsistent segment metadata can prevent playback despite a valid master-playlist URL.
subsystems.household_settings: Persists shared household configuration in householdsettings.json, with file and schema versions, an update version and the identity of the last updating device. Category records carry permission labels and lists of settings; the seeded restricted-admin category includes explicit-content filtering and recently-played configuration. Loading can upgrade the schema, migrate the old tracking-setting name or replace invalid settings. Replication distributes changes, but this does not guarantee that every player has the same values at every instant. The complete membership of categories supplied through replication remains unresolved.
subsystems.ht_audio_sources: Names the internal sources that carry TV audio through different home-theater paths: direct TV processing, the group-member downmix, audio input, and TV or channel-sink feeds for satellites. These sources connect to group and satellite mixer streams and appear in audio-session reporting. A separate operation requests a TV-session report. The names describe paths within the audio graph; they do not by themselves detect a connected television or establish which input should be selected.
subsystems.ht_telemetry: Builds a TV input-session report with session and play durations, connection type, input rate, content type and group-coordinator identity and timing. Correlation identifiers and topology information help relate the report to the group in which playback occurred. Related diagnostics measure the time spent resetting stream, decoder and processing stages, and test commands can inject stream or signal failures. Which fields the cloud requires remains unresolved; this record does not establish that the session report contains every lip-sync or hardware-health measurement.
subsystems.htaudio: Routes television audio through the soundbar's processing path and distributes the appropriate channels to bonded surrounds, subwoofers and group-member downmixes. It applies role-specific delays and gains, reacts to surround mode, channel level and input-rate changes, and tracks which satellites are active. Satellite control frames carry volume, mute and other settings alongside separately serialized multichannel audio frames. Resynchronization, disabled satellites and playback-end handling are part of the stream lifecycle. Coordinated playback depends on these paths succeeding; serialization or transmission failures can interrupt delivery.
subsystems.htaudio_chproc: Rebuilds home-theater channel routing when the TV channel map changes and updates night mode, dialogue enhancement and speech-extraction state. The input parser identifies and aligns encoded SPDIF bursts, checks repetition and padding, and responds to rate changes, discontinuities and decoder errors. TV autoplay and automatic stop use silence thresholds, with separate transitions for user interaction. This stage determines routing and valid input framing; a stereo signal does not automatically imply that it synthesizes surround audio.
subsystems.htaudio_satellite_tx: Measures audio delivery from the home-theater player to its satellites. Counters record bytes sent, transmission and serialization errors, frames sent too late, resynchronization frames, playback-end frames and peak mixer or transmitter processing time. A time-to-play measurement records the interval between sending and scheduled playback. The sender also propagates volume, mute, bass, treble and loudness changes and reports encoding or mesh-send failures. These readings help locate delivery problems, but a late frame counter alone does not establish the cause of an audible dropout or lip-sync error.
subsystems.http_cache: Classifies cached HTTP responses as missing, fresh or stale and applies directives that permit serving stale data during revalidation or after a server error. A no-store directive prevents a cache update, while private and public directives are part of the parsed policy. Cache writes also validate key and record information, and report whether data was populated, refreshed or rejected. Reusing a response depends on this policy and its current state; a repeated request can still require network access.
subsystems.http_client: Schedules outgoing HTTP operations using an asynchronous thread pool and libcurl's multi-request interface. It tracks active tasks and loop timing and reports empty URLs, missing setup, unavailable worker pools, curl failures and request timeouts. Connection handling includes address lookup and competing IPv4 or IPv6 attempts. If no active pool is available, the request is cancelled before scheduling. This is a recovered HTTP client path; other transport implementations in the player mean it cannot be described as the route for every outgoing web request.
subsystems.http_engine: The device's embedded web engine: route tables for both the main and status-site registry, static and executable page handling, request forgery protection, and the auth plumbing guarding sensitive endpoints. Everything the built-in web server runs on.
subsystems.http_headers: Sonos uses extra HTTP headers for discovery, identity, secure requests, playback and synchronization. X-Sonos-Latency is a numeric value. The colon-separated audio bookmark documented separately is carried in playback state, rather than in that header.
subsystems.httpcache: Coordinates invalidation of named HTTP caches using hashes. It persists cache-hash information, compares local and remote values and marks a local cache invalid when needed. Changed hashes are distributed so peers can discard their cached copy and fetch updated data; this is a pull-based refresh rather than delivery of the new response body. The manager also checks the writable JFFS filesystem. A missing cache cannot be invalidated, and hash propagation does not guarantee immediate consistency across all players.
subsystems.hw_events: Receives hardware notifications for buttons, orientation, temperature, power, battery and other device sources, then interprets them according to the player's current mode. Setup, household joining, playback, transfer and button-lock states can allow or suppress different actions. Button forwarding validates the destination address and port and requires a private IP address. Combined volume-button presses can start a setup timer, while orientation and diagnostic-light changes update their own state. Queue overflow, unknown events and message-read failures are reported, so not every physical event is guaranteed to become an action.
subsystems.interrupt_reasons: Names sources that can interrupt or change an audio session, including cloud control, TV playback or power state, AirPlay, audio clips, speaker or room detection, fixed volume, infrared control and voice-assistant activity. The reason provides context when a transport is suspended or an interruption is reported. The enumeration is not a priority ranking: the predicates that arbitrate competing sources still require investigation. A named reason also does not, by itself, tell the reader whether a particular event stops playback, ducks it or is ignored.
subsystems.iocompress: Wraps zlib compression and decompression for the recovered WebSocket per-message deflate path. It reports initialization, processing and finalization errors, insufficient output space and malformed compressed-stream boundaries. Cloud configuration can change whether this WebSocket compression is enabled, subject to a local override. The traced stream-wrapper caller belongs to that WebSocket path; this record does not establish that saved queues or general replication payloads use the same wrapper.
subsystems.ir_decoder: Reads infrared signals from the device and compares them with configured codes for volume up, volume down, mute and input selection. Each action list has room for ten codes, so adding another can fail when the list is full. Factory configuration comes from /opt/ir/irconfig.txt, while committed learned codes are stored in /jffs/irconfig.txt. Learning recognizes repeated, alternating and non-repeating signals and rejects inconsistent or excessively long captures. Device-open failures or an unconfigured remote prevent normal matching.
subsystems.ir_learn: Teaches the player a remote's infrared codes by capturing several passes and comparing their length and contents. It distinguishes repeat and alternating patterns and rejects captures without enough consistent information. A one-button identification flow can query the remote-code database and fail through an unknown code, timeout or capture error. Learning and committing are separate steps: committing writes the action-specific code lists to /jffs/irconfig.txt. A successful capture therefore does not by itself mean the learned configuration has been saved.
subsystems.json_parser: Documents the custom JSON parser's checks for excessive nesting, invalid escapes or characters, unexpected tokens, oversized sequences, missing values and memory exhaustion. The firmware also contains RapidJSON, with a separate error vocabulary and consumers in settings, HTTP-related code and indexing. There is no single JSON parser used by every component. The complete mapping from each subsystem to its parser remains unresolved, so an error string identifies a parser family more reliably than a universal parsing path.
subsystems.json_schema_validator: Checks decoded JSON against constraints such as required properties, allowed extra properties, string and array lengths, uniqueness, dependencies and numeric bounds. Validation failures carry the location of the offending value and information about the expected constraint. The recovered keyword behavior follows the older draft-04 form of JSON Schema, including boolean exclusive bounds and additional-item rules. This establishes the validator's supported checks; it does not prove that every settings write or API request passes through it.
subsystems.korn_events: Names events exchanged inside the embedded Spotify integration. They cover module startup and shutdown, local discovery and credential transfer, playback and track changes, seeking, shuffle and repeat, volume, stream delivery and failure, download position, and debug diagnostics. Several names distinguish a request from its later completion, such as playback resume versus resumed or stream start versus started. The enumeration identifies the event vocabulary; it does not alone establish the transition order or guarantee that a requested operation completes.
subsystems.korn_kernel: Runs the embedded Spotify modules, delivering queued events, pumping module work and managing timer slots. A temporary-memory allocator checks available space, allocation accounting and proper return of scratch memory. Recursive pump calls are ignored, a full event queue discards new events, and unavailable timer slots or failed module initialization and shutdown are reported. These checks expose resource and lifecycle failures; they do not prove that long-running sessions cannot leak memory. The complete runtime module-registration list remains unresolved.
subsystems.led_hw: Supplies the LED controller with hardware capabilities: whether the player has a microphone, mute and status lights, whether it only has a status light, whether hardware swaps LED roles, and whether white brightness is adjustable. The indicator engine uses these distinctions when choosing which light to drive. This describes the capability inputs rather than a complete product-by-product map of physical lights or a guarantee that every model can display every pattern.
subsystems.leds_zp: Chooses player indicator patterns from the current state, hardware capabilities and pattern priority. It can change white or touch-control brightness, flash feedback for buttons or infrared commands, run diagnostic patterns and restore a saved pattern after temporary feedback. Patterns contain color, hold and fade steps, repeat counts and selected LED identifiers. Applying a mode can be skipped when the engine is not ready or suspension bypass is active. The result therefore depends on both player state and the lights the device actually has.
subsystems.libflac: Bundles libFLAC 1.3.4 to read lossless FLAC streams. The decoder moves through metadata, frame synchronization and frame reading, using caller-provided read, write, seek, tell and length callbacks. It recognizes stream information, seek tables, comments, cuesheets and pictures, and checks headers, frame checksums and stream structure. Unsupported containers, invalid callbacks, unavailable seeking, memory failures and malformed streams have distinct outcomes. A FLAC resource still needs a working input stream and valid data before it can play.
subsystems.local_routes_2: A second cluster of local routes bound through a path-matcher rather than the master route table: group and zone operations like create-group, unjoin, activate, duck, and member settings. They're recorded here because they don't appear in the primary route table.
subsystems.local_settings_mgr: The local settings manager: the device's own settings files, each wrapped in a magic header with length, checksum, and counter, plus migration data and subversion detection. It's where this speaker's own config lives, distinct from household-shared values.
subsystems.log_domains: Lists the main player log and subsystem log files for alarms, playback, audio streams, hardware, HDMI, home theater, Spotify, voice and other modules. Configuration is read from the named system or persistent anacapa.conf paths, and a persistent backup of the main log is also identified. These paths help locate diagnostic output by subsystem. The inventory does not establish that each log-domain name maps to exactly one file or that every listed file is actively written on every player.
subsystems.longpress: Uses a held play/pause button to cycle through remembered, joinable group coordinators and join the next group's playback session. The list follows recent coordinator activity, removes coordinators that are no longer eligible and wraps at its end. This joins an existing session rather than copying its queue into a new independent session. A vertical-orientation event also reaches the recovered cycling path. Separately, holding both volume buttons can let a timer put the player into setup-ready mode.
subsystems.mdns: Speakers advertise their identity, addresses, secure ports and API paths through a local _sonos._tcp. service. An address refresh that skips full rebinding increases the sequence and rebuilds the advertisement, including unchanged-address notifications. Initial address acquisition and permitted rebinding do not increase it. Ordinary TXT updates skip duplicates, and receiving players do not enforce increasing sequence numbers.
subsystems.mdns_controller: Publishes local discovery advertisements so nearby controllers and players can find the Sonos and Spotify endpoints without knowing their addresses in advance. The Sonos service advertises the player's secure listener port; the Spotify service advertises its ordinary HTTP listener port. Alongside those ports, the controller maintains named TXT attributes used by the discovery clients, replaces changed values, skips identical updates and removes the advertisement on shutdown. A failed update leaves the last successfully published attributes in its cache. There is no advertisement-priority argument in this controller.
subsystems.mdns_device: The speaker announces a _sonos._tcp. service so nearby players can find its identity, addresses, secure ports and API paths. Ordinary TXT changes are updated separately and exact duplicates are skipped. An address refresh that skips full rebinding bumps the16-bit sequence and rebuilds the advertisement; this includes a notification with the same address. Initial address acquisition and permitted full rebinding do not bump it. Receiving players log and store the sequence without requiring it to increase. The counter wraps from65535 to0. This refresh can make the discovery record change even when the address has stayed the same. Household filtering exempts the local player itself; this is an identity check, rather than a general permission to accept other households.
subsystems.mdns_discovery: Reads nearby players' mDNS TXT records, checks required keys and household identity, and passes accepted peer information to the topology store. The peer data includes address, boot sequence, listener ports and discovery sequence; departures also carry a reason. Older or incomplete records, invalid discovery URLs, browse errors and unknown departing players are reported. The local-player case is treated separately from foreign-household peers. Discovery acceptance does not by itself verify that a peer can complete a secure connection or play audio.
subsystems.memmon: Samples system memory availability and free memory from /proc/meminfo, plus process memory sizes and command names from /proc. It schedules the next memory report 15 minutes later and records skipped reports with a count. Samples are retained in four rotating memory-log files, with four older copies, and those eight files are included in diagnostic bundles. This provides a history for memory-pressure investigation; the recovered monitor does not itself establish that low memory triggers a recovery action.
subsystems.memory_monitor: Documents the same memory-sampling mechanism as memmon. It reads system available and free memory and per-process memory statistics, records skipped reports, and schedules reports at 15-minute intervals. Four current logs and four older logs retain the history, and the diagnostic-bundle manifest explicitly includes them. These are periodic measurements rather than a trace of every allocation, and their collection does not by itself prove a low-memory safeguard or crashdump attachment.
subsystems.mntmgr: Mounts network music shares in temporary SMB directories and keeps track of up to 16 mount entries. It reuses an existing mount instead of mounting the same share twice and uses trial mounts to test the returned protocol. Three unsupported-protocol strikes reach the give-up path; shares are also detached when removed. HTTP addresses are rejected by this mount path. This allows library files to be read through a local mount, but the recorded unmount conditions do not establish a general idle-share timeout.
subsystems.mod_zp: A zone-player module identified by build-tree naming: part of the player-facing internals recovered structurally, inventoried as part of the complete component map.
subsystems.model_table: Lists product identifiers recognized by this firmware, including the local ZPS9 model and other ZPS, ZP120 and ANVIL identifiers. The related model vocabulary associates identifiers with capability information. Recognizing another model in a table is useful when interpreting product-specific configuration, but it does not prove that this firmware image can boot or operate correctly on every listed product. A complete compatibility decision needs the table's consumers and the build's hardware requirements.
subsystems.mp3_decoder: Decodes MP3 streams using mpg123 with additional player-specific header handling. It skips ID3 tags, reads Xing or variable-bitrate information for duration and seeking, and uses a constant-bitrate assumption when a variable-bitrate file lacks a table of contents. Corrupt data can trigger bounded frame-resynchronization attempts before failure. Unsupported descriptors, invalid sample rates, read errors and unexpected format changes have separate handling; a block immediately after an unexpected format change is discarded. This means duration and seeking can be approximate when indexing metadata is missing.
subsystems.mpegts_id3: Unpacks MPEG transport streams by reading program tables, selecting an audio packet identifier and separating audio from timed-ID3 metadata. Presentation timestamps help relate payloads to playback, while bounds checks reject malformed table or metadata lengths and oversized ID3 tags. Extracted ID3 fields enter the stream-metadata path so supported title or artist information can change with the stream. A missing audio identifier or unsupported stream type can fail parsing. Which individual music services use this format remains configuration-dependent and unresolved.
subsystems.netif_monitor: Receives interface-link information from kernel netlink messages and handles readiness, reset, exception and timeout notifications. It checks message types and reports read errors or unexpected messages, allowing the player to react when network-interface state changes. This record overlaps the address-monitor investigation, but it does not establish a separate ordered subscriber list or prove that every connectivity consumer receives each notification immediately.
subsystems.netstart_events: Names the messages exchanged with the network-startup daemon about setup, Wi-Fi state, network bounces, connection type, household changes and WAC setup mode. The player can rebind after an IP change, clear link-local subscriptions, or defer and suppress changes while shutting down. Connection-type labels distinguish Ethernet, wireless SonosNet and home-theater paths. Satellite additions are also reported to the daemon. These notifications describe network and setup transitions; an alive or setup-stop message alone is not proof that all later network requests will succeed.
subsystems.noderx: Receives framed audio packets from other players, tracks packet order and buffered ranges, and requests retransmission when gaps require it. Startup can suppress requests for a large initial gap, and partial or discontinuous frames have separate rejection rules. Packet-version checks, duplicate handling, buffer limits and frame-length checks protect the receive path. Resynchronization flushes packet ranges, while a read timeout or framing failure can force decoder reset. These mechanisms recover some missing data without guaranteeing uninterrupted playback under every loss condition.
subsystems.nodetx: Sends framed audio blocks to other players and retains packet ranges for retransmission. Receivers can request missing packet identifiers; the sender checks protocol compatibility, resends available eligible packets and refuses stale or unsendable ranges. Separate control frames schedule or force resynchronization and mark transmission end, and counters distinguish data sends from retransmission requests. This is an audio-delivery transport rather than a general channel for broadcasting player status. Some peer-side packet-class meanings remain unresolved.
subsystems.nslookup_detail: The name-lookup diagnostic page detail: a permission gate plus a lookup routine driven by a parameter table. It's one of the tools-page commands, listed separately because it resolves names on demand for network debugging.
subsystems.overrideconfig: The config-override endpoint: a form submission that commits an override file with strict validation and a success redirect. It's the engineering mechanism for config overrides that survive reboot, a deliberate escape hatch over the normal config stores.
subsystems.perf_counters: Collects named measurements such as processed-frame counts and bytes, frame sizes, prebuffered audio, time between frames, blocked sends and queue expiry. Reports group counters into time windows with timestamps, descriptions and, where applicable, minimum, average and maximum values. Window rotation rejects backwards time. Modules register their own counters, so the recovered schema explains how measurements are represented without establishing the complete set present in every running player.
subsystems.perfect_sync: Provides a switch that forces the audio path's initial-synchronization handling. Diagnostics report the candidate synchronization time and available data, and the forced path can ignore a measured time difference that would otherwise affect the synchronization check. This record covers that startup override, rather than the full clock-synchronization algorithm for grouped playback. The recovered messages do not establish a quantitative guarantee about how closely every speaker remains synchronized afterward.
subsystems.player_settings: Manages device-specific options for volume mode, mono playback, Wi-Fi and mesh use, power saving, battery and Bluetooth policies, line-in, EQ and gain trim. Hardware and current mode constrain changes: fixed output may be unsupported, pass-through volume mode disallows EQ adjustment, and satellite settings may need to be changed on the primary device. Network changes can be refused by the network-startup daemon, including disabling Wi-Fi without an Ethernet carrier. A stored request therefore still needs to pass model, mode and network checks before it takes effect.
subsystems.product_models: Associates product model identifiers with names used in audio configuration, including public product names and development codenames. The DSP configuration lookup uses the player's model to select parameter data and reports a failed lookup. These names help interpret model-specific logs and configuration tables. Some per-model numeric fields are recovered without their semantic names, so a row's presence does not yet explain every tuning value or prove that the firmware supports that product operationally.
subsystems.protocol_info: Advertises resource formats through protocol-info strings that pair a transport or Sonos URI scheme with a content type. The vocabulary covers direct HTTP and network-file resources, common audio formats, playlists and adaptive-stream manifests, as well as Sonos queue, group and service references. Some advertised entries are references or metadata conventions that must be resolved before a real stream can open. Matching an advertised format therefore describes a recognized resource type, rather than guaranteeing that a command is accepted or that the resource can be downloaded and decoded.
subsystems.qplay: The QPlay integration: the Tencent QQ Music casting feature, covering the machinery behind the auth handshake and the session that streams audio afterward. It's a China-market feature, dormant elsewhere.
subsystems.radiolog: The radio diagnostic surface: radio-related event logging exposed through the status pages, covering station tuning, stream errors, and metadata events. It's useful when a stream plays but metadata or tuning behaves oddly.
subsystems.rdmbuttonfwd_detail: The button-forwarding endpoint's behavior: it checks authentication and whether the player is in remote-diagnostics mode, and only then do physical button presses get forwarded to the remote observer. Otherwise requests are rejected.
subsystems.reporting: Connects several kinds of reports to their respective submission paths. Playback reports include service and account identifiers, codec, timing, end or skip reasons and errors, and can be sent periodically or when playback ends. Dropout, TV-session and Spotify reports have their own schemas, while crash dumps use a separate Sentry upload path with files, tags and attachments. Collection and upload follow the policy of the particular reporter, rather than a single rule for all telemetry. The name of the message field that supplies the playback-report interval remains unresolved.
subsystems.runtime_policy: The runtime policy object: it consults the config and settings stores to decide allowed-versus-disallowed outcomes for feature gates that depend on live configuration rather than build flags. It's the rule-check layer applied to operations and settings at execution time.
subsystems.select_thread: Waits for events from registered I/O handlers using epoll. It manages adding and removing users and descriptors, uses an interrupt descriptor to wake the wait, and checks whether a handler changed its descriptor without updating registration. Errors cover too many users, duplicate watches, failed epoll operations and inconsistent registrations. Named handlers include infrared, hardware events, interface monitoring, discovery, ARP and IPC. Their actual descriptor numbers are runtime data; this is a shared waiting mechanism rather than proof of one main loop for the whole process.
subsystems.sentry_upload: The crash-dump pipeline: upload endpoints plus the daemon proxies, collecting dump files for each daemon and shipping them to the crash-upload service. It's how crash reports reach Sonos's error tracking after a failure.
subsystems.sethostip_detail: The host-address override endpoint detail: a gate plus a routine that sets the host address and responds. It's one of the engineering endpoints, wired through a different route than the normal pages.
subsystems.shoutcast: Opens internet-radio streams that return either an ICY success response or an HTTP success response. It follows supported redirects, including playlist redirection, and asks the server to include ICY metadata. Inline metadata updates the stream title, while supported private-frame data can supply other metadata or artwork URLs. The request deliberately includes a Winamp-compatible user-agent string. Connection, buffer, end-of-stream or I/O failures can stop the read, and metadata is available only when the server supplies a supported form.
subsystems.shutdown_reasons: Names causes recorded for idle, suspension and shutdown transitions, including API requests, a disappearing partner, recovery, user suspension, user shutdown and critical shutdown. Bluetooth-related activity has its own reason label, and unknown shutdowns are represented explicitly. These labels provide context for power-state changes and are serialized through the power-management interface. The enumeration alone does not define which event wins when several reasons compete or prove that every named reason immediately powers the player off.
subsystems.shutdown_seq: Records the player's teardown order: stop the HTTP client and zone-player work, then the asynchronous Muse pool and internal event distributor, followed by zone reset, dropout handling, timed jobs and the remaining asynchronous pool before the final section. Ordering these stops reduces work arriving after its owner has been torn down. The recovered sequence identifies cleanup stages; it does not guarantee that every in-flight operation finishes or every state write succeeds during shutdown.
subsystems.signal_source: Plays an acoustic room-detection chirp on a selected output channel. Only one signal may run at a time, and stopping it requires the identifier of the currently playing instance. Invalid channels, incorrect identifiers, no active signal, stream-creation failure and policy restrictions produce errors. This is the controlled room-detection signal path, rather than a generic origin for every tone or calibration signal in the player.
subsystems.smb: Reads music from network shares using parsed SMB or UNC paths and supplied credentials. Directory traversal can reconnect after a failure, reopen the directory and advance to the last known entry to resume indexing. Retries are bounded and can fail if the share cannot be reached, the path is not a directory, metadata cannot be loaded or the previous entry cannot be found. The share and mount layers also impose capacity and protocol checks. Recovery helps continue a walk, but does not guarantee the directory stayed unchanged while disconnected.
subsystems.sntp: Maintains timing used by grouped audio, requesting clock information from the group coordinator and supporting local virtual-clock servers. It estimates offset and rate, adjusts within limits, and tracks uncertainty and repeated request failures. Samples that move time backwards are discarded, and the audio path can transition between an audio-derived clock and system time. Diagnostic statistics record success, threshold crossings and clock quality. This describes the clock-control mechanisms and their checks without promising sample-exact synchronization under all conditions.
subsystems.socket_hal: Provides the embedded Spotify SDK with platform socket operations for DNS lookup, listening, connecting, accepting, reading and closing connections. It also sets options for address reuse, multicast behavior and nonblocking I/O. This recovered platform path creates IPv4 sockets and reports IPv6 as unsupported. Invalid hostnames, absent DNS callbacks, socket errors and disconnected reads have explicit outcomes. Per-call timeout values remain unresolved, so the wrapper inventory does not specify how long every Spotify operation can wait.
subsystems.sonarctl_detail: The /sonarctl endpoint detail: a control surface for the room-detection acoustic subsystem, gated like the other engineering endpoints. An internal handle on the chirp machinery used during setup.
subsystems.sonoscp: Maps content objects to music-service resource URLs using service identity, content type and an appropriate account. It rejects unsupported objects or invalid service IDs and can fail when no default account is available or a service URL cannot be generated. For cloud-queue items it caches resolved track URLs and invalidates that cache when needed. This connects catalog entries to fetchable audio resources; resolving or caching a URL does not guarantee successful playback. Parts of the protected-data unpacking modes remain unresolved.
subsystems.sound_device: Connects the audio output pipeline to the device driver, handling device access and checking channel count and sample-width consistency. It includes sample-rate conversion, with a setting that can bypass conversion on the main output path, and reports amplifier, voltage, temperature and other hardware-health flags. These flags are shared across products; their presence in the binary does not mean every corresponding sensor exists on this soundbar. The exact live hardware-flag set for this board remains unresolved.
subsystems.sound_swap: Coordinates a request to move an audio session between players. It selects push, pull or no-action behavior, checks candidate topology and playback eligibility, and can disband the initiating or target group as part of the handoff. Bonded zones, home-theater satellites, unsuitable audio and an already active swap can prevent it. Progress and result records track targets, responses and outcomes, while a failed state transition resets the controller. Some group-disband failures are logged and the attempt continues, so a swap request is not a guarantee of a clean or completed handoff.
subsystems.spdif_burst: Names the encoded burst types used by the digital-audio parser and related reporting, including Dolby and DTS families, null or pause bursts and unsupported data types. The associated writer checks burst size and frame boundaries, while decoder counters identify errors by format. These are recognition and diagnostic categories, rather than a list of formats this model can necessarily decode or output. In particular, a named advanced Dolby or DTS format should not be treated as proof of playback support.
subsystems.spdif_detect: Identifies encoded digital-audio bursts by checking their preamble words, payload type, repetition stride and padding. The parser confirms a candidate, aligns to the burst boundary and reports anomalies or unsupported formats; input-rate changes, discontinuities and signal loss can change its state. These checks help distinguish encoded audio from PCM patterns that merely resemble a preamble. Recognizing a burst selects a possible decoding path, but successful detection does not establish that this product supports decoding every named format.
subsystems.spotify: Groups the records for the player's Spotify integration: the embedded SDK, local discovery and authentication, Connect session handoff, audio delivery, service integration and supporting server or CDN connections. The local Spotify service is advertised through mDNS, with guards against duplicate registration or removal without a service identifier. The detailed behavior lives in the individual component records; this umbrella does not imply one execution path for every Spotify operation.
subsystems.spotify_connect: Bridges embedded Spotify events to the player's playback session. Callbacks report connection changes, volume updates, stream end and seek requests, while track bookkeeping separates current, next, previous and pending tracks. Playback identifiers are checked before size or completion updates are accepted, and position handling has fast resume or seek paths as well as slower restart paths. Queue-end handling suppresses a spurious playback-start event. These checks coordinate a Connect session with local playback, rather than making every activation an unconditional takeover of an existing group.
subsystems.spotify_smapi_ctrl: The Spotify service-integration bridge: the layer that lets a Connect session appear as a controllable media source, translating between component callbacks and the Sonos transport and queue model. It's the Sonos-side control path for the Spotify integration.
subsystems.spotify_thread: Serializes work for the embedded Spotify integration, allowing only one request in progress at a time. It handles login and logout, playback, seeking, volume, metadata, display-name and grouped-state updates, and reports operation timeouts or SDK failures. Login attempts check user changes and username length; a source switch can initiate asynchronous logout. Telemetry and repeated fatal-error reporting are rate-limited. The recovered queue and timeout behavior explains possible delayed or failed commands without establishing that most failures are silent.
subsystems.spotify_vli_session: Carries embedded Spotify playback into the player's virtual-line-in audio session. Session callbacks start, pause, stop or suspend audio and propagate play-mode changes and track metadata. During delegation or state changes, selected flush, seek, track and inactivity events are ignored to avoid interfering with the handoff. Session cookies reject an old stop request aimed at a newer session. Adaptive bitrate can lower quality after repeated buffering errors and later raise it again. Source selection, active state and session identity therefore matter alongside the requested playback operation.
subsystems.spotify_zeroconf: Spotify's local discovery layer: the Connect advertisement, device-added events, credential transfer, and the local web server the Connect handoff uses. This is how the Spotify app discovers and pairs to the speaker on your network.
subsystems.spotifyzc: The zero-config discovery layer the Spotify Connect integration uses: events for device-added, credential transfer, and auth tokens that let a phone hand the speaker a Spotify session. How 'play on this speaker' works in the Spotify app.
subsystems.ssh_keys: The authorized-keys management: gated install and removal of SSH public keys, which is an engineering and debug feature rather than a consumer surface. The gate means it only works when the device is in a permitted state.
subsystems.ssl_sessions: The speaker saves reusable TLS sessions so later secure connections can resume instead of performing a full handshake. Internet and household connections have separate caches, each limited to 32 sessions in this build. Sessions use the server ticket lifetime, or 24 hours when no lifetime is supplied. Saved cache files are consumed and deleted at startup; saving later recreates them. Household sessions can be refreshed while the device is idle. A cache miss falls back to a normal secure handshake. Hostnames compare without case sensitivity, and the least recently accessed session is replaced when a partition is full. Refreshing entries are temporarily unavailable for reuse.
subsystems.stream_fetcher: Fetches playlists and audio segments while tracking how much playable audio remains buffered. Empty playlists can cause another fetch, a source switch or failure when no audio remains; a static playlist has an explicit end. The fetcher selects stream variants, tracks quality changes, prebuffers data and obtains content keys for encrypted HLS. Its decisions depend on both available sources and time left in the buffer, so a temporary fetch error is not always recoverable before playback runs out.
subsystems.stream_metadata: Keeps stream metadata with a reference time so titles and other updates can be related to playback. Sources include ICY radio metadata, timed ID3, MP4 or MP3 metadata and Spotify track notifications. Invalid reference times are rejected. The surrounding resource-resolution path also records URL expiry, chooses a framer and rejects unexpected content such as HTML. Caching avoids losing the current metadata between updates, but the recovered record does not establish that all listeners share one parse result or that metadata is always available.
subsystems.stream_playback: Controls playback state, frame timing and buffering while enforcing content and queue policies. Pause expiry, queue expiry, explicit-content restrictions and stop-on-error rules can pause, clear or stop playback. Frame scheduling waits when audio is ahead, records when it is behind and requests resynchronization after a buffering underflow. Track boundaries, startup hints and crossfading also affect progression. The engine records recovery when an underflow clears; it does not guarantee that every network interruption can be hidden from the listener.
subsystems.sync: Collects the findings about synchronized group audio: coordinator clock information, initial alignment and rate correction that keeps a member following the group's timing reference. The implementation is spread across the SNTP, initial-sync and audio-rate-control records rather than recovered as one standalone module. Here synchronization means coordinating audio time; this record is not an inventory of thread locks and does not promise that every grouping condition produces echo-free playback.
subsystems.telemetry: Defines event envelopes with a name, schema version, category, timestamp and player or household identity, plus context such as audio type. It distinguishes older and newer event callbacks and assigns categories to uploaders with configured intervals and exemption policy. In the shipped revision-13 configuration, only three of 104 categories are enabled by default: now-playing reports, maintenance and quarantining. Runtime configuration can change that selection. Category enablement and uploader policy must both be considered before inferring whether an event is collected or sent.
subsystems.telemetry_client: Encodes telemetry events with their name, schema version, category and device context, then hands them to a sender thread rather than making an HTTP request inside the event callback. The recovered sender posts a binary body over HTTPS to /data/submit.aspx, marked as product-data telemetry. Encoding failures, absent callbacks and rate limits can prevent submission. This record establishes the encoding and transport handoff; it does not by itself prove automatic retries or eventual delivery of every event.
subsystems.thermal: Reads CPU, amplifier and system-chip temperatures, omitting the hardware's absent-sensor value, and reports hardware warning or fault transitions. Hardware condition can clamp the allowed volume, with the resulting limit exposed in state and diagnostics. The kernel classifies temperature status using board-specific policy; the application does not contain all Celsius thresholds. These mechanisms explain reduced output under a hardware warning, while the numeric trip points and every possible shutdown consequence remain outside this record's evidence.
subsystems.timed_jobs: Schedules named maintenance tasks such as network-key rotation, missed-player checks, certificate fetching, log backup and TLS-cache refresh or saving. A job carries its next scheduled time, and removal can cancel a queued add or wait for running work to finish. Diagnostics report jobs that run slowly, consecutive slow runs and a return to normal duration. The registry identifies scheduled work and lifecycle handling; an individual task's interval and side effects need its own record rather than a universal cron-like schedule.
subsystems.tj_wakeup: Schedules attempts to wake missing players and retries them until the attempt completes, is cancelled or times out. One request type resolves players through household topology; another uses a direct device-registry lookup. Both feed the same wake-and-retry worker, which returns the next wake time or a value that prevents rescheduling. Shutdown drops pending timers or requests, and unknown event types are rejected. This is the missing-player wake path, rather than proof that all scheduled jobs automatically wake a suspended device.
subsystems.tp_enums: Names the values used in Trueplay calibration messages: speaker layouts, channel types and direction, product-array families, tone handling, tuning and measurement modes, subwoofer polarity and device orientation. Unspecified values are present alongside concrete choices such as individual-channel versus mono tuning and spatial versus spectral measurement. These tables make calibration messages interpretable, but the mapping from every array type to its DSP parameter values remains unresolved. A named layout does not mean this player supports every calibration configuration.
subsystems.track_pipeline: Tracks embedded Spotify audio from download and decryption through delivery to the player integration and reported playback position. It records delivered samples, download and integration latency, track completion, underruns and position synchronization. Seek and resume can require redelivery, while track identity and position checks reject inconsistent integration reports. Loading a decryption key or fully delivering a track is a different milestone from finishing its audible playback; the pipeline records both delivery and playing progress.
subsystems.track_play_monitor: Records played segments together with track or station identity, metadata, stream context, packet position and errors. Stream and playback events mark opens, closes, boundaries, interruptions and resynchronization, allowing reports to relate audio activity to a specific segment. Storage is bounded: exhausted entry or string pools can reset tracking, full containers can overwrite records, and zero-sample segments are cancelled. This is evidence about what played and when; the record does not establish that it alone supplies the recently-played list or every scrobbling result.
subsystems.trueplay: Coordinates an acoustic calibration session, selecting compatible tuning components and the required tone files. It checks tone-file identifiers, supports different measurement or detection modes, and can clip the requested calibration volume. Session cleanup removes temporary tuning assets and restores relevant audio, surround and transport settings, with different restoration behavior in Trueroom mode. Asset fetch, version compatibility and cleanup can fail. This record describes the player's calibration orchestration rather than the complete phone workflow or every coefficient calculated from a measurement.
subsystems.trueplay_api: Creates and configures a Trueplay SDK node for measurement and data computation. The factory selects a supported SDK version, treats a request for the version already in use as a no-op and can fall back to a previous implementation when a requested version is unsupported. Setup checks microphone and DSP-channel counts and enforces restrictions for a minimal node build. Node messages and schema versions govern compatibility. This is the internal calibration interface; it is not evidence that every product supports the same node features.
subsystems.ttm_helper_detail: The time-to-music measurement endpoint detail: an engineering endpoint that times how long a play command takes end to end. It's a performance probe for the play path.
subsystems.tv_processor: Processes incoming TV audio through reading, parsing, decoding, silence detection and writing stages, with separate waiting, monitoring and error states. It reads digital channel-status information, detects PCM or encoded audio, selects a decoder and reacts to sample-rate, channel-count or input-format changes. Status output exposes signal activity, mode, stream format, channel layout and active decoder. Disagreements between source and parser, invalid bursts and decoder errors can interrupt that path. This is part of the audio pipeline itself, rather than only TV control or session bookkeeping.
subsystems.unlock: The engineering unlock endpoint: a challenge-and-response state toggle with auth checks and a rate limit. When unlocked, additional diagnostic surfaces open up, and production devices keep it closed.
subsystems.update_coordinator: Starts and coordinates a firmware-update attempt inside the player. It rejects a second start while an update is already running, loads certificate and metadata information for verification, checks cloud settings and the allowed software-generation downgrade floor, and writes update information for the upgrade manager. The separate upgrade manager performs the per-player download and installation work. Failures in querying settings, verification data or version policy can prevent progress; this record does not establish that most installation delays have one particular cause.
subsystems.upgrade: Checks the update server and interprets its manifest response, including the latest software-generation header, redirects, update type and result status. It supports cached-only checks and applies downgrade restrictions before the remaining update machinery proceeds. These checks determine whether an update candidate is available and permitted; they are distinct from downloading, installing and rebooting into it. Two opaque signing-related identifiers are recovered without a complete producer-side interpretation, so their exact semantic distinction remains unresolved.
subsystems.usage_metrics: Builds periodic usage and health reports containing controller or content-provider activity, wireless counters, per-access-point signal and packet-error measurements, CPU-temperature history and hardware-warning information. It can retain audio-drop information for a later periodic submission, and fetches configuration for polling and wireless thresholds. The uploader checks the usage-sharing setting, including the NoReport opt-out value. Collecting a counter and uploading its report are separate steps; this record does not justify treating every usage report as governed by the same policy as every diagnostic path.
subsystems.user_update: Runs a household firmware-update check requested by the user, downloads the manifest, identifies devices needing an update and launches the rollout. It distinguishes no available update from manifest failure, no eligible devices, device-check failure and launch failure. Progress comes from upgrade-manager reports, which can time out while being polled; if a report exceeds the supported device count, some entries are omitted from the status event. The predicate choosing the next household member remains unresolved, and starting the flow does not guarantee every device updates.
subsystems.virtual_linein: The virtual line-in subsystem: the machinery for audio pushed at the player by an external source, covering session management behind the VLI commands and service.
subsystems.vli: Connects virtual-line-in sources to group audio through a source manager, transmit sink, playback tracking and control callbacks. Sources can include AirPlay, Bluetooth and other internally adapted inputs. Selection and activation can fail, and session cookies distinguish the current source from stale control events. Group transmission may wait for retransmission to finish, while completion signals can time out. A virtual-line-in session therefore adapts a source into the group-audio path; it is not limited to audio originating outside Sonos.
subsystems.vli_ctrl: The virtual-line-in control interface: the event grammar, the format whitelist, the metadata extractor for pushed items, and the address-to-service routing. It's the control plane for external sources feeding the player.
subsystems.vli_transport: Activates a virtual-line-in source from its stream reference and configures whether playback should start and whether this player becomes the group coordinator. It starts transmission and tracks completion events, but rejects incompatible source types or node-protocol versions and can fall back to stopped or deferred playback. Remote line-in also carries source and group-coordinator context. These checks describe setup and delivery failure paths; they do not establish that every source change is a seamless handoff.
subsystems.voice_skill: Tracks the authorization state used when linking the Alexa voice skill. Fields record whether a token exists, the current skill stage, regional authorization codes, redirect URLs and a timeout. The player's Alexa code-based-linking capability and account or setup settings determine whether that path is available. A token or authorization-code field describes progress in linking, rather than proof that voice requests will work. Complete configuration fields for each voice service remain cloud-document data and are not fully recovered here.
subsystems.wifi: Coordinates Wi-Fi-related policy and observations while the network-startup daemon and wireless stack perform radio configuration. It maintains idle-scan reasons such as audio use, SonosNet peers, upgrading and home-theater swap, and publishes polled interface health and signal strength. Its CrAssoc records measure controller discovery, ARP and device-description or group-notification stages; they are not Wi-Fi station-authentication records. Network changes can require IPC or polling updates, so an observed wireless mode is distinct from a completed configuration change.
subsystems.wireless_modes: Reports whether the player uses SonosNet, Ethernet, ordinary Wi-Fi station mode or one of the satellite and primary-uplink combinations. The wireless status document also includes connection type, idle state, busy clients and whether SonosNet is disabled. A special SonosNet-disable test can schedule an automatic revert. Mode names describe the reported radio role; they do not alone define every transition or prove current connectivity. The meanings of the idle-state bits remain unresolved.
subsystems.zpinfo_dpimpl: The ZPInfo diagnostic surface: the device-info document schema (attributes, network info, support fields) plus the ethernet-port statistics and shutdown-log surfaces. The structured 'everything about this unit' report for support.
subsystems.audio_in: The line-in input path: the machinery for audio arriving on the physical input jack. On this build the network-facing service is a reject-everything stub, but the lower capture machinery exists in the shared codebase, which is why the service advertises commands at all.
subsystems.esdk_internals: Identifies the bundled Spotify embedded SDK and its integration checks. Initialization validates the API version, device type, supplied memory, unique identity and display-name or alias configuration. Notifications distinguish login, reconnection, temporary errors, active-device changes and track or stream events. Failures include missing connection state, invalid credential data, event overflow and playback logging problems that can force logout. This is the recovered SDK integration map, rather than proof that all Connect behavior is implemented by one module.
subsystems.ws_client: Opens outgoing WebSocket sessions by checking the HTTP upgrade response and negotiating extensions. Per-message deflate must be established before the connection opens, and unsolicited compression is rejected. Session retries and disconnect reasons cover network-address changes, power, updates, sleep and reconnection. Status records show time open or closed, failures, ping activity, message counts and compressed or uncompressed traffic. These readings distinguish a live transport from a failed handshake, but an open connection does not guarantee that every application message succeeds.
subsystems.auto_update: Schedules household firmware-update attempts according to the configured policy, check interval and update window. An upcoming alarm or active device can block an attempt, and the scheduler can shorten the usable window. It tracks session state, attempts, start and target versions and per-device results, retries within its limit and reports when it gives up. The household member-selection predicate remains unresolved. Automatic scheduling therefore creates an opportunity to update; it does not guarantee installation every night or on every player.
subsystems.smartplay: Attempts to obtain and start content after a button trigger or when the current transport is empty, subject to feature configuration. It requests content through the bridge-content service, parses the reply and loads the selected content for the target group. Timings record the fetch and load stages, and separate errors identify failed retrieval, parsing or playback loading. This can supply content when there is nothing queued, but the record does not establish how the cloud chooses a recommendation or guarantee that the chosen item starts successfully.
subsystems.settings: Groups the configuration records for household values, device-specific options, local file storage, replicated settings and cloud feature configuration. Effective settings represent the values selected for use after the relevant configuration layers are applied. Each component has its own validation, persistence and update behavior, documented in the linked records. This is an overview of the distributed settings system rather than evidence of a single store or one universal precedence rule for every key.
subsystems.chanmapset: Builds and validates sets used to describe channel assignments. An initializer that exceeds capacity is truncated, and duplicate entries are reported. Related synchronization exchanges compare each indexed entry's device identity and state with local data, then record the identity supplying an update. These structures support keeping assignments consistent between players. Some phase writers remain unenumerated, so this record does not yet establish the complete state sequence or every bonded-speaker role transition.
subsystems.esdk_api: Lists the calls exposed by the embedded Spotify SDK to the player integration. They register callbacks, log in or out, configure device names and grouping, control playback and volume, seek, manage shuffle and repeat, queue resources and report stream or track information. Platform callbacks supply DNS, sockets and TLS, while an event-pump call advances SDK work. This API inventory identifies available entry points; it does not establish that every call is used or that a request completes synchronously.
subsystems.esdk_socket: Implements network access beneath the embedded Spotify SDK, including DNS request queueing, IPv4 sockets and socket reuse. It parses resource URLs, reads and writes HTTP headers and manages data channels to Spotify servers. IPv6 is explicitly unsupported in this platform path. A full DNS queue, no free socket, insufficient buffer space, invalid headers or connection errors can stop an operation. These resource limits and error paths explain why SDK network activity can fail before audio reaches the player.
subsystems.esdk_callbacks: Defines how the embedded Spotify SDK calls back into the player and its platform services. Playback callbacks notify state, seeking and volume; stream callbacks deliver data, start or end a stream, flush it and query position using a stream identifier. Other callbacks handle credentials, device aliases, DNS, socket operations, TLS and errors. Registration and removal are recorded. The exact ordering of all callbacks remains unresolved, so the list describes the communication points rather than a universal session sequence.
subsystems.esdk_crypto: Contains cryptographic checks used by the embedded Spotify login path, including large-integer modular arithmetic, signatures, SHA-1-related buffers and platform random-byte generation. The code checks workspace sizes and reports login or signature-allocation failures. These findings establish components of the authentication implementation, while the exact greeting-packet field layout and key derivation remain unresolved. Naming the primitives therefore does not yet describe the full protocol or justify assuming how every session key is produced.
subsystems.esdk_events: Encodes and sends diagnostic events from the embedded Spotify SDK, including playback statistics, playback or HTTP errors, downloads and capability information. End-of-song records include played duration and track identity, while errors can include playback and device identifiers, resource URL, host and response status. The recovered event destination is the SDK's hwp-events logging channel. Missing identifiers, encoding failures and send failures are reported. These diagnostic events are distinct from callbacks that directly control local playback.
subsystems.esdk_httpio: Formats and reads HTTP requests within the embedded Spotify SDK. It handles redirects and byte-range responses, checks content-range against the requested offset, and rejects unsupported transfer or content encoding. Malformed header boundaries, missing URL host or scheme, DNS errors, socket EOF and operation timeouts can fail a fetch. This is the SDK's web-data path, including CDN reads; the numeric request-pipeline depth remains unresolved.
subsystems.watchdog: Registers named clients with health-check callbacks and runs those checks at a configured interval. It rejects invalid frequencies, missing callback functions and duplicate client names. An unresponsive client or manual trigger records the event and can invoke /sbin/reboot, with the command result logged. The driver interface and watchdog capture files provide related diagnostic state. This mechanism depends on registered checks and successful recovery actions; it does not prove that every possible software hang is detected or that every reboot attempt succeeds.
subsystems.trueplay_service: The Trueplay room-tuning interface: eight methods covering setup, spatial and satellite tuning, clearing, and reading back tunings, plus its status codes. On this Playbar build the whole interface is present but inert: the service object and its method table are fully constructed, yet every method is a placeholder, because Playbar has no microphone and literally cannot tune itself even though the service shell exists.
subsystems.spec_object_table: The master vocabulary for the whole cloud-API schema system: a table of 331 entries where every type name, field name, event name, and namespace label lives. Number codes inside each operation's spec index into this table to spell out that operation's fields, and both directions of the lookup were found in the binary, which is what proved the numbering scheme beyond doubt.
subsystems.spec_pair_stream: How every modern-API command's field list is stored: each operation's spec lives in a packed table of small numbers pointing into the master vocabulary table, recovered as a complete field-name dictionary. It's the compressed form of the API's argument lists.
subsystems.muse_verb_ns_registry: The complete menu of commands the cloud protocol supports, organised as namespace/verb pairs: 'authorization.resolveToken' means the resolveToken command inside the authorization group. It's the two-part naming system behind every modern-API operation.
subsystems.spec_descriptors: The full type system behind the cloud API: 383 machine-readable descriptions of every request, response, event, and data structure the protocol uses. Each is a schema the engine can validate messages against, making it the API's complete grammar.
subsystems.diag_build_artifact: Documents a separate factory and retail diagnostic image rather than the main firmware under analysis. It contains production audio-test modes, synchronization and wireless controls, serial capture files and lockup dumps. A retail-display form controls demo behavior, inactivity timeout and model-specific volume options. Embedded redaction recipes remove sensitive settings fields before diagnostic output is shared. Findings from this older image help explain test and support tooling, but should not be treated as proof that the main player build runs the same handlers or workflows.
subsystems.ducking: Tracks requests to lower playback volume temporarily using per-source flags that can be forwarded to group members. A heartbeat expires remote flags, and a local request flag has a timeout, so some abandoned requests can be cleared. Policy can drop requests when ducking is disabled, TV is playing or the device's voice behavior requires it; a full pending list or failed forwarding can also interfere. Status reports expose whether playback is ducked and the active flags. These mechanisms support temporary attenuation, but do not guarantee that every member lowers and restores volume simultaneously.
subsystems.libsonos_certval: Verifies device certificates in a shared library using trust-root bundles, certificate identity checks and validation status. Root bundles include a header, manifest and certificates; the loader selects a versioned bundle, has a fallback, checks hashes and watches for file changes. Updates use a temporary file and rename, and bad or unused bundles can be removed. This makes trust data separately updateable from the main player program, while a bundle update or presented certificate still has to pass validation before it can be used.
subsystems.netconfig_fsm: Runs the shell-script steps for changing network mode. Modes cover SonosNet, ordinary Wi-Fi, satellite links, an open setup access point, credential checking and an isolated configuration without an Ethernet uplink. Credential checking tests proposed Wi-Fi data before committing it. The open setup path configures the local access point at 10.69.69.1, while station and satellite modes set up their bridge and supplicant configuration. The script coordinates several operations; selecting a mode does not guarantee that all radio, authentication and bridge changes succeed.
subsystems.rootfs_boot_chain: Describes startup through /etc/Configure: mount virtual and persistent filesystems, create RAM-backed working directories, load drivers, inspect factory-reset requests and prepare networking and daemon startup. Reset-check results select different network reset paths. A persistent /jffs/Configure file can replace the rest of the standard script, and development-build conditions provide additional overrides. The init configuration separately starts and respawns named daemons.
