This establishes the recovered startup sequence without claiming that every boot decision is controlled by one script or that all paths have been verified safe.
subsystems.rootfs_data_files: Inventories the non-code assets shipped with the player: the Playbar woofer-array coefficients, factory infrared codes, the initial music-service catalog and web-interface files. The audio array supplies six-channel, 16-tap weights and delays for its configurations. The service seed contains TuneIn; the full catalog is fetched at runtime. Web assets include control descriptions, status scripts and product imagery. These files supply initial configuration and presentation data, while their presence alone does not prove which variant is selected during a particular session.
subsystems.sibling_daemons: The sibling-daemon interface: how this program relates to the player's other system processes like the network daemon and updater, covering what's delegated to whom. The multi-process split means this program hands off whole feature areas, and knowing the sibling set explains why some work happens elsewhere.
subsystems.ws_server: The local websocket endpoint: the player runs a websocket server so apps can hold a live control connection instead of polling. It does the standard handshake, negotiates compression, and then carries the same event traffic the cloud pipe does, making it the local twin of the remote channel.
subsystems.store_commit_faults: The save-to-disk layer for every replicated store (favorites, saved queues, alarms, timezones, accounts): it writes a temp file, flushes it, then renames it into place. That's the crash-safe write pattern that keeps your settings from corrupting on power loss.
subsystems.bin_upgrade: Separates firmware installation from rollout coordination. The upgrade executable reads update information, constructs the package request and performs an individual transaction, while upgrade_mgr coordinates attempts and exposes update status. A no-op mode skips download and reboot, and the surrounding scripts start and stop these processes. Recovered strings, symbols and related traces document substantial parts of the contract; they are not evidence that the executables have never been analyzed. Detailed verification and package behavior belongs to the technical findings rather than a blanket claim about partition fallback.
subsystems.bin_mdputil: Reads and writes the player's manufacturing-data partition. Its normal output includes hardware-manifest and identity values in KEY=value form, which boot scripts use for the player hostname. Other options write indexed fields, force a write past an existing-valid-data guard or select signing-key material where supported. The utility validates signed manufacturing pages and works through the manufacturing-data and flash libraries. Some field positions inside those pages remain unresolved; it is not a generic firmware-partition helper.
subsystems.bin_frcheck: Decides at startup whether the player should continue normally or perform a factory reset. It examines a persisted reset request and front-panel button state. The boot script interprets result 1 as normal startup, 0 as a full reset and 2 as a settings-only reset, and starts the corresponding reset indication and network reset path. This is a reset-decision tool rather than a checker that validates a newly installed root filesystem.
subsystems.bin_sddpd: Runs the Control4 Simple Device Discovery Protocol channel so compatible controllers can discover the player alongside SSDP and mDNS. It sends periodic advertisements, answers matching searches, supports an identify announcement and rejects unknown packet versions or requests. Multicast and unicast sockets operate per interface. Startup uses the shipped configuration unless a persistent development override is present. This is a third-party integration discovery channel, rather than Sonos's own replacement for initial household setup.
subsystems.bin_mdnsd: Runs the bundled Apple mDNSResponder-based daemon that serves local multicast DNS and DNS-SD clients. The player registers Sonos and Spotify services through its client interface; the daemon handles the network advertisement and discovery traffic. Startup can be held by the stopmdns flag, and the daemon attempts to drop privileges, reporting failure if it continues with elevated identity. The exact upstream release remains unresolved, so the recovered implementation family is more certain than a precise version.
subsystems.bin_netstartd: Owns network bring-up, SonosNet configuration, Wi-Fi station and DHCP supervision, household setup and network-related factory-reset work. It communicates with the player and the WAC agent over local IPC, and the over-the-air setup protocol uses DTLS. It can generate or distribute network key material and steer radio or connection changes. Message and state identifiers are recovered, while individual setup-message payload layouts still need investigation. This is an active network coordinator rather than just an early-boot bus.
subsystems.bin_wacd: Runs Apple Wireless Accessory Configuration provisioning. It constructs the temporary setup network identity and Apple device information from manufacturing data, starts the software access point and sends progress messages to the network-startup daemon. Those messages distinguish access-point open or close, station transition, completion, timeout, stop and error. A signal can simulate timeout for testing. Creating or advertising the setup network can fail, so starting the agent is distinct from successfully transferring and applying new Wi-Fi credentials.
subsystems.bin_wpa_supplicant: Authenticates Wi-Fi station connections using the bundled wpa_supplicant 2.10 with a Sonos-specific driver wrapper. Helper scripts generate configuration from stored credentials, launch it on the wireless interface and bridge, and can prompt a DHCP attempt afterward. Satellite configuration provides an additional home-theater network path. The recovered integration explains how settings reach the supplicant; some private-driver argument fields and event payloads remain unresolved, and authentication alone does not establish a usable IP connection.
subsystems.bin_athconfig: Provides command-line controls for the Atheros wireless interfaces, including channels, scans, antenna selection, network identity, key handling, allowlists and link statistics. Its radartool companion exposes DFS-related radar, channel-availability and non-occupancy controls. Network scripts and daemons invoke these utilities to configure or inspect the radio. The recovered command vocabulary documents those controls; the presence of a radar utility alone does not prove how every detected radar event is handled or that every command succeeds.
subsystems.bin_dropbearmulti: Bundles Dropbear 2020.81 for SSH service and key utilities. The startup script waits for the device-unlocked flag, then runs the server in the foreground with host-key generation enabled. The host key is stored in the persistent SSH directory, while authorized public keys use a separate debug path. Console login has its own gate and should not be confused with the SSH startup flag. This documents the launch and key arrangement without assuming a server is always reachable once the flag exists.
subsystems.bin_chronyd: Maintains the system clock using chronyd and its chronyc control client. The shipped configuration selects four Sonos NTP pool names, stores a persistent drift estimate and logs timing measurements; NTP serving is disabled. Startup waits for DNS before launching the daemon. The system clock then feeds household time and scheduling consumers, distinct from the audio-specific group-clock control. The build lacks NTS, and successful daemon startup does not mean it has already obtained a reliable time source.
subsystems.bin_net_utils: Documents the DHCP client, its event script and the bridge-control utility used during network bring-up. The DHCP client handles lease acquisition and renewal, SSID changes and ARP checks; its script reacts to bound, renew, deconfigure and rejection events to adjust interface state. Sonos-specific bridge controls configure the local network topology. These components turn a radio or wired link into an IP configuration, but a link being up or a DHCP request being sent does not prove that a usable lease was acquired.
subsystems.bin_keyval: Extracts a named value from KEY=value text supplied as input or in a file. Boot and configuration scripts use it to read manufacturing identity, wireless credentials and settings, with options that change delimiter handling. For example, the boot script extracts the serial value from manufacturing-tool output when forming the hostname. The utility reparses its input on each invocation; it does not itself maintain a persistent key-value store.
subsystems.bin_setmac: Assigns network-interface MAC addresses during boot using manufacturing identity and radio-address information. It can program Ethernet interfaces, both wireless interfaces and the bridge, and prints the resulting bridge address for scripts. The utility checks whether an address is already set and can refuse to overwrite it. This configures the interfaces' runtime addresses; it should not be described simply as writing a new factory MAC into persistent manufacturing data.
subsystems.bin_capsh: Provides the standard libcap capability shell, with options to inspect or adjust capabilities, identity-related state and execution environment. It is present in the image, but the recovered shipped scripts and binary references do not show an invocation. The player's launcher instead asks the player executable itself to change user and retain capabilities. This distinguishes a provisioned tool from a proven step in daemon startup.
subsystems.bin_pcap: A packet-capture utility, most likely used by the diagnostics tooling. How it gets invoked and where captures end up is undetermined.
subsystems.bin_sonosledmgrd: Runs the physical LED pattern engine and touch-feedback color handling. Patterns select LED identifiers and contain RGB color steps, hold and fade times, and repeat counts. The daemon applies modes for boot, setup, joining, playback, mute, warnings and faults, with a fallback to the default pattern. Hardware access uses the LED abstraction and ownership checks. Some message-kind-to-handler assignments remain unresolved, so this record does not yet establish every client command or state transition.
subsystems.bin_busybox_applets: Bundles BusyBox 1.35.0 with 133 compiled-in commands used by startup and maintenance scripts. They include init and shells, filesystem tools, network inspection and fetching, process controls, module loading, clock utilities and compression. The recovered applet table establishes which commands are available; it excludes BusyBox httpd, so the player's web server comes from a separate implementation. Availability does not mean every listed command is used during normal boot.
subsystems.kmod_sonos: Connects the player software to custom kernel interfaces for audio, hardware notifications, infrared and watchdog checks. The boot script loads the core Sonos device layer, watchdog, event queue and audio module, then the infrared module where present. The event queue sends hardware notifications through netlink, while other consumers use device nodes and control operations. These driver and consumer relationships are recovered; they should not be described as untouched simply because individual ioctl fields still need further decoding.
subsystems.kmod_ath_wifi: Documents the wireless-driver stack loaded during boot: Atheros framework and support modules, the hardware abstraction, optional DFS support, the Sonos wireless driver and the bridge module. User-space tools and the Sonos supplicant wrapper configure the interfaces, while the DFS path handles radar-related channel decisions. Many control operations are mapped to argument sizes and destination fields, but the semantic parameter names of numerous individual commands remain unresolved. The module inventory is therefore more complete than the per-command specification.
subsystems.fmt_upd: Describes the firmware package as a sequence of typed sections. Each section has a fixed header carrying its type and total length, followed by its payload. Recovered sections include the target version, required feature declarations, compatibility ranges, a preinstall script and separate system or device-data payloads. The updater checks supported features and compatibility before using the package. Parts of the encrypted section envelope still require interpretation, so the section layout is better understood than every cryptographic field.
subsystems.fmt_device_payload: Contains the model-specific manufacturing and calibration data supplied with an update. It has a prologue followed by tagged records, including a configuration-data identity, build date and time, and binary calibration regions. It is separate from the kernel and root filesystem, which occupy other update-package sections. The updater writes this device-data blob to its own flash region. Some calibration records remain unnamed, but the image is not an undecoded bundle of the operating system.
subsystems.sonos_custom_libs: Separates Sonos-built shared libraries from bundled third-party libraries. The custom set handles manufacturing identity, flash access, device hardware, event notifications, time arithmetic, cryptography, certificate validation, telemetry and satellite audio packets. These libraries place substantial functionality outside the main player executable, which explains why some paths delegate to another binary. Library roles and exported-symbol inventories are recovered, while the complete map from every export to its consumers remains unresolved.

primitives.http_extra_endpoints: Catalogs additional web paths found in the firmware, including SSH-key installation, firmware download, audio-processing controls, support-bundle submission and links to other local daemons. This helps distinguish the player's ordinary control API from maintenance and development surfaces. A path appearing as a string is a lead for investigation, not proof that the running player accepts a request at that address; registration and access checks must be established separately.
primitives.internal_result_namespace: Collects names the firmware uses for errors and other internal results, such as an invalid parameter, unsupported media format or unavailable music account. It also separates genuine error names from other symbols beginning with R_, including playback operations and LED modes. The list helps interpret logs and follow error translation, but a symbolic name alone does not establish its numeric value or the code returned by a particular network command.
primitives.system_property_keys: Lists named settings that the player reads or reacts to, including content filtering, radio location, crossfade duration, music-service bitrate and automatic-update policy. Some changes trigger work immediately: for example, a radio-location change reaches the radio configuration code, while audio-related settings reach playback configuration. The inventory distinguishes a real settings key from a similar-looking log label. Whether a specific command permits reading or writing a key still depends on that command's validation.
primitives.smapi_capability_vocabulary: Describes how a music service advertises the features and sign-in methods the Sonos player can use. Flags cover operations such as search, playlists, favorites, playback logging, content filtering and alarm restrictions; sign-in choices include anonymous access, username-based login and device or app linking. The optional document URLs provide translated strings, presentation instructions and a service manifest. Declaring a capability tells clients which interaction to offer; it is separate from successfully authenticating or completing that operation.
primitives.csrf_protection: The player puts a csrfToken value in its browser forms and checks that value when the form is submitted. This ties a settings-changing submission to a recently rendered form rather than accepting a blind request from another website. The device shares one current token: rendering a new form replaces it, so an older open form can become invalid. Submissions also fail when the token is missing, differs from the stored value or is about five minutes old. This check is separate from any permission required for the operation itself.
primitives.device_description_variants: Provides different XML descriptions according to the speaker's role. An ordinary player exposes the full device description; a bonded satellite exposes the satellite description, and a separate group-description endpoint describes the group coordinator. These documents tell a controller which identity, role and services it is looking at. The shipped description that omits AudioIn is another file a client can request; the player's role-selection routine does not automatically substitute it.
primitives.gena_internals: Maintains the classic subscription channel through which clients receive player state changes. Notifications use a LastChange XML document: playback updates can contain state, track number, track address, metadata and play mode, while queue updates identify the queue and its update version. Subscriber records distinguish a stable local subscription identity from the identity assigned by the remote publisher. Delivery workers handle individual subscribers and record failures or retries, so a notification being queued is a different stage from it reaching a listener.
primitives.didl_classes_ext: Labels catalog entries so a controller can distinguish a song from an audiobook chapter, podcast episode, playlist, radio broadcast or input source. The class is carried in the item's XML metadata alongside information such as its title and playable resource. This lets a browser present a container that can be opened differently from an item that can be played. The vocabulary also contains names without live emitters in this build, so a listed class is not proof that the player produces that kind of entry.
primitives.protocol_info_full: The player returns a list of advertised transport and media-format combinations, for example MP3 over HTTP or FLAC from a network file share. A controller can compare a proposed item's transport and content type with that declaration when deciding how to offer it for playback. The list includes ordinary media files and playlist or streaming-manifest types. It records what this firmware advertises; the exact file, codec parameters and playback conditions can still cause a later failure.
primitives.icy_metadata: Reads song-title updates embedded between the audio blocks of an internet-radio stream. The player asks the station to include metadata, uses the station's metadata-interval header to find those blocks, and extracts StreamTitle for the now-playing information. It also reads the station name and can follow redirects to another stream or playlist. Only StreamTitle is extracted from the inline metadata here; this is not a general parser for every field a station might include.
primitives.alert_engine: Arbitrates short sounds such as feedback chimes and voice alerts alongside other audio. A clip can be refused when the currently playing clip has a priority that prevents interruption. A separate ducking policy decides whether a request should temporarily reduce existing playback volume: it can always apply, always ignore, or depend on microphone presence or TV playback. These decisions explain why the same request to make an alert audible can be honored on one source or device and ignored on another.
primitives.household_psk_vocabulary: Names four families of shared household keys: household communication, control communication, local-network swapping and room-name encryption. Each has a corresponding backup-key identifier in the replicated settings. Rotation generates all four replacement keys and commits them together, rather than changing one family independently. Replicated XML carries the key identifiers, which name the selected keys; those identifiers are distinct from the secret key bytes used for encryption or authentication.
primitives.replication_elements: Describes the messages speakers exchange to keep shared household data consistent, including settings, accounts, alarms, network configuration and saved queues. Documents identify the device that last changed them and carry a version, sometimes with a schema version as well. A receiving player checks those markers and the supplied format before accepting a replacement; incompatible or corrupt data can be skipped or rejected. Local settings changes generate notifications that initiate further replication work.
primitives.token_refresh_state_machine: Coordinates refreshing a music account's authentication token when an operation needs a usable credential. Refresh work is tied to the account transaction: callers can request a refresh, wait for another refresh to complete and continue or report an error according to the resulting state. The account serial number keeps those steps associated with the correct saved login. The recovered transition vocabulary describes that coordination, rather than proving there is one independent background thread that renews every account token on a fixed universal schedule.
primitives.xml_schema_clusters: Collects the document structures used by status pages and saved configuration files, including alarms, household settings, cloud feature settings, calibration and playback diagnostics. These structures show what information the player persists or exposes for support, rather than describing a single command. For example, cloud feature configuration can come from an override, a cached cloud copy or a persisted copy, while household settings include their file and schema versions. Named elements whose detailed behavior remains untraced should be read as documented vocabulary, not a complete implementation contract.
primitives.internal_error_families: Translates playback and feature failures into names a diagnostic report or log can display. Examples distinguish a music-service account problem, an expired subscription, a streaming limit, an unavailable resource, a codec problem and a network connection failure. Several numeric ranges use separate lookup tables or generated names, including a SonosAPI error range. These internal result names are a separate layer from the numeric fault a particular control command returns to its caller.
primitives.http_status_endpoints: Inventories the built-in support pages used to inspect the speaker's current state. They cover subjects such as active zones, music services, queues, wireless settings, temperatures, certificates, decoder activity and performance counters. The route records identify which module supplies a page and the access flags applied to it. Some pages simply show diagnostics, while neighboring maintenance paths can change settings or trigger work; the presence of a path should not be treated as permission to perform every associated operation.
primitives.http_chunked_strictness: Handles HTTP bodies delivered as a succession of length-prefixed chunks instead of one body with a known total length. The HTTP layer requires chunked to be the final transfer encoding, validates hexadecimal chunk lengths and recognizes the final chunk and its trailers. It avoids installing a duplicate chunk decoder and rejects chunked uploads over HTTP 1.0. When no length, chunk framing or explicit close rule is supplied, the connection closing can serve as the end of the body.
primitives.http_range: Allows an HTTP request to name a byte interval within a resource, such as bytes starting at a saved position in a remote audio file. A request can specify both ends of the interval or leave the end open, and Content-Range describes which bytes were returned and the resource's total size. The recovered response template uses the partial-content status 206. Byte-range access supplies only part of a file; whether it implements a useful seek depends on the media format and playback path.
primitives.device_description_template: Builds the speaker's discovery XML by filling a shipped template with this player's identity and configuration. Values include the room name, model, software and hardware versions, serial number, network addresses, supported protocol versions and secure listener ports. A controller uses that document to identify the device and locate its advertised services and service-description files. The template therefore describes a particular player instance, rather than returning one identical static document for every speaker.
primitives.proprietary_headers: Lists Sonos-specific HTTP headers that carry context alongside a normal request or response. Examples identify the household, device, playback session, software generation or correlation identifier used to relate operations and logs. Other headers describe replicated content or provide authentication material. Their meanings and requirements belong to the particular protocol using them; finding a header in the firmware does not make it mandatory on every HTTP request.
primitives.websocket_impl: Keeps a network connection open so clients and players can exchange messages without making a new HTTP request for each one. Connections begin with an HTTP upgrade handshake, then carry message, continuation, ping, pong and close frames. The implementation rejects unsupported frame opcodes and records failures while writing frames. Its diagnostic history exposes connection endpoints, registrations and close details, which helps distinguish a failed handshake from a later disconnect.
primitives.soap_fault_wire_format: The fault wire format: the exact document shape of a returned error, which is what a failure looks like on the network.
primitives.soap_fault_code_vocabulary: The fault-code vocabulary: the full set of numeric error codes the command layer can emit, in their own terms.
primitives.soap_param_redaction: Parameter redaction: which argument values get scrubbed before logging, which is the privacy machinery keeping credentials out of the logs.
primitives.soap_client: The classic command-protocol client: the machinery for outbound classic-API calls, used when the player itself calls another device's commands like group fan-out to members.
primitives.gena_eventing: Sends state updates to clients that subscribe to an individual UPnP service. The subscriber supplies a callback address and receives a subscription identifier that must be renewed before expiration; updates arrive as XML property notifications. The player validates callback addresses, tracks sequence numbers, retries failed deliveries and records connection, handshake, write and timeout statistics. Secure notification connections are also supported. A subscription existing in the registry does not mean every queued notification has already reached the client.
primitives.upnp_eventing_impl: Implements the outgoing notification work for the classic UPnP event channel. It prepares state changes for subscribed clients, tracks delivery and lets some callers wait for notification work to finish. A configurable notification-deduplication option can coalesce repeated changes while delivery is already in progress, reducing redundant traffic rather than introducing a new event format. The record keeps the delivery counters and buffer handling separate from the individual service's list of reported state fields.
primitives.upnp_client_stack: Lets the speaker subscribe to state changes published by another device and keep that subscription alive. It tracks both the remote subscription identifier and a local logical identifier that can survive resubscription. Reboot markers and event sequence numbers help recognize a restarted publisher or an out-of-order update; renewal failures can lead to cancelling and recreating a subscription. The corresponding cloud resource mirrors these subscription operations using the logical identifier.
primitives.upnp_genaclient: Provides the client half of the classic UPnP event protocol: the speaker can ask another device to send state notifications to it, renew that arrangement and cancel it when it is no longer needed. This is used when a player must follow another device's changing state instead of repeatedly asking for it. The implementation is shared with the outbound subscription and renewal stack, where subscription identifiers, expiry and sequence handling are documented.
primitives.upnp_cloud_tunnel: Exposes classic UPnP subscription management through the cloud-facing player API. A remote client can request subscription, renewal or cancellation against a player service using a logical subscription identifier. The player translates that operation into its local subscription machinery, allowing subscription state to be managed through the cloud resource. This record describes that management path; the actual notification payload and the subscribed service's state remain separate contracts.
primitives.subscription_manager: The subscription manager: it owns the registry of active event subscribers, covering who subscribed, renewals, and expiry cleanup, so a lapsed client stops receiving traffic.
primitives.ssdp_discovery: Finds speakers through local-network discovery searches and announcements. A searching controller sends M-SEARCH, and a responding player supplies its identity and the URL of its device description; alive and byebye announcements indicate presence or departure. Sonos adds household and boot information and can attach signatures to those messages. The topology layer also considers discovery through multicast DNS, so a departure reported by one mechanism is interpreted in the context of the device's recorded discovery origin.
primitives.ssdp_signed_msearch: Adds an authentication signature to a local discovery search when a key has been supplied to the search handler. The signature is carried in the discovery message so the receiving side can check it against the request data and detect a mismatch. If the handler has no key or the key length is zero, it falls back to an unsigned search. Key provisioning is separate from constructing the search, so the presence of signing code does not imply that every discovery request is signed.
primitives.mdns: Provides the player-side components for publishing local discovery advertisements and receiving announcements from other devices. Nearby clients use those advertisements to find Sonos or Spotify services and their ports without manually entering an IP address. Device-service code supplies the advertised attributes, discovery code tracks peers, and listeners pass changes to the rest of the player. Detailed TXT fields, update behavior and service-port selection are documented in the associated device and controller records.
primitives.dns_sd: Connects the player to the local multicast-DNS service-discovery daemon. The player asks this library to register its service name, port and TXT attributes or to watch for matching services on the network. The daemon handles sending and receiving the discovery traffic while the player handles the resulting callbacks. This keeps discovery advertisement transport separate from the player's decisions about which services and attributes to publish.
primitives.discovery_layer: Combines two ways of finding speakers: UPnP discovery announcements and searches, and multicast-DNS service advertisements. It also registers Spotify Connect discovery and refreshes local advertisements when information such as certificates changes. When a mechanism reports that a peer has disappeared, topology checks which discovery mechanism owns that peer's registration before acting. This prevents an unrelated channel's departure report from removing a device that remains registered through the other channel.
primitives.target_udn_routing: Target-UDN routing: how requests addressed to a specific device ID get routed, which is the mechanism directing commands to the right unit.
primitives.svcmanifest: The service manifest: the build's service inventory, which is the list behind what the device description advertises.
primitives.svc_array: The service array: the registry of service objects embedded in the program, which is the table behind which services exist.
primitives.mega_impl_object: The mega implementation object: the large composite structure at the heart of the player, assembled from dozens of sub-interfaces. Most services reach into this single structure for their real work.
primitives.composite_subobject_interfaces: How the big implementation objects are assembled: a single service object is built from many sub-objects each providing one interface, and this maps which sub-objects exist and what each contributes.
primitives.deviceproperties_impl_vtable: The DeviceProperties wiring: how each of that service's commands reaches the internal settings object, via the same table structure other services use. It's the link between the documented commands and the real settings store.
primitives.audioin_impl: The line-in implementation object: the internal machinery behind the AudioIn service, which on this build is the stub that rejects every command. It's why the AudioIn commands accept a call and return an error, because the object exists but the feature behind it doesn't.
primitives.device_auth: Supplies credentials that identify the speaker when it contacts another device or a service. A device certificate is checked against trusted roots and Sonos-specific identity fields, while account-related requests can obtain or refresh an authentication token. Requests may carry the device certificate, device identifier, API key and a correlation identifier in headers. Certificate and token changes notify other components so they can use the updated identity. The exact token-refresh interval and revocation-event contents remain unresolved in this record.
primitives.device_account_endpoint: Exposes the player's device-account provisioning information as an encoded response. The response differs depending on whether a registration certificate exists in the local certificate store: the registered form has four fields and the fallback form has three. The encoder also decides whether the response is plain text or JSON. Registration state and transfer mode therefore affect the information this endpoint supplies; it is not simply a fixed page containing a user's account name.
primitives.device_registration: Establishes and maintains the player's registered-device identity for secure communication with Sonos services. The process exchanges registration messages, installs or refreshes a registration certificate, manages a signing key and publishes registration-state changes. Some work waits for required fields or retries after errors. Secure registration also controls access to configuration retrieval and can remove settings restrictions once registration succeeds. The local registration status and transfer controls expose progress through this process.
primitives.cloud_registration: Coordinates registration records that connect a player, household and user account in the cloud API. The available operations initialize, complete, refresh, transfer or remove a device registration and report its current status. Secure exchanges can use the registered-device client certificate, and certificate or registration-state changes notify the local player. This record describes those enrollment and maintenance operations; individual cloud features still have their own credential and permission requirements.
primitives.cert_identity: Provides the certificate identities the speaker can present when establishing a secure connection. The firmware distinguishes a general Sonos identity, a device identity, a legacy-compatible device identity and a registered-device identity, so different connections can require different credentials. Validation checks the certificate chain and Sonos-specific fields against trusted root bundles. The player can download updated root bundles and expose certificate information on diagnostic pages, helping distinguish an untrusted peer from an unavailable local certificate.
primitives.auth_capability: Collects capability checks that influence which endpoints and authenticated operations the player can use. Some named capabilities describe the product or group, such as microphone support, stereo pairing and speaker detection; their changes can cause endpoint selection to change. Other checks concern authentication policy, including mutual authentication and whether an authentication token is required for a support operation. These are different uses of capability information, so a hardware feature flag should not be read as a user permission or an API key.
primitives.smapi_auth_policies: Describes the sign-in method declared by each music-service descriptor and the extra context that service asks the player to supply. Anonymous services need no user login; other services can use a session-based user login, device linking or app linking. Capability flags can require a device certificate, player identifiers, authorization headers or account and playback reporting. A client uses this descriptor to choose the appropriate sign-in interaction and request fields; a successful login remains a separate result from the descriptor advertising a method.
primitives.service_accounts: Stores and identifies the music-service accounts the player uses for browsing and playback. An account has both a service identifier, which selects the provider, and an account serial number, which distinguishes saved accounts for that provider. The account machinery selects preferred accounts, manages direct-control sessions and updates associated user information. It also contains a migration path from older credentials to OAuth and downloads per-account manifests; either operation can fail without making all accounts interchangeable.
primitives.muse_authhelper: Checks credentials and authorization policy for modern API clients, using cached authorization information where available. The recovered token vocabulary includes signed JWT credentials associated with a household or unit and a playback-control scope. Operations also carry policy keys that the Thor authorization component maps to roles and evaluates. The detailed rules for every operation are still being traced, so the presence of a valid token alone should not be taken as proof that a client may perform any operation.
primitives.noncehandler: Creates a random, context-bound nonce and includes it with credentials and a key type in an encoded signing package for cloud requests. On receipt, the nonce handler checks the record's validity flags before asking a separate policy object whether it should be accepted. The nonce lets authentication distinguish individual exchanges rather than relying on the credentials alone. The exact expiry duration and whether a value can be accepted more than once remain unresolved; the available trace does not justify promising one-time use.
primitives.audio_pipeline: Connects the stages that turn an audio source into speaker output: source input, stream buffering, mixing, digital signal processing and the sound device. TV sound, external voice and chirp sources have separate input and output paths through the processing chain. Control events start or pause streaming, while sample-rate conversion adjusts incoming samples to the output clock. The main device, rate controller and music path labelled Hi-Res share the same filter coefficients; changing input timing can reset conversion history without selecting a different quality tier.
primitives.audio_subsystem_files: Maps source modules embedded in the firmware to the audio work they perform. The inventory separates home-theater configuration and channel processing, local and DSP playback streams, mixing and the sound device, amplifier management, and diagnostic taps. It helps a researcher choose the code family to inspect for a TV-audio, output or capture problem. These are recovered source-file names, rather than a list of tuning blobs that the player loads from disk.
primitives.audio_clip: Loads and schedules a short audio asset separately from the ordinary music item a room is playing. The player fetches the asset, reports asynchronous progress or completion and identifies the clip so a later request can cancel it. Missing clip identifiers and media-fetch failures have separate errors. In this recovered path the clip is inserted through the streaming pipeline; it is not proof that the player mixes it over uninterrupted music. Some playback situations require the current queue to pause for the clip.
primitives.autoplay: Starts a configured source in a chosen room when an autoplay trigger occurs. The settings select the target room, whether linked rooms should join, and whether to use a specified autoplay volume instead of the room's current volume. The player resolves a local line-in source or a stream from another room, sets the group coordinator's playback source and requests playback. A missing target, a user override or a failure to resolve the coordinator can prevent the action. Alarm-triggered autoplay also has a buzzer fallback when its intended source cannot be loaded.
primitives.extaudiosrc: Feeds externally supplied audio jobs into named mixer streams, including external voice, external chirp, setup chirp and setup discovery sound. Each playback job receives an identifier used to track or stop it, and a higher-priority source can preempt a job already playing. The source interface writes samples to the stream and reports transport or write failures, including unsupported sample frequencies. The recovered chirp source uses this interface to inject its pairing tones into the player's audio path.
primitives.chsnk_processor: Identifies the receiving side of the player's internal group-audio path. When a player consumes audio supplied through a Sonos channel stream, this component feeds the received samples into the local playback-processing path. That separates receiving a group stream from fetching an original music-service resource. This entry locates the receiver code; the packet layout and individual timing behaviors are documented in the more specific channel-source and channel-sink records.
primitives.ht_chsnk_processing: Processes incoming audio channels for a home-theater playback path before they enter the local or DSP output streams. It has channel-processing reset operations and a buffered stream processor that can skip forward in its input buffer. Those controls matter when the processing path must discard old buffered audio or restart with new channel state. This record identifies the home-theater processing components; it does not by itself describe every packet field or model-specific speaker-channel assignment.
primitives.bt_sbc: Provides encoding and decoding for SBC, the compressed audio format used in Bluetooth audio. The packet layer checks the number of SBC frames and whether encoder or configuration results match the expected sizes. Bluetooth connection and exclusive-mode state also influence the available status indicators. Finding these shared libraries and code paths in the firmware shows that the software contains Bluetooth-audio components; it does not establish that this particular hardware exposes a usable Bluetooth input.
primitives.hdmi: Exposes controls for reading HDMI cable or input status, obtaining EDID-related status and requesting a power cycle. The player delegates cable detection and hardware operations to an external hardware-abstraction library and driver rather than constructing the low-level transactions in its own code. The HDMI log records this player-side activity. The exact driver command numbers and control-message contents remain outside the recovered player implementation, so this record cannot specify those wire transactions.
primitives.sounddev: Resamples incoming audio so it fits the speaker's output clock, normally at 44,100 samples per second. The main audio device, TV rate controller and music path labelled Hi-Res all use the same 16-tap filter table. A change in input rate can reset the saved sample history or recalculate the timing ratio; it does not select a different quality setting. The TV controller accepts decoded audio at 32,000, 44,100 or 48,000 samples per second, while its digital-input line clock has a wider accepted range. Creating the developer file system/src_disable bypasses conversion in the main SoundDevice path; the separate TV and music converters keep their own behavior.
primitives.hls_radio: Plays an audio stream supplied as an HLS playlist and a sequence of downloadable segments. Live sessions follow a changing playlist, while static sessions use a fixed segment list; variant entries describe available bitrates and codecs. Diagnostic views expose the selected playlist, target segment duration, bitrate and encryption information, as well as the variant list. This helps distinguish an unavailable segment or playlist from a decoder problem, but the remaining parser and session behavior is still being traced.
primitives.smartplay: Responds to a hardware-button trigger by asking a cloud content service what the player should load and play. The request includes the button trigger, whether the current transport or queue is empty, and whether the device is a bonded or home-theater satellite. Returned content is loaded into the group queue before playback is started. A disabled feature setting, missing required context, or failure to fetch, parse or load the result stops the flow. This path asks for content rather than choosing a recommendation from a local music list.
primitives.queue_engine: The queue engine: the machinery owning the play queue, covering ordering, editing, and sequencing tracks through playback. It's the structure underneath every queue command.
primitives.queue_engine_object: The queue engine object: the internal structure the queue commands reach, which is the manager holding the queues and their state.
primitives.cloudqueue: Plays from a server-managed queue while keeping a working window of items near the current playback position on the speaker. Window requests identify the current item, position in milliseconds and queue revision; refreshes reconcile server changes with that local window. The player separately fetches queue versions and context and handles actions such as skipping or rating an item. Errors can trigger retries or a reset, and the server can report skip limits. The available trace does not establish that the entire queue is downloaded or that it can always be restored from an account.
primitives.play_state_mgr: Keeps a combined record of currently active audio sources, including TV sound, music-channel input, feedback sounds, setup chirps and chimes. It counts playback sources separately from informational sounds and announces each change so other parts of the player can react. It also writes a four-byte activity mask to /tmp/current_play_state. After a detected crash, the previous mask can be preserved as /tmp/crashed_play_state, letting a crash report classify the earlier activity as idle, TV, music-channel input, home-theater input or informational sound. The file contains no song address, queue or playback position, so it cannot resume a listening session.
primitives.trackplaymonitor: Records how long the current track has been played and emits a CurrentTrackPlayed event for playback tracking. This supplies information about listening duration, rather than merely identifying which track was loaded. The record identifies related Spotify playback-tracking and track-acknowledgment vocabulary, but the remaining producer and consumer details still need tracing. It should not be treated as evidence that this component detects every stall or abnormal track ending.
primitives.content_managers: Organizes collections the player exposes or maintains, including favorites, live and saved queues, playback history, radio-station history and network music shares. Different managers own each collection's stored entries, update identifiers and browsing objects. Favorites can be replicated between household members, while queue and share items are represented with the metadata and resource addresses needed for browsing or playback. Collection-specific validation still applies, such as queue-size limits and rejecting an invalid share.
primitives.cd_object_resolver: Looks up the content object named by a browse or edit request, whether it is the root, an album, a share, a queue, a saved queue or a favorite. ObjectID 0 selects the root; prefixes such as A:, S:, Q:, SQ: and FV: choose the corresponding family of objects, whose suffix is parsed by that family's resolver. The common entry point trims whitespace and rejects carriage returns or line feeds. If it cannot find an object, it returns no match and the calling operation decides how to report that failure.
primitives.media_player_mgr: Creates, registers and shuts down the player's media-player objects. Each instance has a target key, an assigned network port and its own logging configuration, so playback can be associated with the right instance rather than one undifferentiated global player. Construction rejects an invalid target key and can fail to create the instance's logging directory. The shared software also contains headphone-player identifiers, but those names alone do not prove that this hardware has a usable headphone output.
primitives.topology: Maintains the player's map of zones and their stored configuration. The map is backed by zones.json and supplies the group-state XML used by the classic API as well as the zones exposed by the modern API. It lets a controller relate a device to its room and group instead of treating every network address as an unrelated speaker. The zone manager and its storage are distinct from the separate discovery mechanisms that announce devices on the network.
primitives.topology_engine: Maintains and checks the household's current player and group relationships. It validates that groups have usable player and coordinator identifiers, probes members to detect unresponsive devices and can remove stale members. Bonded and home-theater changes can start monitoring or trigger recovery work, including regrouping an orphaned secondary speaker and retrying satellite reconnection while topology settles. Group-state snapshots provide the current member list to other operations; a proposed relationship is not automatically a consistent, settled topology.
primitives.group_coordination: Changes which speaker coordinates a playback group and which speakers belong to it. Becoming or changing the coordinator installs the group synchronization clock, and source takeover can use local audio transmission or a saved virtual-line-in state. Moving members and delegating coordination are separate transitions with their own checks. Some handoffs reset receiving buffers or omit restoring source state, particularly in bonded setups, so changing the coordinator is more involved than replacing a leader identifier in a list.
primitives.group_modes: Separates two internal ways of representing a speaker group. A player-only group carries player relationships used for transport and volume coordination; a location-and-player group also carries the associated location and settings information. This distinction determines which context the group object provides to surrounding code. The record describes the two implementations, not a guarantee that an app exposes a switch between these modes.
primitives.bonded_zones: Maintains permanent room-level relationships such as a stereo pair, a speaker bonded to a subwoofer, or a home-theater primary with satellites. The player records each member's role, checks that members agree on the bonded map and handles missing members or channel-swap changes. Bonded satellites have their own saved configuration and DSP files. These relationships carry configuration and role information beyond temporary playback grouping; the exact purpose of every satellite DSP blob remains unresolved.
primitives.ht_bonded_zones: Attaches, removes and reconnects satellites in a home-theater room. The primary records the satellite and its channel map, commits home-theater state changes and checks that the participating speakers agree on their bond. Notifications cover satellite configuration and channel-swap changes, while missing members can trigger reconnection or consistency checks. Separation normally goes through the primary but can fall back to local removal when that fails. The associated DSP-file names are known, although those names do not establish every file's processing role.
primitives.avt_session_lock: The transport session's lock: the mechanism that serializes access to session state so concurrent commands can't corrupt it mid-operation. It's the concurrency guard on the thing being played.
primitives.persistent_stores: Inventories files the player uses to retain configuration and selected playback or support state. Examples include local settings, household settings, room and zone data, cached cloud configuration, service manifests, authorization policy files and upgrade reports. Live track-queue backups are separate from saved playlists and favorites, so a queue backup and a named playlist should not be treated as the same object. The inventory identifies where these kinds of data are stored; individual writers and readers determine which changes survive a restart.
primitives.device_state_store: The device-state store: where the player's own runtime state persists, which is what it remembers across restarts.
primitives.alarm_store_object: The alarm store itself: the internal object holding the household's alarms in memory, created at startup and persisted by the writer. Together with the writer it's the persistence pair, since the object holds alarms in memory while the writer puts them on disk.
primitives.alarm_persist_writer: Writes stored alarm configuration into alarmclock.xml under the player's settings directory when alarms are created, updated or destroyed. The saved document includes the alarm collection and its schema/version information as well as clock-format and time-source settings. Mutation operations call the persistence wrapper before issuing their change notification. This connects an in-memory alarm edit to its saved representation, while the wrapper's result determines whether the write step succeeded.
primitives.sp_store_object: The system-properties store object: the internal object behind the settings-store commands, which is where the key/value configuration actually sits.
primitives.sqlite_timers: Stores active and paused timers in a SQLite database named timer.db. Active records contain an identifier, trigger time, total duration and whether they have triggered; paused records retain the remaining seconds, pause time in UTC and total duration. Keeping those values in a database separates saved timer state from an in-memory countdown. The storage schema describes what can be reloaded, while the caller determines what happens when a particular timer fires.
primitives.toml_config: Reads structured configuration from TOML files, including conf/anacapa_logger.toml for logging configuration. The parser provides separate accessors for text, integer, Boolean and array values within named tables, so configuration is interpreted according to value type rather than as one opaque string. This record identifies the parser and the known logging file. It does not establish that every player setting can be changed through TOML.
primitives.xml_parser: Parses the XML documents exchanged or stored by the player, including control messages, track metadata, group state and settings documents. Wrapper code creates a parser context and installs callbacks that receive the document's elements and text; malformed XML or unsuitable parameters can fail before the caller gets usable data. The bundled Expat parser also includes accounting and debug instrumentation for entity expansion and related parser behavior. Each consuming protocol still validates its own required fields after parsing.
primitives.sonos_concurrency: Supplies the synchronization tools shared by the player's background workers: threads to run work, mutexes and read/write locks to protect shared state, and condition variables to wait for a change or a new job. These tools are used by modules that update the same playback, settings or network objects from different execution paths. The record identifies the implementation families; the lock ordering and shutdown behavior of a particular feature must be read from that feature's callers.
primitives.sonos_libs: Identifies reusable Sonos library components linked into the control program. They provide thread synchronization, pooled strings, outbound HTTP, modern-API request context and event handling, nonce tracking, and watchdog support. Several higher-level features call the same implementation rather than carrying their own copy of each helper. The inventory describes the components present in this firmware, not a public API or a promise that every exported routine is used on this model.
primitives.thread_inventory: Maps named background-work registrations to the tasks they handle, including ARP reachability checks, address changes, hardware messages, infrared input, local-daemon messages, discovery traffic and track-play monitoring. The select-loop registrations provide callbacks for readiness, exceptions, resets and timeouts; those callback names should not be counted as four separate operating-system threads. Modern API command queues also have named asynchronous workers. This inventory helps locate where work is scheduled, while the owning module defines what each callback actually does.
primitives.watchdog: Tracks watchdog creation, shutdown and trigger activity associated with the player's progress monitoring. Diagnostic pages expose watchdog state and timestamps, while saved watchdog logs and kernel messages provide evidence after a trigger. Event-loop shutdown can cancel its watchdog, and configuration can trigger watchdog behavior. The recovered record identifies these controls and diagnostic outputs; it does not establish that every software hang necessarily causes a full-device reboot.
primitives.healthcheck: Maintains a deadline for a diagnostic check, initially one day ahead. Scheduling an update can move the deadline to half an hour before the update check, and a group-membership change can request a check in 45 seconds. In this firmware, the background thread wakes every five minutes and logs when the deadline has passed or been changed; its timer routine does not run a diagnostic test or upload anything. A separate compiled routine can fetch a small XML file from a diagnostics server and read whether submissions are allowed, but the timer does not call that routine.
primitives.diagnostics: Collects information about the player's state for support and troubleshooting, with a separate progress component for following diagnostic work. Related records describe the support collection manifest, status-page output and saved logs. Together they let a support investigation inspect conditions such as network configuration, playback activity and recent errors rather than relying only on the app's visible symptoms. The exact contents of a particular submission depend on the selected collection tasks.
primitives.diagnostic_manifest: Lists the material and collection operations used by the support-aggregation path. Examples include network interface and bridge information, mounted filesystems, process and network status, wireless scan results, player logs, saved alarm and household settings, and watchdog logs. The record also identifies referenced maintenance tasks such as report upload and crash-dump handling; those references should not be treated as proof that every support submission runs every task. The manifest provides the concrete packing list to consult when asking what diagnostic information may be collected.
primitives.devmode: Handles an engineering unlock code submitted through the developer-mode form. The firmware verifies a signed statement, saves the accepted state in devmode.bin through a temporary-file rename and publishes developer-mode status changes for other components to observe. Gated features consult that state rather than becoming available merely because their code was compiled into the firmware. The verifying-key file and the complete signed-statement fields remain unresolved, so this record does not supply an unlock procedure or establish every privilege a code can grant.
primitives.testenv_logger: Provides separate web forms for changing backend environment selection and runtime logging. The test-environment form selects among production and development environments, can override the online-update base URL and exposes bases for cloud, catalog, system, transfer, metrics and update services. The logger form selects an output destination such as a file, UDP or standard error, together with a category and verbosity level. These are live configuration changes that can affect where requests go or what gets logged, rather than pages that only display diagnostic information.
primitives.runtime_policy: Runtime policy: the rules governing what the running system may do, which are the policy checks applied to operations and settings at execution time.
primitives.system_overrides: Maintains overrides for service URLs and selected runtime options used by the player. Examples redirect cloud configuration, music-service catalogs, registration, history, diagnostics, crash submission or voice-service endpoints, while other options control reporting intervals or submission behavior. Setting or clearing an override changes the value that the relevant component resolves for that purpose. An override is specific to its consumer; it does not move every connection to one new server or bypass all authentication.
primitives.startup: Describes how the control program is initialized before it handles normal player work. Startup selects configuration from the firmware or writable configuration locations, accepts a requested user and capability set, and initializes shared components such as HTTP clients, settings overrides, TLS configuration, recovery networking and audio mixing. The constructor inventory also identifies components registered automatically by the compiled program. A component appearing in that inventory shows initialization code is present; its feature-specific checks still determine whether it becomes usable.
primitives.idle_events: Identifies the listener module for internal idle-related events. An idle notification gives other code a way to react to a change in activity without continuously polling the player. The available record locates that listener but does not establish every condition that produces an idle event or every job it triggers. In particular, its name alone should not be read as proof that all idle notifications mean music stopped or that the device immediately enters a low-power state.
primitives.wake_on_lan: Attempts to wake missing secondary speakers that belong to a bonded or home-theater primary. It sends a wake magic packet addressed to the missing speaker's hardware address and schedules asynchronous wake work or a later retry. The resulting diagnostics count missing players and packets sent, allowing a researcher to distinguish an attempted wake from a speaker being present again. Sending the packet is not confirmation that the remote player has resumed or successfully rejoined the room.
primitives.internal_event_bus: Passes messages between components inside the player when conditions such as playback, group membership, the local IP address, certificates or settings change. Components register observers for the event kinds they need, and delivery can use immediate, scheduled or cached-event observer paths. The event layer also measures observer handling time and reports slow callbacks. This is internal coordination rather than a client network subscription. The payload fields and complete consumer list for every event type remain separate reverse-engineering work.
primitives.hwmessagelib: Receives structured messages from the hardware-side daemons and makes them available to the control program. Subscriptions are grouped by hardware domain, including buttons, LEDs, temperature, sensors, battery, switches, audio and home theater. The connection exposes a readable file descriptor so the player can process messages when they arrive rather than repeatedly polling each hardware component. Individual message definitions determine the fields and possible state changes for each domain.
primitives.hw_input_events: Names the physical input events and the actions that can follow them. Inputs include play/pause, volume and join-button presses, held or repeated gestures, connection changes and device-orientation changes. The corresponding action vocabulary includes advancing tracks, joining or leaving a household, opening a setup access point and preparing or performing a device swap. These are distinct stages: detecting a button or gesture identifies the input, while policy and state determine which action the player performs.
primitives.ir_remote: Converts the timing of infrared pulses into a remote-control code and supports learning selected remote-button codes. The decoder distinguishes pulse-width, pulse-distance and biphase patterns and handles repeat-style transmissions; malformed or excessively long captures can be ignored. The learning path collects captures and compares button codes with the remote database before updating configured status. Recognizing a transmission and finding a usable button mapping are separate steps, so the decoder's presence does not guarantee support for every remote.
primitives.component_map: Maps embedded source-path names to the major parts of the control program, including playback, discovery, settings replication, event delivery, device properties and alarm handling. These names help a researcher identify which implementation family to inspect for a particular behavior and distinguish Sonos code from linked third-party components. They are paths from the firmware's build and logging metadata, not proof that the corresponding source files exist on the device or are publicly available.
primitives.linked_libraries: Inventories external libraries the program links for media decoding, cryptography, discovery, hardware access, messaging, compression and local data storage. Examples include MP3, DTS, Bluetooth SBC and FFmpeg media components; mbedTLS certificate and cryptographic libraries; multicast-DNS discovery; SQLite; and zlib compression. Sonos-specific libraries supply certificate validation, flash and device-data access, timekeeping and hardware-message handling. A linked library makes its code available to the program, but the active consumers and product capabilities determine which operations are used.
primitives.circuitbreaker: This protects the speaker from repeatedly contacting a failing cloud service. Six failures within two minutes pause new attempts for 30 seconds. The next check then permits retries, and a successful response clears the failure history. The retry threshold counts failed results, not requests in flight. A received HTTP error response can still count as a successful connection, because the callers check whether a response arrived rather than whether it was a 2xx response. Its telemetry label successful retries actually counts openings of the retry state; it does not count successful retry responses.
primitives.cloud_request: Locates the player-side module for requests sent to cloud services. This helps distinguish outbound work initiated by the speaker from a control request that an app sends to the speaker. Registration, configuration retrieval and report submission have their concrete endpoints and behavior documented in the corresponding feature records. This entry identifies the shared cloud-request code family; it does not establish a universal request body, retry interval or authentication rule for all those operations.
primitives.muse_common: The modern-API common layer: shared machinery all modern-API operations use beneath their route logic, covering the common request handling every verb relies on.
primitives.pinewood_remote: Provides API operations shaped like remote-control buttons, including mute toggling, volume steps, playback toggling, navigation directions, back, home, settings and power. A remote caller addresses the player and the desired operation rather than supplying an infrared pulse sequence. The route vocabulary also includes loading a resource. The recovered names establish the remote-control surface, but they do not identify a particular commercial handset or prove the exact hardware effect of every operation.
primitives.migrationmanager: Converts older saved data when the player moves to a newer representation or account model. The recovered paths include music-account changes to SMAPI or OAuth, service-identifier migration, legacy music-service address rewriting and migration of saved zones during setup. Account work can be deferred until a cloud connection is available and can fail during authentication. Migration is therefore a feature-specific conversion process, not an unconditional rewrite of every stored file on each update.
primitives.usage_data_sharing: Controls whether the speaker records player-activity events and sends them through its ordinary reporting channels. Playback reports can include the station identifier, audio format, whether playback succeeded, error details and timing information. Before the speaker successfully reads the UMTracking setting, ordinary event reporters can save records in their buffers, but their upload routines require permission before sending them. The exact value NoReport refuses sharing; any other successfully read value permits it. Some reporting channels have separate exceptions, so this setting does not stop every diagnostic report.
primitives.telemetry_pipeline: Collects and packages reports about player configuration, playback, account actions and operational failures. Concrete report families include playback seconds and offsets, radio failures, time-synchronization failures, TLS-cache statistics, vanished players and crash dumps. Uploaders serialize event fields and can identify a submission as product-data telemetry, while rate limits and missing uploaders can prevent delivery. Consent rules are applied by individual reporting paths as described under reporting_policy; this inventory does not mean every listed report is sent on every player or after every action.
primitives.reporting_policy: Decides which event records each reporting channel can collect and send. Ordinary channels stop recording new events when usage sharing is explicitly refused, and they wait for permission before uploading a collected batch. Two configured channels bypass that consent check. Some device-diagnostic reports still go out after refusal, but omit selected information such as the line-in name, boot sequence or status-light setting. The periodic usage-statistics sender clears its pending counters before checking consent, so a refused batch can be discarded instead of saved for later. These are the speaker's local rules; they do not describe what the receiving server stores.
primitives.spotify_esdk: Contains the Spotify embedded client used by the player's Spotify integration. Separate components handle login and the authenticated access-point connection, track playback, media output and the Sonos player binding. Its media-download code receives CDN addresses, fetches audio in chunks, can switch to another CDN and records download size, timing and bandwidth. These are different stages from a controller discovering the Spotify endpoint or transferring a listening session. Some Sonos glue and message-header details remain unresolved in the technical record.
primitives.location_engine: Retrieves and applies settings associated with the player's current location. When the location changes, the cloud connection changes or a settings group is invalidated, the update manager queues work to fetch or merge that group's settings. Generation counters help reject stale data, and settings for an unfamiliar group can be discarded. Diagnostics expose pending and running tasks, completion status, retries and the next retry time, letting a reader distinguish a location change from its settings actually being applied.
primitives.zone_experiments: Holds experiment assignments that can change the behavior enabled for a zone. Each diagnostic entry identifies an experiment by name and identifier and shows its current value and default value. Cloud feature configuration and a system override can supply the assignments, so two players with the same software need not have identical experiment values. The inventory describes those assignments and their reporting surface; the code consuming each experiment determines its actual effect.
primitives.wss_event_vocabulary: Lists the named updates a client can subscribe to over the secure WebSocket event channel. Topics include playback and track metadata, group changes, volume, alarms, wireless state, certificate or registration state, settings versions and diagnostic results. The receiver translates wire identifiers into a topic before selecting the corresponding processing path. This registry establishes which topic names and identifiers exist; the fields inside each event and every handler's behavior still require the individual producer and consumer records.
primitives.native_protocols: Catalogs the private message formats and transport families embedded in the player, including WebSocket event records, local-daemon messages, settings replication, group-audio streams, acoustic pairing and Spotify protocol components. Formats differ: some use tagged records with type and length fields, some carry audio frames, and others exchange structured settings or commands. A decoder must identify the relevant protocol before applying its field layout or integrity check. The inventory is a map to those specific records, not one universal header shared by every Sonos connection.
primitives.wifi_hal: Provides a common interface through which the player queries and controls the wireless driver. Operations report association and link statistics, connected-network information, roaming events, channel frequencies, watchdog data and whether wireless operation is enabled. Other operations configure idle scanning, update boot-sequence information or force a group-key refresh. Functions are resolved from the driver library, so the player-side API is separate from the chipset-specific implementation and the diagnostic files exposed by that driver.
primitives.wifi_sonosnet: Manages wireless settings and coordinated SonosNet channel changes, with the network-start daemon applying the requested configuration. The state includes the wireless mode, frequency, enable status and wired-network condition. Before a change that could disconnect the controller, the player records recovery information; if controller confirmation does not arrive, it can re-enable wireless operation or revert the change. Channel-change messages coordinate a later channel hop with other players. These recovery and coordination steps are separate from saving an SSID and password.
primitives.assoctracker: Measures how a phone or other controller discovers the speaker and starts communicating with it. For each controller IP address, it records discovery searches and reply failures, whether the local network resolved the controller's hardware address, requests for the speaker's description and zone state, and subsequent group notifications. It keeps at most four records. A record becomes eligible for expiration after 30 seconds from its first discovery request and is cleared on the next sweep. A qualifying record becomes a CrAssoc connection-health report containing the observed times, attempt counts and errors. Later activity does not extend the window, and expiration clears the record even if the reporting channel does not accept it.
primitives.arping: Checks a local-network IP address by scheduling address-resolution probes. A caller supplies the probe timing and arms the ARP manager; its worker performs the network work rather than making the caller run the probe synchronously. The manager retains probe results and pending-reset state, which the requesting monitor can read on a later cycle. That monitor then decides whether to retry or reset its connection. The remaining probe-result and caller-policy details stay open in the technical record.
primitives.netsettings_mgr: Owns the saved network configuration and pushes changes to the network-start daemon for application. Its operations include incrementing the configuration version and rotating network keys, with diagnostic JSON or text views of the current settings. Applying a new configuration is a separate step from storing it. Failed updates can enter automatic-revert handling, and failure of that recovery is reported explicitly, so a successful settings write alone does not prove the new network connection is working.
primitives.mdp_flash: Reads manufacturing data pages from flash storage, including the player's serial identity and calibration information. Sonos and flash libraries expose the original and second-page forms, serial-number conversion, page version information and write operations. This data is separate from ordinary room names and user preferences stored in the settings directory. The record identifies the factory-data access layer; individual field layouts and write permissions belong to the relevant page and accessor implementations.
primitives.mod_zp: Provides the application-level zone-player module and its background worker pools. The module includes player and service-account components and a related album-art module. Shutdown is ordered: it stops HTTP and player work, modern-API and event workers, resets zone-related state, and releases timed-job and thread-pool resources. This ordering helps explain why stopping the program requires more than dropping one playback object. The module inventory does not itself define a new client command.
primitives.rmd_op_worker_class: The RMD worker class: a worker-object family in the remote-diagnostics machinery, where operations run as discrete work items.
primitives.timedjobs: Schedules in-memory jobs to run at an absolute next-fire time, such as a reporting task or a network-disable test. A job must belong to a registered endpoint, and a job marked scheduled must have a usable time set. Jobs can be added, moved to a later time, cancelled or removed after outstanding work finishes. Separate manager channels serve different classes of work, including alarm-clock and button-related tasks. The job registry itself has no persistent storage, so it should not be confused with the database of saved timer records.
primitives.timers: Identifies the zone-player implementation for timer-related work. Timer storage retains active or paused countdown records, while the timed-job manager separately schedules callbacks at their next-fire times. Those neighboring records supply the concrete saved fields and job-lifecycle rules.
