The source-module name in this entry alone does not specify every timer interval, clock choice or action triggered by expiration.
primitives.dropout_logging: Records audio-dropout events and produces diagnostic material that can be collected after playback cuts out. The dropout-triggered XML surface and dump collection task let support inspect the state captured around an event, rather than only seeing a later report that music stopped. The firmware also has a test path for injecting a dropout error. The record identifies this logging and collection path; it does not establish that every interruption has the same cause or is repaired automatically.
primitives.tls_stack: Establishes encrypted connections using the bundled TLS and certificate libraries. Connection configuration chooses trust roots, client certificates, authentication requirements, cipher options and protocol negotiation, while network callbacks perform the handshake and subsequent encrypted reads or writes. Session tickets and saved sessions can let a later connection resume earlier TLS state instead of starting every handshake from scratch. Certificate validation and each connection's selected profile still determine which peer identities are accepted.
primitives.entitlements: Fetches and caches entitlement information for a household or user and notifies other components when that information changes. Stale data can schedule a refresh, and runtime policy consults the cached result when deciding whether a feature is available. One recovered example uses the Sonos Business entitlement to suppress automatic Sonos Radio preinstallation. Entitlements are therefore inputs to feature-specific decisions; a cached document does not mean that every named feature is usable without its other requirements.
primitives.audiotap: Copies audio from selected processing locations into diagnostic captures, for example the DSP output or the TV's digital input. The tap manager normally allows two simultaneous locations, rejects duplicate names and refuses locations whose source does not permit capture; its three physical slots allow a configured maximum of three. A separate SPDIF recorder keeps up to 25 MB of recent input. Taking its snapshot removes captured bytes from the rolling buffer and writes a zlib-compressed file. Exporting wraps that file in base64 text inside an XML element and then deletes it, so the same saved snapshot cannot be exported repeatedly.
primitives.location: Tracks a household-related location identifier and the versioned settings associated with that location. A new identifier can notify topology, player and music-account components, while the update manager retrieves or merges settings groups. The record also contains playback logs that use location to mean a resume time or byte offset; those are a different use of the word. The resume paths report falling back to the last known point or disabling pause-at-end behavior when no point can be determined.
primitives.albumart_proxy: Lets a controller request cover art from the speaker's /getaa endpoint using a source image URL. Medium, small or virtual-line-in image selectors choose different fetch paths; selector parameters must come before u because the handler stops reading parameters when it reaches the source URL. The emitted v parameter acts as a client cache-buster and is not parsed by this handler. Artwork requests run asynchronously, and an upstream fetch failure can become a 404 response. Cached images can be reused, but this does not guarantee that all artwork remains available without an upstream connection.
primitives.muse_route_verbs: The modern-API route verbs: the operation-name vocabulary bound to routes, covering every verb the API can invoke.
primitives.accepted_mimes: Maps recognized HTTP content types to the parser or decoder the player should try. Entries cover formats such as MP3, WAV, AIFF, FLAC, Ogg, WMA and AAC, as well as playlist and segmented-stream manifest types. A playlist type first needs playlist processing rather than being treated directly as audio samples. The table establishes format recognition and backend selection; codec parameters, file validity and the selected playback path can still cause an item with a recognized content type to fail.
primitives.aha_ops: Names five operations used by the audio-hardware and home-theater session lifecycle: stop, restore, and end, suspend or pause a virtual-line-in session. Virtual line-in represents an audio source carried into the player's coordinated playback path. These commands connect session state changes with starting or pausing audio streaming and, where appropriate, joining a group or becoming standalone. The AHA names in this record describe those audio operations rather than identifying a separate music-service partner.
primitives.auto_update_policy: Checks whether the household can perform an automatic software update for each participating player. The recovered checks include software-generation compatibility, battery charge, household-size limits, whether the update manifest contains the exact model and submodel, and whether that model or its installed version requires a manual update. The manifest supplies the offered version and download address for a player. Scheduling an update window is therefore only one condition; these compatibility and eligibility checks can still prevent automatic updating.
primitives.avt_session: Maintains the identity and lifecycle of a playback session, including whether it has been preserved, destroyed, evicted or is waiting to resume. Commands that name a session can fail when no session exists or the identifier does not match. Unexpected playback stops can lead to a restart attempt, but an explicit halt, a fatal error, no prior playback or repeated failures can prevent restarting. Chimes, alarms and sleep timers interact with this state, including preserving playback for later restoration when the relevant path permits it.
primitives.boot_reasons: Provides readable labels for device lifecycle and reconfiguration reason codes. The known labels include a new IP address, household change, remote request, satellite-role change, sleep, upgrade, low battery, a switch between wireless modes and a new SSID. Those reasons help explain which transition the player is reporting, rather than forcing a reader to interpret a numeric code. The label list is not a complete reconstruction of every cold start, crash or watchdog event and should not be treated as one.
primitives.browse_categories: Names the collections a content browser can encounter, such as music shares, artists, albums, genres, composers, radio stations, favorites, live queues and saved queues. Display names and object identifiers have different roles: a readable label tells an app what to show, while an identifier such as a queue or favorite prefix tells the player which collection to resolve. The available categories span local libraries, inputs and service content. Their names do not imply that every category contains entries on every player.
primitives.channel_source_types: Classifies where an audio channel stream originates and how it reaches the player. The recovered values distinguish compressed or uncompressed line-in and dock sources, virtual line-in, a coordinator's local library or music service, local inputs and a group member. Channel diagnostics print the source name alongside its numeric value and use it when reporting listening or synchronization activity. These are source classifications; left, right and subwoofer assignments are described by separate speaker-channel maps.
primitives.chirp_sdk: Provides the audio-data encoding components used to send setup or identification information as tones. The SDK has routines for sending a payload and processing audio samples, together with validation for profiles, channels, modulation, gain and mute state. Its compiled decoder routines also contain errors for malformed or unrecognized symbols, but their presence does not prove the player actively uses every receive function. Several packed configuration fields still lack proven names, so their byte values should not be presented as a complete acoustic protocol specification.
primitives.config_parsers: Identifies the configuration-file reader established in this record: the TOML parser used for conf/anacapa_logger.toml. It reads typed values from tables and arrays so logging configuration can contain text, numbers and Boolean options. Other player documents, such as XML settings or JSON cloud configuration, have separate parser and schema records. This entry is not a complete file-to-parser map for every configuration file in the firmware.
primitives.ddthrd: Processes local discovery messages on the device-discovery worker. The recovered inventory identifies searches, player or controller presence announcements and departure messages, with per-message work completion and lost-message counters. Unsupported message types can be discarded. This connects incoming discovery traffic to queued device-discovery work rather than treating every announcement as an immediate topology change.
primitives.dev_unlock: Implements the device-unlock challenge form used by manufacturing or development flows. The page reads manufacturing data from flash and displays the serial identity, fuse-related value and challenge before accepting a response code. Attempt limits can reject further requests, while a successful flow records unlocked state and reports that a reboot is being initiated. Locked and unlocked states also select different web-content directories. The helper that validates and applies the response remains separate from simply displaying the challenge.
primitives.diag_instructions: Contains a compiled routine for retrieving a small diagnostics-permission XML document from the server, optionally including the household identifier in the request. It accepts a known body length below 1,024 bytes and reads text inside ServerDiagInstructions and SubmitPermission. Text beginning with yes sets the stored permission flag; other parsed text clears it, while fetch or parse failure leaves the old value intact. This recovered routine reads a permission value rather than interpreting a general language of diagnostic commands, and the healthcheck timer in this build does not call it.
primitives.diagnostics_submit: Coordinates a support submission that can collect material from multiple household players. It first requests a diagnostic identifier from the server and distributes that identifier to participating devices or a controller, then gathers the selected support documents. Each document can have a hash sidecar and compressed payload, and the manifest identifies the player, software and registration or quarantine state. Artifacts are submitted before the final manifest, and confirmation identifiers are checked against the expected submission. A request already pending or a failed or mismatched acknowledgment can prevent successful completion.
primitives.didl_escaping: Escapes characters in track-metadata values before inserting them into XML. For example, an ampersand in a title becomes & so it is read as title text instead of the start of an entity. Apostrophes, double quotes and angle brackets have corresponding replacements as well. The builder applies this to values while constructing element names separately. Its metadata output buffer is limited to roughly four kilobytes, and truncation is logged, so exceptionally long metadata may not be returned in full.
primitives.dsp_drc: Loads home-theater sound-processing options and presets used to control dynamic range and related effects. Named presets include movie, night and disable; a missing configuration can fall back to the default, and invalid dynamic-range settings can be rejected. The configuration also contains processing modes, speaker-angle and upmix options, filters and a named crossover-frequency vocabulary. These are inputs to the DSP configuration path, while the exact processing effect and supported values depend on the selected preset and product.
primitives.ducking_engine: Temporarily reduces playback level when an accepted duck request needs another sound to be audible, then clears the request through unduck or expiry handling. Requests carry per-zone flags and can be forwarded to the coordinator, secondary players or a bonded peer. Policies can ignore requests globally, on microphone-equipped devices or while TV audio is playing, depending on the selected mode. Local timeout and remote-flag expiry keep abandoned requests from remaining active indefinitely. Ducking controls playback level; the separate clip scheduler determines how a particular sound is inserted.
primitives.enum_tables: Maps named internal choices to their actual numeric values or bit flags. The recovered tables cover subjects such as play modes, authorization roles, account tiers, source classes, update results, timer states, orientation and network modes. For example, a role name and a play-mode name each belong to their own table rather than one shared numbering system. These mappings help interpret stored or binary fields; a network API that sends names or uses a different representation still needs its own field specification.
primitives.ext_audio_source: Schedules auxiliary audio jobs such as voice responses, voice alarms, guidance, alerts, setup chirps and discovery tones. Each job has a type, identity and play state, and the engine writes it into a compatible voice, chirp or setup mixer stream. Stop and completion handling operate on those jobs, with status events and explicit errors for incompatible streams, unsupported sample rates or failed writes. This record describes the auxiliary job engine rather than assuming every physical line-in source is routed through it.
primitives.group_capabilities: Represents the features a playback group reports through a named capability mask. Known names include Widevine content protection, Atmos, voice, portable behavior, TV input and HLS version support. Capability changes can influence endpoint selection or spatial-audio handling, and the strict name-conversion path rejects bits that have no registered name. The flags describe available group behavior; they do not imply that grouping creates a hardware feature that none of its members supports.
primitives.healthcheck_job: Runs the background deadline-observation loop for healthcheck scheduling. The loop waits five minutes at a time, checks whether the stored deadline has passed, logs a timer pop and acknowledges requested schedule changes; shutdown uses a separate stop-and-acknowledge exchange. It does not invoke the compiled diagnostics-permission HTTP routine or perform the previously claimed liveness test in this build. The related healthcheck record documents the initial one-day deadline, earlier scheduling requests and the exact acceptance conditions.
primitives.http_request_security: HTTP request security: the checks applied to incoming web requests, covering validation and restrictions protecting the web surface.
primitives.httpcache_manager: Maintains shared cache information for HTTP content used by the player and saves cache metadata in httpcaches.json. Local and remote content hashes let it compare cache state between zones and decide when to invalidate a local copy or request invalidation elsewhere. A force-clear path removes cached state, while a missing cache is reported rather than silently treated as an existing entry. This record establishes cache comparison and invalidation; it does not establish every entry's freshness deadline or eviction policy.
primitives.ibt_engine: The IBT engine: an internal data-movement component identified by build-tree naming, recovered structurally.
primitives.idle_shutdown_reasons: Labels the reason supplied when player activity or a stream transitions toward idle, suspension or shutdown. Names include an API call, a Bluetooth connection, a missing partner, recovery, user suspend and several shutdown classes. The caller chooses the reason: for example, the recovered stream-end path uses UserShutdown and a seek-related teardown uses CriticalShutdown. Those names therefore describe software transition categories and should not automatically be interpreted as the physical cause of a reboot.
primitives.inprocess_events: Delivers typed events between components within the control program. A component subscribes an observer to an event type; the dispatcher assigns an event identifier and sends it to the registered receivers, then records completion. Subscribing or unsubscribing can be deferred while dispatch is active, and invalid types or unauthorized senders can be rejected. Known types cover transport transitions, generic updates, home-theater configuration, calibration mode, feedback, entitlements and deferred settings changes. This mechanism coordinates internal work rather than sending every event to an app.
primitives.lechmere_cmds: The lechmere command vocabulary: the command set of the websocket and eventing layer, meaning what messages the modern event channel carries.
primitives.location_settings_sync: Queues updates to settings groups when the player changes location, reconnects to the cloud or invalidates previously fetched settings. It can discard work during a location transition, skip a duplicate pending request or upgrade a narrower request into fetching all settings. Version and generation checks keep unfamiliar or stale updates from being applied as current configuration. The record also describes a checksummed migration-file container, which is distinct from the live task queue used to retrieve location settings.
primitives.mdns_stack: Publishes and receives local discovery advertisements containing player identity, household and address information, secure ports and API paths. Changed TXT attributes are updated individually, while identical values are skipped. A minor address-refresh path rebuilds the advertisement and increments its 16-bit sequence counter, even when the notified address is unchanged; initial address acquisition and the full-rebind path do not increment it. Receivers log and store that counter without requiring it to increase before notifying topology. Household and required-field checks still determine whether an advertisement can be treated as a usable peer.
primitives.misc_components: Collects smaller implementation families that would otherwise be easy to miss in the component inventory. Concrete examples include HTTP cache invalidation using local and remote hashes, boot-sequence updates associated with wireless changes, the discovery worker processing search and presence messages, and storage-health checks that can mark a device as broken. The entries point to those specific tasks and their diagnostics. Their names alone should not be used to infer additional commands, enabled product features or a complete failure-recovery policy.
primitives.misc_health: Collects the healthcheck deadline observer and related long-press behavior found in the player. The long-press handler can restore a configured volume level and cycle through recently active group coordinators. For a selected coordinator it attempts to obtain playback state, join that group or fall back to local playback when the other paths fail. These are concrete button and playback behaviors, rather than an additional catalogue of periodic hardware self-tests. The healthcheck worker itself only waits and logs in the recovered build.
primitives.misc_mgrs: Collects additional managers with specific background responsibilities. The wireless-idle manager requests driver idle-scan changes and retries failed updates. The automatic-update scheduler maintains an allowed time window, performs update checks, tracks pending hours and attempts, and can block updating because an alarm is approaching or a device is active. Its saved report records timing, versions, player counts and failure details. Each manager has its own trigger and state; these names do not imply one shared maintenance loop.
primitives.muse_grouping_ops: Changes a playback group using a group identifier, arrays of players to add or remove and an optional hint about the future coordinator. The operation computes the effective member set and carries out the necessary join, leave, coordinator or playback-state work. Some paths copy a music context while creating a group, and failed intermediate operations can be retried. Authorization, invalid arguments and inconsistent topology can prevent completion, so submitting the desired member list is different from obtaining the requested final group.
primitives.muse_network_test: Runs connectivity tests identified by a networkTestId so a caller can request the result later. The recovered connection probe has a five-second deadline and reports whether it established a TCP connection; that result is not proof that the server returned valid application content. A separate test waits a requested delay, disables wireless networking for a requested duration and then attempts to enable it again. An existing test, invalid identifier or failed disable/re-enable step can produce a separate failure.
primitives.muse_upnp_bridge_actions: The bridge operations: modern-API verbs that reach through to the classic command layer, which is how the JSON surface drives the old services like stereo pairing and satellites.
primitives.netif_events: Polls network-interface status while interested listeners are subscribed and emits updates containing a health description and wireless signal strength. Signal strength is reported as a signed dBm value, and the interface is identified by its hardware address. A subscription starts the polling work; unsubscribing or letting its lease expire can stop it. This explains why these status updates are tied to active interest rather than an always-running history of every interface change.
primitives.netstart_ipc: Receives local messages from netstartd, the daemon that applies network setup. Message identifiers distinguish events such as setting or clearing an SSID, enabling or timing out setup modes, connecting or disconnecting Wi-Fi, changing household identity and establishing a recovery access point. The player translates those messages into its own state changes or events for other components. Shutdown can cause a network-bounce notification to be ignored. The per-message payload fields still belong to the individual message-handler records.
primitives.nodetx_transport: Transmits blocks of audio between players and handles recovery when a receiver reports missing packets. A negative acknowledgment identifies a packet range to resend; incompatible protocol versions and packets that have become too stale can be ignored. Resynchronization operations reset the transmission position, while packet timing and crossfade state help follow changes in the audio stream. Its counters distinguish retransmitted data, missing-data requests and resynchronization work. This is an audio transport, not merely a channel for household health reports.
primitives.ota_update: Identifies the user-initiated update scheduler reached by checking for software updates or beginning a household update. It coordinates work requested explicitly by a user or controller, separately from the automatic-update scheduler and its eligibility rules. The actual download, package checks, installation and update-daemon interaction are described in the upgrade records. A scheduled update request is therefore a starting point in the process rather than proof that new firmware is installed.
primitives.ota_upgrade: Coordinates firmware retrieval and household upgrade work with the external upgrade manager. Requests use a software-generation-specific firmware path and can be rate-limited; the household flow tracks participating players, progress, retries and per-device outcomes. An approaching alarm or a permission restriction can prevent or defer an update. Saved reports and upgrade logs retain versions, results and failures so completion can be checked after the process runs. Package verification and flash installation belong to the upgrade executable rather than being performed entirely inside this control program.
primitives.platform_details: Collects hardware and build information the player can read for identification or compatibility checks. A recovered device-control query reads bootloader information, checks a U-Boot version and exposes an OTP or fuse identity value for diagnostics. Other entries identify the platform architecture and a parser for key/value attributes. The remaining work is to connect every platform key with its actual consumer; a key being present in the platform data does not establish which feature it enables.
primitives.rate_limiter: Limits how often a named activity is permitted to proceed. Its configuration includes a maximum number of events per period, a suppression interval and a delay, with diagnostics showing those values for the particular limiter instance. Audio and networking code can use the helper to control repeated work without giving each caller its own scheduling implementation. This record identifies the configured limits and usage families; it does not establish one global limit applied to every client request.
primitives.rincon_didl_fields: Adds Sonos-specific information to the XML metadata describing a playable item. Fields include radio names and stream text, per-track gain, audiobook chapter number and total chapter count, rating-related connotation and input icons. An advertisement marker can cause a link URL to be supplied for that item. These extensions let a client display or interpret information beyond a title and artist, while the standard metadata class and resource still identify what the item is and how it is played.
primitives.rincon_uuid: Describes the RINCON_ identifiers used to name player devices consistently across discovery and control records. The recovered device-identity form combines the prefix, a twelve-digit hexadecimal hardware address and the suffix 01400, with uuid: added where a UPnP device identifier is required. That identifies the player independently of its current network address. Other long hexadecimal strings in diagnostics can be different identifiers, so they should not all be parsed as this device-ID format.
primitives.settings_xml: Stores named settings as XML entries containing a Name and Value, with another indexed form carrying update and version information. The file families include system settings, secure settings and mobile-device settings. Invalid system settings can lead to a factory-default fallback; the recovered embedded seed supplies a customer identifier and a TuneIn visibility setting. Additional keys are created and read by their callers, so the seed is not a complete fixed list of every setting the player can store.
primitives.smapi_jwt: Generates a signed JWT for a secure request using the fixed RS256 signing algorithm. The caller supplies the claim names and values, and the generator encodes a header, payload and signature into three dot-separated segments. Encoding or signing failures prevent a usable token from being returned. The routine also requires trusted time for generation; the request supplies its lifetime information rather than this record establishing one universal expiry duration. Token generation and the receiving service's acceptance rules are separate operations.
primitives.smapi_layer: Provides the music-service integration path alongside the player's other stream-source modes. Service descriptors and presentation maps describe how a provider is exposed, while account matching, authentication, metadata requests and stream bookkeeping connect the selected content to playback. Switching between SMAPI and virtual-line-in or Spotify Connect modes can require clearing state from the previous mode. Service-provided position information can override a seek, and expired radio entries or login failures have explicit handling paths.
primitives.smb_shares: Connects the player to network music folders shared through SMB. It builds a read-only mount request with the server, share, user and optional domain credentials, probes compatibility and records whether the mount succeeded. Changed credentials can require unmounting and reconnecting, while idle shares may be released when they are not busy. Mount limits, invalid mount identifiers and unsupported protocols produce distinct failures. The recovered legacy mount options do not establish that every NAS or SMB dialect is compatible.
primitives.sonarcal: Names audio resources used by the sonar-calibration path, including a leader sound, a test tone and a home-theater completion sound. Their special resource addresses let the player load those predefined sounds without an ordinary music-library item. The record also identifies a bound on the constructed address. This resource vocabulary alone does not establish the full measurement and equalization procedure or its chronological relationship to Trueplay.
primitives.speaker_group_advertise: Announces a playback group's identity and communication endpoint to other components. The advertisement supplies the group coordinator, group identifier and name, household identifier, WebSocket endpoint and supported API-version range, with boot and configuration counters. Presence and departure forms indicate whether that advertisement is being introduced or withdrawn, and publication can be delayed. A listener can use the resulting endpoint to contact the group while interpreting its identity and version compatibility.
primitives.ssh_authorized_keys: Provides a browser form for adding SSH authorization keys to the player's saved authorized-keys file. After validating the form token, the add path appends the submitted key text and a newline; the remove-keys operation deletes the entire authorization file. The related display uses the SSH tooling to show fingerprints, with a persisted ECDSA host key identifying the SSH server. The form changes saved SSH authorization material, rather than acting as a test that merely prints a key.
primitives.stream_error_counters: Counts different kinds of audio-pipeline trouble so diagnostics can distinguish where playback failed. Music, voice, chirp and TV streams separately record synchronization problems, missing data and read errors; home-theater counters also record inserted silence or concealment audio used for lost packets. Additional counters identify TV decoder formats, sample-rate conversion, input overflow and processing underflows. The counts narrow the failing stage, but a counter increment alone does not identify every underlying network or media cause.
primitives.telemetry_endpoints: Separates two report-upload formats used by the player. The /data/submit.aspx channel sends gzip-compressed XML using HTTP chunked transfer, while /binary sends a binary event body with a declared content length and the product-data-telemetry message type. Both use categorized on-device event storage before upload work drains the records. These are upload paths rather than fixed server hostnames, and the reporting-policy record explains which channels check consent or have exceptions.
primitives.timezone_table: Supplies standard-time and daylight-time rules used to interpret the player's local clock. Rules contain an offset from GMT and transition details such as the month and day of the week, so a time-zone setting determines more than a display label. The player can accept a versioned table from the timezone-update service, save it and parse it again; an invalid file can lead to loading the default table. Clock and alarm operations consult these rules when reporting or scheduling local time.
primitives.tsclient: Separates audio and timed metadata from an MPEG transport stream. It reads transport-packet headers, identifies the program and stream tables, then follows the configured audio and timed-ID3 packet identifiers while handling adaptation fields and continuity information. Unsupported stream types or malformed ID3 tags can be rejected. This lets a segmented stream carry both playable audio and synchronized metadata without treating every packet as an audio sample.
primitives.txst_enum: Records which transmit path currently owns an outgoing audio session. The named states distinguish a channel-source stream, line-in rebroadcast, a home-theater mesh and virtual line-in, along with no active transmission and an uninitialized state. Session operations such as starting, suspending or pausing streaming cause the corresponding changes. The value identifies the transmission source class; it is not the playback position or a direct label for a physical speaker channel.
primitives.uri_service_map: Chooses the playback implementation from the leading part of a resource address. Radio, HTTP audio, playlists, service-specific resources, docks and internal sounds have different prefixes that select different handling paths. The classifiers test those prefixes in a fixed order and use the first match; they do not dynamically choose the longest matching string. Once a family is selected, that family's parser and playback implementation determine whether the rest of the address is valid and usable.
primitives.vli_grouping: Maintains group membership and source state for virtual-line-in audio, including AirPlay, Bluetooth and TV-proxy endpoint families. It checks whether members and the coordinator support the relevant source type, can skip suspended rooms and can remove or reorganize incompatible members. If the local coordinator becomes standalone, the flow may delegate coordination to another member; absent a suitable coordinator, a player may become standalone itself. Source-state snapshots support handoffs, but the chosen source type and membership still determine which paths are allowed.
primitives.vli_playback_tracker: Records the lifetime and operating conditions of a virtual-line-in playback session. A session needs a clock; while it runs the tracker observes wireless channel changes, disconnections and accumulated errors. At the end it can upload a numbered report containing duration, sample frequency, framing type and the session's diagnostic data. A missing uploader prevents that submission, and a skip path excludes Spotify-sourced sessions. These reports describe a session's observed conditions rather than automatically correcting its playback.
primitives.vli_transport_detail: Coordinates virtual-line-in session changes through internal transport-action events. Actions include pausing, suspending or ending a session, joining a group based on source state, becoming standalone and updating the current virtual source. Source transmit settings also advertise the time-synchronization port used by receiving players. Companion events signal session end and processing completion, separating a requested transition from the work finishing. The remaining detailed transport fields stay open in the technical record.
primitives.wakelock_guard: Keeps an operation from allowing the player to sleep or become idle while that operation holds a wake or prevent-idle guard. The guard acquires the named operation and timeout when created and releases it when its scope ends. Changing the operation timeout is accepted only through the expected acquired guard; an unguarded modification returns an error. Operation identifiers and timeout values belong to the caller, so the observed numbers should not be assumed to be one fixed playback or update policy.
primitives.watchdog_crash: Registers named components that provide a health-check callback and polls those callbacks from the watchdog worker. A component reported unresponsive can produce a log with its name and UTC time and trigger the /sbin/reboot command, whose result is also logged. This watchdog checks registered clients rather than independently inspecting every process on the device. The player cancels it during normal event-loop shutdown, so shutdown and a watchdog-triggered recovery are different paths.
primitives.websocket_server: Accepts an HTTP upgrade request and turns an accepted connection into a persistent WebSocket channel. The handshake uses the client's key and version and selects the versioned lechmere application subprotocol; modern API traffic is carried within that channel. Once connected, the server handles message and continuation frames, ping/pong keepalive and close frames with reasons. Handshake refusal, a later failed write and a client closing its connection are separate stages recorded by the implementation.
primitives.wifi_idle_roles: Classifies wireless clients according to the work they are doing when the manager chooses idle-scan behavior. Roles include carrying audio out or in, participating in local SonosNet, having no peers or primary, upgrading and undergoing a home-theater swap. The manager combines those roles with primary-channel and retry information before requesting the driver's idle-scan setting. The names describe inputs to that decision; they should not all be interpreted as interchangeable low-power sleep states.
primitives.action_dispatch_records: How each service looks up your command: a sorted name table that gets binary-searched, each entry pairing a command name with the routine that runs it. The authoritative list behind which commands each service can execute.
primitives.service_impl_vtables: The service implementation tables: how the object-based services wire commands to the routines that run them, showing which services route through implementation objects and how.
primitives.dirobj_class_map: Identifies the object classes used to represent browsable content, including music shares, live and saved queues, saved-queue tracks, favorites and attribute or artwork objects. Different classes expose different lookup and prefix-search capabilities, so an object's identifier determines more than the text shown in a catalog. The recovered map also distinguishes an AudioInput object class from a separate report-server class that had previously been misidentified. The technical tables provide the method bindings behind those concrete object roles.
primitives.binary_section_map: Maps where code and data are stored inside the executable so recovered structures can be checked against the actual firmware. Read-only regions contain strings and tables; other regions contain relocated pointers, shared state and the startup-constructor list. The code-region map uses string references and call patterns to locate implementation families. Some regions have only been sampled rather than fully cross-checked, so the map is an aid to finding evidence, not a claim that every proposed component boundary is verified.
primitives.protobuf_descriptors: Describes the structure of 103 embedded nanopb message schemas, including numeric field tags, scalar types, strings, byte fields and nested messages. Repeated fields represent lists, while tagged-union fields select one alternative payload within a larger message. The recovered structure can guide encoding or decoding a binary record without guessing its field sizes. It does not by itself give every field a human meaning or identify every message's consumer; those semantic bindings remain unresolved.

uri_formats.x-rincon-queue: References a queue by the identity of its owning player, with an optional position fragment. A fragment of #0 refers to the queue itself; positive positions select tracks, so #5 identifies the fifth entry. The recovered prefix check is case-sensitive. The reference is an instruction to use queue content, not a URL containing the audio bytes, and its owner need not be inferred from the player receiving the command.
uri_formats.sonos_queue_track_uri: Identifies one entry in a player-owned queue using the owner identity and a numbered fragment. Positions start at one: #1 selects the first track, while #0 denotes the queue itself. Replies can use this form to name an entry precisely. It is a position reference rather than a permanent track identifier, so a changed queue can put different content at that position.
uri_formats.x-rincon-stream: References an audio stream by the source player's identity, with an optional stream-type selector. The proven spdif selector names the TV or optical-input stream. The recovered classifier accepts mixed-case spelling of the scheme. This form allows a player to use an inter-room source, rather than carrying a music-service URL itself; resolving the source still needs a reachable player and compatible transport.
uri_formats.x-rincon-mp3radio: Wraps a web address for the player's internet-radio path. The wrapped resource can lead through a playlist, including M3U or ASX variants, before the stream is opened. The recovered prefix checks are case-sensitive. Despite the scheme name, the address alone does not prove that the response is already a live MP3 stream; the fetched resource still has to be interpreted and opened.
uri_formats.x-rincon-playlist: References saved playlist content separately from the live queue. It carries an owner selector and can use the same position convention as queue references, with #0 denoting the start or playlist itself. The browse path decodes encoded identifiers, while the prefix check is case-sensitive. Loading this reference selects stored content; it does not mean the saved playlist contains the audio files or guarantees that each item can still play.
uri_formats.x-rincon-cpcontainer: Names a content-provider object using a provider namespace and object identifier, sometimes with a subordinate path. The recovered RDCPA and RDCPI forms distinguish container and item records, while an SCPB form carries two identifier components. Translation uses these identities to reach the corresponding browse or content object. The namespace is not proof that the object is hosted by an external music service: local-library classification is also represented.
uri_formats.x-rincon-buzzer: Selects a locally stored buzzer sound by numeric index. The player maps the index to an MP3 file in its buzzer directory, and emitted forms include sounds 0 and 1. An optional colon-plus-character suffix is accepted by the recovered parser, which does not distinguish the character's meaning at that point. Using a local sound avoids a network music fetch, but still depends on the selected asset and audio path being available.
uri_formats.x-rincon-sonarcal: Names tone assets used during acoustic calibration, including leader.ogg, testtone.ogg and complete_ht.ogg. Related configuration-mode references select calibration completion or speaker-detection behavior. These are tuning-session resources rather than music-catalog entries. Calibration code checks and can fetch tone assets, so the reference should not be described as proof that every tone is permanently built into the player.
uri_formats.x-rincon-configmode-sonar: Selects setup or tuning audio through two related address families. Configuration-mode names include calibration-tone, calibration-completion and speaker-detection actions; sonar-calibration names identify tone files such as the leader and test tone. The player can carry them through its normal audio transport during tuning. They are internal calibration resources, but their names do not establish how the assets were supplied or guarantee successful playback.
uri_formats.x-sonos-vli: Describes a virtual-line-in source with the member identity, channel index and a backing-source reference separated by a comma. Recognized backing types include Bluetooth, Spotify, a URI source and TV proxy. The member identity is checked so it cannot introduce an extra comma into that structure. Virtual line-in adapts these sources into the player's session and group-audio system; it does not mean the sound bypasses normal playback machinery.
uri_formats.x-sonos-misc: A catch-all of internal Sonos address schemes for odds and ends: home-theater audio streams, plain HTTP variants, MMS-era stream types, service locators. Individually rare, collectively the long tail of sources the player can address.
uri_formats.x-sonosapi-*: Groups service-reference addresses for streams, HLS, static HLS, radio, recently played and other service content. The variant identifies the resource path, while tokens and parameters can carry service identity, flags and account lookup information. These references normally require service resolution before opening concrete audio. Their presence does not by itself prove where the final stream is hosted, what its token means or whether playback will succeed.
uri_formats.x-sonosapi-radio: Names a radio-station reference with a station identifier, music-service identifier and flags. Its optional sn parameter is a service serial used to look up credentials, rather than a playback-session number. The service descriptor and account lookup connect the reference to the appropriate provider, and the fetch path can carry an API-key header. This family is not sufficient evidence that every referenced station belongs to the branded Sonos Radio service.
uri_formats.spotify_scheme: Names native Spotify content and related objects, including tracks, podcast episodes, advertisements, interruptions and images. Internal x-spotify and x-spotify-file forms distinguish network-stream and local-file resources used by the integration. The kind marker helps the Spotify path interpret the identifier. An image or interruption reference is therefore not necessarily a playable music track, and recognition does not establish account authorization or availability.
uri_formats.explore_scheme: Describes catalog collections such as albums, artists, artist releases, top tracks and playlists. Templates combine a collection kind with an identifier prefix such as alb., art., pp. or mp., allowing the content-provider translation path to build the corresponding browse reference. These are collection identities rather than direct audio locations. A browsable collection still needs expansion or item resolution before its contents can play.
uri_formats.rdradio_scheme: Identifies service radio objects, including artist-based and station-based references. The recovered forms carry a kind and an identifier prefix such as Art. or ps., and sit alongside the service-serial lookup used to select account context. This is a service object reference rather than a direct audio-file URL. Its kind helps choose the radio path, but does not by itself prove that a station is saved or available to play.
uri_formats.hls_radio: Marks an HLS radio resource for the segmented-stream path. The player recognizes hls-radio:// when classifying streams and probing playlist formats, while sonos.com-hls-radio names the corresponding type in protocol-info strings. The reference therefore identifies how the resource should be opened and interpreted. A usable playlist, compatible audio and successful segment downloads are still needed for playback.
uri_formats.hls_aac: Marks the AAC variant of the HLS stream path. The hls-aac:// address form is recognized by the stream classifier, and sonos.com-hls-aac is the matching advertised service-type name. It selects a segmented-audio resource family rather than containing audio bytes itself. Recognition does not guarantee that the playlist or encoded segments are valid.
uri_formats.hm_scheme: Names services addressed through the embedded Spotify SDK's Hermes messaging path. Recovered examples include device state and playback operations under hwptp, event logging under hwp-events, and content-encryption or cache-key resources. A host and versioned path identify the service operation. This is protocol addressing within the Spotify integration, rather than a music URL or the local discovery advertisement that makes the speaker appear in the app.
uri_formats.pndrradioad: Marks the advertisement stream form used by the Pandora integration. It is distinct from Pandora's ordinary radio reference and HTTP stream form, and has a corresponding service type in the stream vocabulary. That distinction lets the player classify an ad resource separately from station content. The scheme record does not yet describe every insertion, skipping or playback-policy behavior for advertisements.
uri_formats.skd: Records an Apple StoreKit-style content-key reference with a host, product identifier, stream and epoch components. The specific sample literal in this record has no code references in the recovered binary, so it does not establish an active parser or request path. Related content-key metadata is documented separately. This preserves the meaning suggested by the reference format while distinguishing an unused example from proven runtime behavior.
uri_formats.stub_scheme: Creates a temporary transport reference for a player discovered through mDNS before full transport setup. The emitted form is stub://stub: followed by a discovered-instance index. It allows discovery to retain a placeholder player entry without inventing a working audio endpoint. It is not a marker proving that the real player is permanently unplayable.
uri_formats.misc_schemes: Collects additional address families found in the binary, including Pandora and HLS variants, Spotify Hermes resources, local files, older streaming transports and temporary discovered-player references. Related URNs identify metadata, authentication or service namespaces rather than audio locations. Each entry has its own role and reachability evidence; the collection is an inventory, not proof that every listed scheme is actively used or that all possible schemes have been recovered.
uri_formats.protocol_info_schemes: Lists the transport and content-type combinations exposed in source or sink capability strings. They include ordinary HTTP or network-file resources, common audio formats, playlists and adaptive-stream manifests, plus private queue, group and service-reference forms. A controller can use these strings to recognize a resource family, but some entries need further resolution before any audio is fetched. Advertisement of a format does not guarantee successful playback of every resource carrying that label.
uri_formats.sonos_albumart_path: Builds a large-artwork filename using a GUID-shaped identifier beneath a base path. Related artwork references use the player's getaa endpoint with the item URI, optional size flags and a revision value used in generated URLs. These forms allow metadata to point to an image resource or artwork proxy. A formatted GUID does not prove that the image exists, that the address never changes or that every item has unique artwork.
uri_formats.sonos_settings_rest: The settings paths the player calls on the household's configuration service, which is where effective settings and per-location settings live on the REST surface.
uri_formats.http-endpoints-muse: The outbound API paths the player itself calls. When the player acts as a client toward other players or the cloud, these are the route templates it formats its requests against.
uri_formats.cloud_api_routes: The full map of outbound cloud API calls the player can make: hundreds of route templates covering everything the player asks Sonos's cloud for, including accounts, services, updates, and telemetry. It's documented as the outbound counterpart of the API the player serves.
uri_formats.rinconnetworks_urn: Identifies Sonos metadata extensions within XML documents. The recovered namespace covers fields such as audiobook resume position, author and narrator, podcast information, album artist and display title, and is also declared in transport-event XML. The namespace tells a parser how to interpret those element names; it is not a playable resource address or evidence that every item supplies every extension.
uri_formats.oauth_jwt_urn: Names the JWT-bearer grant type used by the token-exchange client. It tells the receiving authorization service which credential-grant format is being submitted, while the separate bearer token names the HTTP authorization scheme. This is authentication vocabulary rather than a content location. The identifier itself does not establish a successful token exchange or the permissions granted by the returned token.
uri_formats.sonos-schemes: Bare 'sonos:' addresses used internally as templates and identifiers, a small family of Sonos-namespaced locators for housekeeping rather than playable content. They show up inside the system's own bookkeeping rather than in anything you'd browse to.
uri_formats.x_rincon_schemes: Groups private references for queues, saved playlists, inter-room streams, radio, provider objects, buzzer sounds and calibration resources. The individual forms have different components and parser rules: a queue names its owner and position, a stream can name a source type, and a buzzer selects a local sound. The shared prefix does not make them interchangeable, and recognition of a reference is separate from opening or playing its content.
uri_formats.x_sonos_schemes: The x-sonos* scheme family as a group: every Sonos-prefixed address type and the headers that travel with them, collected so the whole family's grammar lives in one place.
uri_formats.tqueue_scheme_registry: The complete zoo of playable address schemes harvested from the queue engine's routing table: every scheme the queue knows how to direct, in one inventory. It is the master list of what kinds of source addresses exist.
uri_formats.tqueue_probe_chain: Refines a resource's type after its address scheme has been recognized. It examines playlist extensions such as M3U, M3U8 and ASX and reads playlist contents to locate stream resources; content type and response handling can also steer the open path. Redirect limits and truncation warnings constrain this process. The probes interpret a fetched resource, rather than guaranteeing that an ambiguous address eventually resolves to playable audio.
uri_formats.pndrradio-http: Names the HTTP stream variant in the Pandora resource vocabulary. It is separate from the raw Pandora radio reference and the advertisement stream form, with matching service-type names used for classification. This distinction describes how the resource enters the streaming path. The marker alone does not establish that a response contains uninterrupted station audio or that the account can access it.
uri_formats.hls-radio: Identifies a radio resource handled through HLS playlists and segments. The scheme is recognized by stream classification and playlist-format probing, while a separate sonos.com-hls-radio label represents the transport in protocol-info data. It is a resource reference rather than the segmented audio itself, so playback still requires a usable playlist and successful segment reads.
uri_formats.hls-aac: Identifies the AAC variant of the HLS resource family. Stream classification recognizes this address form and associates it with a separate service-type label. It steers the resource toward segmented-audio handling; it does not prove that the playlist, audio format or account context is valid.
uri_formats.stub: Names a placeholder player entry created from mDNS discovery before a complete transport is available. The number in stub://stub: identifies the discovered instance. This preserves an identity during setup of the peer record rather than selecting a silent audio file or proving that the device can never play.
uri_formats.hm: Addresses the embedded Spotify SDK's Hermes service resources. The hwptp host carries device and playback-related requests, while hwp-events carries event logging. A versioned path selects the relevant resource, including device state, volume, queue or key-related operations. This describes the SDK's messaging destinations, rather than the mDNS announcement or an audio-download address.
uri_formats.sonos_com-hls-radio: Names a service type used in protocol-info and resource classification for HLS radio. It maps to the separate hls-radio:// address scheme. The label identifies a transport convention, rather than a URL host or the specific music provider serving the station. Confusing the type label with a playable address would skip the resource-resolution step.
uri_formats.pandora_com-pndrradioad: Names the Pandora advertisement service type used in resource classification. The corresponding resource address uses pndrradioad://, while ordinary Pandora radio and HTTP variants have their own labels. This is a type identifier rather than an address containing an ad's audio bytes, and it does not by itself specify insertion policy.
uri_formats.last_fm-radio-http: Records a Last.fm radio HTTP label found in the firmware's service-type vocabulary. It identifies a radio transport convention associated with that integration. The presence of the label does not establish a complete current login or playback path, nor explain whether the service is still available.
uri_formats.x-sonos-unknown: Marks a source whose type could not be identified during source resolution. The recovered form is the bare x-sonos-unknown: marker, without decoded parameter fields. It records uncertainty for later handling; it is not a playable resource and does not itself establish what fallback or error the caller chooses.
uri_formats.rhapsody_imageserver: Constructs an artwork URL for Rhapsody-sourced content by inserting an image identifier into a fixed image-server path ending in 300x300. It is separate from the service's audio protocol label and older provider-object migration references. The template establishes how an artwork address is built, without proving that the remote image still exists or that the integration is maintained for a particular compatibility reason.

payload_formats.didl_lite: Describes media items and collections in XML, including title, artist, album, artwork, class and resource information. Sonos extensions add context such as source identity and specialized metadata, while resource protocol-info identifies how an item should be opened. The class vocabulary covers music, broadcasts, podcasts, audiobooks, playlists and adapted audio inputs. This is a widely used media-description format, rather than proof that every now-playing path uses one document or that describing an item makes it playable.
payload_formats.didl_lite_header: Opens a DIDL-Lite media-description document and declares the namespaces used by its fields. They distinguish Dublin Core titles and related metadata, UPnP media properties, Sonos extensions and the default DIDL item or container structure. These declarations let a parser interpret identically spelled names in the right vocabulary. The header alone carries no track title, audio URL or playback result.
payload_formats.didl_res_protocolinfo: Labels a media resource with its transport and format convention. Recovered labels cover saved playlists, queues, radio, shows and local playlist files; some contain wildcards rather than a specific MIME type. The resource reference and its protocol-info work together to describe how the player should interpret it. A queue or service-reference label can require further resolution, so the field does not by itself establish a directly downloadable audio file.
payload_formats.didl_cdudn_desc: Adds the identity of the item's originating content-directory player to its metadata. The descriptor uses the cdudn identifier in the Sonos metadata namespace. This lets an item retain a link to the player that supplied its directory information. It identifies origin context rather than a playable resource or proof that the originating library is currently reachable.
payload_formats.soap_envelope: The request and response envelope: the wrapping document every command call and reply is built inside, consisting of header, body, and the per-command element naming the operation and its service.
payload_formats.soap_envelope_variants: The two envelope openings the command layer uses: one with an explicit encoding-style declaration and one without. Both wrap the same request and response bodies.
payload_formats.soap_fault_wire: The body of a fault reply: the exact document skeleton every error response is built as, carrying the code and description fields that tell a caller what failed.
payload_formats.soapaction_header: The command-name header: the HTTP header that says which operation a request wants (service type plus action name). It's the routing key telling the player which command to run.
payload_formats.gena_event_envelope: Sends changed state variables as an XML property set, with one property wrapper for each variable. Notification headers identify the event type, subscription and sequence, and Sonos extensions carry boot-sequence and variant information. These values let the receiver associate an update with its subscription and track ordering. Permission denial can reject eventing, so a correctly shaped message is not sufficient evidence that it will be accepted.
payload_formats.upnp_gena_event_doc: Wraps changed state in an XML property-set document for subscribers. A LastChange property can itself contain a bundled event document, whose recovered instance wrapper names instance zero. A reader therefore needs to distinguish the outer property set from the inner bundled update when extracting values. The literal templates establish the emitted structure, without promising that every notification contains a LastChange property.
payload_formats.lastchange_templates: Defines bundled state-change XML for three services: transport playback, rendering controls and the queue. Each uses its own event namespace, with the transport form also declaring Sonos metadata extensions. Variables are represented by named elements with value attributes, grouped beneath an instance where applicable. These are the three recovered LastChange producers, rather than a template used by every service; other services can report changes through ordinary event properties.
payload_formats.sonos_lastchange_attr_form: Writes the listed transport-change fields as XML elements whose value is carried in a val attribute. They include queued or next-track references and metadata, direct-control identity and suspension, sleep-timer generation, restart state, alarm and snooze state. Readers must inspect the attribute instead of expecting text inside the element. This documents the recovered serialization choice without claiming that attribute-valued LastChange fields are inherently incompatible with all standard parsers.
payload_formats.protocolinfo: Describes the transport and content-type vocabulary advertised for media resources. It includes direct HTTP or network-file audio, local playlists, adaptive-stream manifests and Sonos queue, group or service-reference types. Decoder integration and resource resolution determine what can actually be opened. This is therefore an advertised format vocabulary rather than a complete guarantee that every labeled resource can play on this product.
payload_formats.scpd: The service-specification documents: the advertised command lists served at /xml/*.xml, describing what the product claims to support as distinct from what the binary actually implements. This page's whole availability story rests on that comparison.
payload_formats.device_description: The root device-description document: the file every client fetches first, containing the player's self-description with its substitution tokens filled and the list of all 16 service specs it advertises.
payload_formats.sonos_alarm_doc: Wraps alarm configuration in a versioned XML document that records the last updating device and, in the Alarms form, a schema version. Related scheduler-state output describes the current clock, pending alarms, recurrence and the next UTC or local activation time. The stored configuration and current scheduling state are different views of an alarm. An alarm appearing in either document does not prove that its selected content was fetched or played.
payload_formats.savedqueues_rsq: Stores saved playlists as records with an identifier, curation information, track count and track entries, beneath a root carrying update identity, version and the next playlist identifier. The save path uses a temporary file before replacing the stored file, and loading or importing rejects invalid data. Track entries preserve references and metadata rather than copies of the audio. This reduces exposure to partial writes, but does not guarantee a valid file after every crash or that referenced content remains available.
payload_formats.sonos_saved_queue_file: Names the persistent saved-playlist store at /jffs/settings/savedqueues.rsq. Its records retain playlist identity, version information and track references, and the player validates data at boot or when importing a replicated copy. Saving uses a temporary-file replacement path. This is separate from a live queue and from the audio files referenced by the playlists; persistence of the file does not guarantee that every playlist item can still be played.
payload_formats.sonos_saved_queue_id: How a saved-playlist ID is written: 'SQ:' followed by a number. It's the identifier commands use to name which stored playlist they mean.
payload_formats.trackqueue_rsq: The live-queue persistence format: how the current play queue is written to disk. It's a transactional store with a guard mechanism so an interrupted write doesn't destroy the queue.
payload_formats.sonos_queue_doc: Writes a queue or saved-playlist record's track count as an unsigned decimal NumTracks XML attribute. The recovered emitters establish how that count is represented in output. This record alone does not establish the parser's validation rules, and a serialized count is not proof that every referenced track is accessible or playable.
payload_formats.sonos_track_summary_doc: The track-summary document roots: the envelope the player's queue-summary endpoints emit when describing what's in the queue.
payload_formats.sonos_browse_filter_vocab: Which metadata fields a browse request can ask for: the accepted filter lists (title, artist, album, duration, resource) so callers know what they can select back.
payload_formats.upnp_search_criteria_vocab: The search grammar the library accepts: which 'where' clauses a search request can legally use, namely matching by object class and reference-ID existence.
payload_formats.scrobble_submission: Submits listening records using the Audioscrobbler form protocol. The body carries a session value and indexed fields for artist, title, playback timestamp, source, rating, duration, album, track number and MusicBrainz identifier. A versioned handshake establishes session context, and a BADTIME response makes the client reread the server's HTTP Date header. This is a listening-history submission format rather than simply a live now-playing update; creating the form does not establish that the service accepted it.
payload_formats.SonosSeekTime: How a seek-time argument is written. When you scrub to a position, the time arrives as text with a specific grammar: an optional minus sign for 'go back', then numbers. The parser is strict enough that the exact accepted shapes were recovered, and this entry documents what the seek argument can legally look like.
payload_formats.SonosTrackOrdinal: How 'play track N' is expressed: the number you send to select a track by position. The parser accepts ordinary decimal text with the usual tolerance for spacing and signs, and this documents what counts as a valid track number.
payload_formats.SonosRcInstance: The instance-number convention on the volume service: the commands expect the instance to be 0 and reject anything else. It uses a different rejection code than the transport service, a quirk worth knowing when an app gets a fault back.
payload_formats.SonosRcChannel: The channel names the volume and tone commands accept: 'Master', 'LF' (left-front), 'RF' (right-front), plus some extended tokens used internally. Sending an unrecognized channel name is an error, so the accepted vocabulary is documented exactly.
payload_formats.sonos_duration_hhmmss: How durations are written: the sleep timer's hours:minutes:seconds format, where 'stop in 20 minutes' travels as 00:20:00. This documents the exact accepted shape of the duration argument.
payload_formats.sonos_iso8601_timestamps: Parses timestamp text in a compact date-time form ending in milliseconds and Z, or an extended form with date separators, time separators, milliseconds and a positive numeric offset suffix. The recovered parser consumes but discards the offset fields in the extended form. That quirk matters when interpreting a timestamp: matching the spelling is not proof that the stated offset was applied. The record describes these specific parse formats rather than general support for every ISO-8601 representation.
payload_formats.sonos_http_date: Reads server date text through three alternative parse patterns. The recovered handling includes named-month text, clock fields and a literal GMT marker in some forms. Month-letter matching accepts mixed case, while the GMT literal is case-sensitive. This supports server-clock interpretation, including the scrobbling client's time-error handling, but the existence of three patterns alone does not prove that every standards-permitted date spelling or malformed variant is accepted correctly.
payload_formats.sonos_signed_blob_json: Wraps persisted group effective-values data with a fixed magic marker, declared length, hexadecimal checksum and counter. These fields let the reader check the expected structure and detect a length or checksum mismatch. The recovered envelope is checksummed; this record does not establish a cryptographic signature simply because earlier descriptions called it signed. A checksum also does not by itself prove that a file came from an authorized writer.
payload_formats.group_effective_values_blob: Stores group effective-values data in a JSON array ending with integrity metadata and a version-11 trailer. The reader checks the trailer first, locates the header and then validates the declared length and checksum. Two output paths build the same envelope for a file or a buffer. The counter supplies sequence context, but the format alone does not establish cryptographic authenticity or every rule that rejects an older value.
payload_formats.sonos_access_settings_json: Reads a household-settings document containing update version and device identity, a restricted-admin category, its permission label and the explicit-content-filtering and recently-played values. The recovered parser first tries a fixed form with both settings, then a legacy form without recentlyPlayed. Text matching true is converted to a Boolean value. This is a specific persisted-settings grammar, rather than a generic way to configure all access permissions or all settings categories.
payload_formats.sonos_track_encryption_meta: Writes the track-encryption method and format as text inside two named XML elements. The fields describe encryption associated with the track or stream and also appear in status output. The recovered evidence establishes these emitters, with no parser site located for this format. Reporting an encryption method is separate from obtaining a key or successfully decrypting the audio.
payload_formats.sonos_state_flags: Reads named text fields for frozen, allow and auto state using an integer after each colon. The recovered keys are case-sensitive and enter the zone-player settings path, where they represent frozen state, source allowance and autoplay flags. This record establishes the field spelling and parse form; it does not define the full set of operations blocked by each flag or a combined state-machine transition.
payload_formats.sonos_audio_settings_line: The packed audio-settings line: a compact serialization stuffing every tone and volume setting into one text record, covering volume, balance, bass, treble, loudness, and the surround and sub fields in a fixed order.
payload_formats.sonos_linein_demo: The line-in demo-mode settings field: a bracketed flag the settings store carries for the line-in feature, which is stubbed on this build.
payload_formats.zone_audio_state: Reports audio state for each zone, separating the requested or unscaled volume from effective, deferred, overridden and ducked values. Other fields describe mute, EQ, loudness, stereo role, bonded subwoofers, surround levels, delay and tuning state. A separate queue block reports entry and string-storage capacity, usage, high-water marks and ownership. These snapshots help explain why visible volume or configuration differs from effective output; a reported setting is not a direct measurement of audible sound.
payload_formats.SonosAvtStateFile: The vocabulary of names used in the transport's save and restore machinery: the keys the player writes when it persists playback state so it can resume after a reboot.
payload_formats.status_doc: The complete element grammar of the diagnostics pages: every field the built-in status website can emit, so the diagnostics surface is fully documented rather than just its route list.
payload_formats.sonos_diag_filename: Parses a diagnostic filename containing an IPv4-style address followed by a date and time separated with underscores and hyphens. The recovered numeric fields have input-width limits for date and clock components, and the punctuation must match. This lets tooling recover source and timing information from the name. The grammar alone does not establish calendar validity, address validity or the time zone represented by the timestamp.
payload_formats.fixed_volume_tokens: 'FV' markers and related tokens the tone machinery parses for fixed-volume handling: the small vocabulary inside the extended-EQ router that decides when volume stays locked.
payload_formats.sonos_favorites_version: The 'FV:' version token: a marker used in two different places, inside the EQ parameter machinery and as a favorites-list version. It's documented separately so the same-looking token isn't misread.
payload_formats.contentdir_root_map: The top of the music library tree: the fixed root containers every browse starts from, including artists, albums, tracks, genres, playlists, and folders, recovered from the enumeration code.
payload_formats.sonos_metadata_urn: Recognizes the rating field in the Sonos metadata namespace using a case-sensitive namespace-and-name key. This distinguishes the intended rating element from an identically named field in another XML vocabulary. The recovered match establishes how the field is identified; it does not decode the rating values or prove whether a particular consumer uses them for display, filtering or another decision.
payload_formats.sonos_packed_object_id: This token captures what another speaker needs to take over playback: the track ordinal, byte position in the audio stream, packet cursor and playback timing, seek target, and group capabilities. Its last64 characters carry the audio-framer bookmark. The worker finishes the snapshot before it is serialized. A cloning flag can preserve the existing transmitter cursor instead of resetting it. Parsing can leave partial changes on failure, so callers must check its result.
payload_formats.sonos_hex_blob_line: This is a playback bookmark that lets the speaker recover where it was in an audio stream. For HLS it remembers the bitrate, which stream was selected, and the segment sequence. It travels with a separate byte offset. The parser accepts optional sections and trailing text, and a failed parse can leave partial data behind; callers must check its result.
payload_formats.sonos_mac_parse: Reads six hexadecimal MAC-address components separated by colons. The recovered scan accepts one or two hexadecimal digits per component, so A:B:C:D:E:F can parse as well as the usual two-digit spelling, and trailing text can be ignored. Hexadecimal letters may use either case. Other address-format literals exist, but this site establishes the colon form rather than a single strict parser for every MAC spelling.
payload_formats.sonos_mac_dash: Uses a separate scan pattern for six dash-separated hexadecimal MAC-address components, followed in the format by a colon and a discarded character. Each component has a two-character input limit. This documents the actual pattern found in the certificate or network region; it should not be simplified into a promise that any ordinary dash-separated address is accepted by the colon-form parser. Successful numeric conversion and complete consumption of all trailing syntax also need to be distinguished.
payload_formats.sonos_version_pair: Reads a version as two decimal integers separated by a dot, such as 86.10. The recovered scans use integer-conversion behavior, including leading whitespace or signs, and can ignore text after the second number. This establishes the lexical form used by those helpers. It does not by itself enforce nonnegative version components or decide whether an update is compatible.
payload_formats.sonos_https_ep: Formats a secure endpoint as https:// followed by a dotted IPv4 address and an explicit port. The recovered site is an emitter, so it establishes the text the player produces rather than the complete input grammar of a URL parser. Naming a secure endpoint is separate from connecting to it or validating its certificate.
payload_formats.sonos_http_statusline: How the player reads an HTTP status line: the 'HTTP/1.1 200' shape its own HTTP client and server machinery parses.
payload_formats.sonos_http_date_emit: Writes date text with a weekday, day, month name, four-digit year, clock time and a GMT suffix. This is the canonical server-date representation produced by the recovered helper and is related to the HTTP-date reader used in time-error handling. The format describes emitted text; it does not establish that every date read from another server must use the same spelling.
payload_formats.sonos_path_two_seg: A two-segment path split: the 'first/second' grammar used where a route or locator is divided into exactly two parts.
payload_formats.sonos_iv_token: Reads the initialization vector from an HLS EXT-X-KEY tag. The value must begin with 0x and is decoded as hexadecimal bytes until a comma or the end of the attribute text. It joins the method, key URI and key-format data used by the stream's decryption path. This is a specific HLS encryption field rather than an unidentified generic token; the related HLS player uses the segment sequence number when no IV is supplied.
payload_formats.sonos_buzzer_uri: Builds local file references for the player's alarm buzzer sounds, including the numbered MP3 assets under /opt/buzzers. The shipped inventory contains sounds 0 through 3, and the private buzzer scheme maps to these local resources. Selecting a local sound avoids downloading music from a service, while playback still requires the file and output path. The evidence does not establish a blanket prohibition on inspecting or changing those files.
payload_formats.itunes_plist_importer: Reads iTunes Library.xml or iTunes Music Library.xml, recognizing their names without case sensitivity. It walks the XML property-list structure to recover tracks, playlist identifiers, names and track membership, then maps local tracks into the content index. Nonlocal tracks are ignored, and malformed nesting, mismatched tags or exhausted storage can fail processing. The importer can expose supported library references; it does not copy all audio into the player or guarantee that every imported playlist item can be opened.
payload_formats.sonos_class_audioBook: Labels a media-description item as an audiobook using the exact object.item.audioItem.audioBook class token. Browse and search code recognize that category, and the token can appear in emitted metadata.
