It distinguishes audiobook items from other audio classes; the classification alone does not establish chapter handling, resume behavior or how every client displays the item.
payload_formats.vli_mimes: Lists content types recognized by the virtual-line-in or queue resource path, including PCM, common compressed audio formats, Spotify audio, playlists, HLS and DASH manifests. Several names are aliases for the same format family. A manifest type describes a document that leads to audio segments rather than the audio bytes themselves. Recognition by this list does not prove that an external source can push every listed type directly or that every item will decode successfully.
payload_formats.ncd_device_payload: Carries a model-specific manufacturing-configuration template inside the firmware package. The recovered data includes a board identifier, template date and time, tagged records and fields intended for device identity or calibration. Some identity locations contain erased or placeholder values for later device-specific filling. Its old date describes the template, rather than the date of the current firmware build. This is separate from the kernel and filesystem payloads, and not every calibration record has been semantically decoded.
payload_formats.http_status_map: The player's HTTP status-code tables: two parallel maps translating internal results into web status codes, covering the extended set of statuses its web layer can emit.
payload_formats.smapi_capability_bits: Combines music-service feature declarations into a bitmask. The recovered names cover search, track or album or artist favorites, extended metadata, playlists, logging, account restrictions, authorization headers, device certificates, content filtering and manifests. These declarations help select the integration behavior a service offers; for example, different favorite classes have separate bits. The name-to-bit table is decoded, but individual consumer tests still need evidence before every bit's effect can be described completely.
payload_formats.transport_action_bits: The packed transport-actions field: how the 'currently legal commands' answer is encoded as bits, and which bit means play, pause, seek, and the rest.
payload_formats.skip_restriction_bits: Represents stream-control conditions as flags for already paused, not paused, licensing restriction, advertisement, no previous track and no next track. They supply context when deciding whether playback navigation is permitted; an advertisement flag can block skipping. The table names and bit values are recovered, while a restriction message alone does not establish every priority or transition rule used when several conditions are present.
payload_formats.codec_mime_flags: Maps selected audio-format names and MIME types to classification bits. WAV aliases share one bit, WMA aliases another, and the playlist MIME type x-mpegurl has its own bit; the related format table also names ADTS. The stream-opening path uses this classification to interpret a fetched resource. These flags distinguish format families rather than promising that a valid decoder, compatible parameters and readable audio are available for every response.

state_variables.AVT.TransportState: Reports whether the transport is playing, paused, stopped or transitioning. It describes the playback state exposed to subscribers; it is not a direct measurement that audible sound is reaching every speaker, and other integrations can report their own state.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrackMetaData: Carries the current track's media description, which can include title, artist, album and artwork references. A client can use these fields to display the item, but missing metadata or additional integration-specific information means this is not necessarily the complete now-playing display.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrackURI: Names the currently selected track resource, distinct from the transport's overall source reference. For queue playback, the transport can name the queue while this value names its current item. A selected resource does not by itself establish successful downloading or audible playback.
state_variables.AVT.AVTransportURI: Names the source loaded into the transport, such as a queue, radio stream or adapted input. It identifies what the player is configured to use, while the separate transport state indicates whether it is playing. Loading a new reference and successfully starting it are different events.
state_variables.AVT.r:EnqueuedTransportURI: Reports the enqueued transport reference separately from the current source and current track. It supplies context about queued source content in the Sonos extension fields. The reference alone does not guarantee a particular switch time or that the next source will open successfully.
state_variables.AVT.TransportStatus: Reports the transport's status separately from its playing or stopped state. An error indication can add context to a stopped transport, but it is not a complete diagnosis of why playback ended; detailed error and stream information may also be needed.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTransportActions: Lists the transport actions currently advertised as available for the source and playback state. A client can use the list when presenting controls. Because state can change, the list is a snapshot of availability rather than a promise that a later command will succeed.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentPlayMode: Reports the current repeat and shuffle mode, including normal, repeat-all, repeat-one and shuffle combinations. It describes the selected playback mode rather than a guarantee about the next item, which also depends on source content and restrictions.
state_variables.AVT.NumberOfTracks: Reports the transport's current track count. It can describe queue or list content where the source supplies that information. The count is distinct from the number of tracks already played or known to be accessible.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrack: Reports the current track position within the transport's program or queue. Together with the track count it can describe a position such as track 4 of 23. This is a positional value rather than a permanent identity for the audio item.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentTrackDuration: Reports the current track's duration as text. A client can combine it with playback position when displaying progress. The value depends on available source or metadata information and should not be assumed to provide a useful finite duration for every live stream.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorHttpCode: Reports an HTTP code associated with a transport error, such as a server rejecting a resource request. It can distinguish a response from some network failures, but the code alone does not fully explain the cause or establish whether retrying will work.
state_variables.AVT.r:DirectControlClientID: Identifies the client associated with direct control in the transport's reported state. It supplies session context rather than a music-resource identity. The identifier alone does not establish the client's permissions or prove that its last command completed.
state_variables.AVT.r:SleepTimerGeneration: Reports the sleep timer's generation counter so consumers can distinguish timer-state revisions. It is separate from the timer duration or remaining time. The counter by itself does not say whether the timer is currently active or when playback will stop.
state_variables.AVT.r:AlarmRunning: Reports whether the transport considers an alarm active. It is a Sonos extension included in transport-change state, distinct from the stored alarm schedule. An active alarm flag does not by itself prove that the selected music was fetched or is audible.
state_variables.AVT.r:SnoozeRunning: Reports whether the transport considers alarm snoozing active. It distinguishes snooze state from the alarm schedule and ordinary playback state. The flag does not carry the remaining snooze duration or establish that the alarm will successfully play afterward.
state_variables.RCS.Volume: Reports the stored volume value for the master, left-front or right-front channel. It lets subscribers track channel-specific control state. Effective output can also depend on mute, ducking, gain processing and hardware limits, so this value is not a direct sound-level measurement.
state_variables.RCS.Mute: Reports the mute flag for the master, left-front or right-front channel. It describes channel control state through change notifications. The record does not establish that each physical or app action produces a separate notification, or that a cleared mute flag guarantees audible sound.
state_variables.RCS.Bass: Reports the signed bass-adjustment setting in rendering-control change state. Clients can use it to display the selected EQ value. It is a control parameter rather than a measured bass response in the room.
state_variables.RCS.Treble: Reports the signed treble-adjustment setting alongside other rendering controls. It describes the selected EQ value, rather than a measurement of high-frequency output. Subscriber updates do not guarantee that every view refreshes immediately.
state_variables.RCS.Loudness: Reports whether loudness processing is enabled for the master channel. The setting belongs to the audio EQ state; its Boolean value does not specify the resulting gain at every volume or measure how the room sounds.
state_variables.RCS.NightMode: Reports whether the home-theater night-mode setting is enabled. It supplies control state for dynamic-range handling, rather than measuring loudness or guaranteeing that every input format receives identical processing.
state_variables.RCS.DialogLevel: Reports the signed dialogue-enhancement level selected in rendering-control state. It describes a speech-related tuning parameter; the field alone does not establish its accepted range, gain in decibels or availability on every model.
state_variables.RCS.SubGain: Reports the signed subwoofer level adjustment. It is a control value relative to the rest of the configured audio system, rather than a measured bass level or proof that a subwoofer is currently connected.
state_variables.RCS.SurroundLevel: Reports the selected surround-level adjustment. It describes a control value for the surround path; connected-speaker state and other processing determine the resulting output.
state_variables.RCS.SurroundEnabled: Reports the surround-enable setting in rendering-control state. It should be read separately from whether surround devices are present, reachable or receiving audio; the setting alone does not establish those conditions.
state_variables.RCS.AudioDelay: Reports the configured audio-delay value used in the home-theater path. The setting can help compensate for timing differences between TV picture and sound, but it is not a measurement of current lip-sync error or proof that synchronization is correct.
state_variables.RCS.SonarEnabled: Reports whether the sonar or room-calibration processing setting is enabled. It is separate from calibration availability and session progress. An enabled flag does not by itself prove that a fresh calibration completed successfully.
state_variables.RCS.PresetNameList: Reports the names of presets exposed by the rendering-control service. The recovered event vocabulary includes FactoryDefaults. This names selectable presets rather than proving that the product offers a broad set of user-defined or one-touch sound modes.
state_variables.CD.FavoritesUpdateID: Reports the revision marker for the favorites collection. A changed marker tells a consumer that its cached collection may need refreshing. It is distinct from the identity of a favorite or a guarantee about which individual item changed.
state_variables.CD.RadioFavoritesUpdateID: Reports the revision marker for radio favorites, separately from the general favorites collection. Consumers can compare it with a cached value when deciding to refresh. The marker does not itself contain the station list or guarantee that every app refreshes it immediately.
state_variables.CD.SavedQueuesUpdateID: Reports the revision marker for saved playlists. It lets consumers detect a different saved-queue version without interpreting the entire store. The value alone does not identify the edited playlist or prove that every player has already replicated the change.
state_variables.CD.ShareListUpdateID: Reports the revision marker for the configured music-share list. A consumer can use a changed value to invalidate a cached list. This is separate from music-index progress and does not prove that newly added files have already been indexed.
state_variables.CD.ShareIndexInProgress: Reports music-share indexing state as a string. It can inform a client that a library update is in progress. This status is distinct from the eventual result, so starting or observing a rescan does not guarantee that every folder is reachable or every file is indexed.
state_variables.CD.ContainerUpdateIDs: Reports change markers associated with library containers so consumers can identify cached portions that may need refreshing. The list concerns container versions, rather than an exhaustive history of every edit since a particular client last checked. Refresh policy remains the consumer's responsibility.
state_variables.GRC.GroupVolume: Reports the group-level volume value separately from individual member volume settings. It provides group-control context, while differences between member levels and local output processing can affect what each room sounds like. The field alone does not specify the aggregation formula.
state_variables.GRC.GroupMute: Reports the group mute state through event updates. It describes the state exposed by group control, rather than proof that every member has applied the change or every controller has already received it.
state_variables.GRC.GroupVolumeChangeable: Reports whether group control currently advertises that its volume can be changed. A client can use it when presenting a group slider. It is a snapshot of capability state, rather than a guarantee that a later volume request is accepted.
state_variables.Queue.QueueID: The identifier of the queue being described, naming which managed queue an event or answer refers to.
state_variables.Queue.UpdateID: Reports a queue revision value that distinguishes versions of its contents. Operations that check an expected revision can use it to detect stale edits. This value alone does not establish that every operation performs that check or that all lost updates are impossible.
state_variables.Queue.Curated: Reports the queue's curated marker as a Boolean. It distinguishes that queue property from its identifier and revision. The flag alone does not establish who manages the queue or which edits its policy permits.
state_variables.GM.LocalGroupUUID: Names the local player's reported group identity. Consumers can use it to relate the player to group membership and coordinator information. It is distinct from the player's own identity, and the field alone does not define when every grouping operation commits.
state_variables.GM.DelegatedGroupCoordinatorID: Identifies the coordinator target associated with delegated group leadership. It provides handoff context alongside the group identity. Naming a target is separate from proving that the target has completed takeover or every member has followed it.
state_variables.GM.VirtualLineInGroupID: Names the group context associated with virtual-line-in playback. It links that adapted audio session to group-control state. The identifier does not itself say whether the source is active, which input supplied it or whether audio delivery succeeded.
state_variables.ZGT.ZoneGroupState: Carries a serialized topology snapshot with groups, coordinators and player information such as identity and room name. Clients can use it to construct a household or group view. The document reports the topology known to its producer, rather than guaranteeing immediate knowledge of every player or one notification for every underlying change.
state_variables.DP.CurrentZoneName: Reports the local player's room or zone name, such as Kitchen. It is a display label distinct from the device's stable identity. A changed label can be distributed to subscribers, but the field does not guarantee that every controller has already refreshed its display.
state_variables.DP.MicEnabled: Reports a microphone-enabled setting where the product supports a microphone. This model has no microphone, so the shared variable vocabulary should not be read as evidence of physical voice-input hardware on it.
state_variables.DP.Invisible: Reports the player's hidden-status flag, which can help represent bonded members without showing each as an independent room. It describes presentation or topology state rather than absence from the network. The flag alone does not establish how every client chooses to display the member.
state_variables.AC.AlarmListVersion: Reports the revision marker of the alarm collection. Consumers can compare it with a cached version when deciding to reread the list. The marker does not identify a particular alarm change or establish whether an alarm has fired.
state_variables.AC.TimeServer: Reports the configured time-server value. It identifies intended clock-source configuration, separately from whether the time client has reached that server or synchronized successfully.
state_variables.MS.ServiceListVersion: Reports the revision marker of the music-service catalog. It lets consumers detect a different catalog version and refresh cached descriptors. The value does not itself establish account login, subscription status or playback availability.
state_variables.HT.RemoteConfigured: Reports whether the player considers its infrared remote configured. It describes setup state, rather than proof that every button on the remote has been learned, saved or recognized. Client setup decisions require that context rather than an assumed universal wizard rule.
state_variables.HT.LEDFeedbackState: Reports the home-theater LED-feedback setting as a string. It concerns indicator feedback associated with control activity, rather than the instantaneous electrical state of a light. The value does not guarantee that each received remote command produces a visible flash.
state_variables.AI.TOSLinkConnected: Whether something is plugged into the optical input, which is the line-in detection flag. It is part of the AudioIn surface that is a reject-everything stub on this firmware.
state_variables.AI.IRRepeaterState: Whether the infrared repeater is currently on. It mirrors the home-theater IR setting so a change shows up as an event, though it is dead on this build along with the rest of the AudioIn surface.
state_variables.RCS.OutputFixed: Reports the fixed-output setting where that mode is supported. Fixed output differs from ordinary adjustable volume control, but the variable alone does not establish the physical output type or imply that this model has a line-level connector.
state_variables.RCS.SpeakerSize: Reports the speaker-size classification used by audio configuration. It supplies a control parameter relevant to channel or bass handling; the reported number is not a measurement of the enclosure and this record does not decode every accepted value.
state_variables.RCS.SubCrossover: Reports the selected subwoofer crossover setting. It concerns how frequency content is divided between the subwoofer and other speakers. The value is configuration, rather than proof that a subwoofer is connected or a measurement of the current acoustic crossover response.
state_variables.RCS.SubPolarity: Reports the selected subwoofer polarity setting. It distinguishes the intended polarity or inversion configuration from the subwoofer level and crossover. It does not by itself guarantee phase alignment at every frequency or listening position.
state_variables.RCS.SubEnabled: Reports the subwoofer-enable setting. It describes whether configuration allows the subwoofer path to participate, separately from bonding, reachability and successful audio delivery.
state_variables.RCS.SpeechEnhanceEnabled: Reports whether speech-enhancement processing is enabled. It is separate from the dialogue-level amount, allowing consumers to distinguish the feature switch from its tuning value.
state_variables.RCS.SupportsMaxDialogLevel: Reports whether the device advertises support for the maximum dialogue-level option. It is a capability indicator, separate from whether speech enhancement is enabled or which level is selected.
state_variables.RCS.MusicSurroundLevel: Reports the signed surround-level adjustment for music playback. It is separate from the surround-mode selection, so the amount of adjustment should not be confused with the ambient or full-mode choice.
state_variables.RCS.AudioDelayLeftRear: Reports the configured delay for the left rear audio path. It provides a separate timing setting from the main audio delay and right rear delay; it is not a measurement of current synchronization error.
state_variables.RCS.AudioDelayRightRear: Reports the configured delay for the right rear audio path. Together with the separate left rear setting it describes channel-specific timing configuration, rather than proving that the rear speakers are currently synchronized.
state_variables.RCS.SurroundMode: Reports the selected surround mode, including the music behavior described as ambient or full. It is distinct from the surround level and enable setting, which describe other parts of the configuration.
state_variables.RCS.HeightChannelLevel: Reports a height-channel level setting in the shared rendering-control vocabulary. The field can exist in firmware without this product having physical height speakers; its presence should not be used to infer hardware support.
state_variables.RCS.SonarCalibrationAvailable: Reports the room-calibration availability flag. It is distinct from calibration being enabled, a session running or a tuning being applied successfully. The flag alone does not explain every condition that makes calibration available.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentCrossfadeMode: Reports whether the crossfade setting is selected. It concerns blending at track transitions, while source compatibility and the playback path determine whether a particular transition actually crossfades.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentSection: Reports the transport's current section value separately from the current track. It provides position context for sources with sections, but the shared field does not establish one universal mapping from section numbers to chapters or audio segments.
state_variables.AVT.r:EnqueuedTransportURIMetaData: Carries metadata associated with the enqueued transport reference. It describes that source separately from the current track and current source metadata. Availability of a description does not prove the enqueued source will open or start.
state_variables.AVT.PlaybackStorageMedium: Reports the storage-medium label associated with the current transport. It adds source-category context alongside the resource reference. The label alone does not establish a reachable file, current network connection or complete path to the audio.
state_variables.AVT.AVTransportURIMetaData: Carries the media description associated with the overall loaded source. For a queue or collection it can describe that source rather than just the currently selected song. It is separate from CurrentTrackMetaData, and individual descriptive fields may be missing.
state_variables.AVT.NextAVTransportURI: Reports the next transport reference when one is supplied. It is lookahead state, distinct from the current source and track. This variable alone does not establish prebuffering, gapless playback or a guarantee that the referenced content will start next.
state_variables.AVT.NextAVTransportURIMetaData: Carries descriptive metadata for the next transport reference. A consumer can show available title or artwork information before a transition. That description is separate from whether the next resource has been fetched or can play.
state_variables.AVT.r:CurrentValidPlayModes: Lists the play modes currently advertised as valid for the transport. It lets consumers distinguish available repeat or shuffle choices from the currently selected mode. The list is a state-dependent report rather than proof of one fixed policy for every live stream or service.
state_variables.AVT.r:DirectControlIsSuspended: Reports the suspended flag for direct control. It should be interpreted alongside transport state and direct-control identity, rather than assumed to mean only an ordinary pause or to guarantee how long the session remains available.
state_variables.AVT.r:DirectControlAccountID: Reports the account identifier associated with direct-control state. It is distinct from the controlling client and the media resource. The value alone does not establish account permissions, subscription validity or successful audio delivery.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorDescription: Carries descriptive text associated with a transport error. It can supplement the error code and failing resource reference, but is not a complete recovery instruction or proof that the same message has one cause across all sources.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorURI: Names the resource associated with a transport error. It helps relate a failure to a stream or item, separately from the currently loaded source. The reference identifies context rather than proving whether the resource is permanently unavailable.
state_variables.AVT.TransportErrorHttpHeaders: Carries HTTP response-header text associated with a transport failure. It provides extra server-response context alongside the error code and resource reference, rather than a complete history of every request involved in the failure.
state_variables.AVT.r:RestartPending: Reports that a source or endpoint change requires playback to restart instead of continuing through a seamless handoff. The setting is produced in endpoint selection and transport-settings restoration. It concerns playback restart, rather than a pending reboot of the whole player.
state_variables.AVT.r:NextTrackURI: Names the next-track reference in the Sonos transport extensions. It is track-level lookahead state, distinct from the overall next transport reference. The field alone does not prove that both references are identical or that the next track is already buffered.
state_variables.AVT.r:NextTrackMetaData: Carries descriptive metadata associated with the next-track reference. It provides track-level lookahead separately from next-source metadata, and the description can be available before the audio resource is successfully opened.
state_variables.AVT.TransportPlaySpeed: Reports the fixed normal-speed value emitted by this build's transport-change template. It represents normal playback rather than an independently changing speed field. Its presence does not establish a variable-speed playback implementation.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentMediaDuration: Emits the fixed not-implemented value for whole-media duration in this build. Track duration is reported separately. This distinguishes an unsupported aggregate-duration field from a changing track-length measurement.
state_variables.AVT.RecordStorageMedium: Emits a fixed value indicating no recording medium in this transport interface. It is part of the shared transport schema, rather than evidence of an active recording destination. It says nothing about separate diagnostic audio-capture facilities.
state_variables.AVT.PossiblePlaybackStorageMedia: Emits the fixed list NONE, NETWORK in this build's transport-change template. This is a broad storage-medium declaration, separate from codec and URI capability lists. It does not enumerate every input type or guarantee that a network resource is playable.
state_variables.AVT.PossibleRecordStorageMedia: Emits the fixed recording-medium declaration used by this transport interface. It does not advertise an active recording path. The field should be distinguished from diagnostic capture or other internal data recording.
state_variables.AVT.RecordMediumWriteStatus: Emits a fixed recording-medium status in the transport-change template. It is a schema field rather than a live indication that this interface is writing audio to a medium.
state_variables.AVT.CurrentRecordQualityMode: Emits the fixed not-implemented recording-quality value in this build. It describes the transport interface's recording field, without ruling out separate internal capture tools or implying a selectable recording quality.
state_variables.AVT.PossibleRecordQualityModes: Emits the fixed recording-quality declaration in the transport-change template. This is separate from playback codec support and does not establish an operational recording-quality selector.
state_variables.Queue.QueueOwnerID: Names the reported owner associated with a queue. It supplies ownership context separately from the queue identifier and update revision. The field alone does not prove which caller has edit rights or which ownership policy is enforced.
state_variables.AC.TimeFormat: Reports the configured clock-display format. It is presentation state, such as a 12-hour or 24-hour convention, rather than a change to the underlying time or time zone.
state_variables.AC.TimeGeneration: Reports a generation value associated with clock state. Consumers can compare it to distinguish clock-state revisions. It does not itself specify how far time moved or establish the complete set of changes that increment it.
state_variables.AC.DateFormat: Reports the configured date-display format. It supplies presentation preferences separately from the stored date-time value and time zone. A client can use the setting without inferring a format solely from locale.
state_variables.CM.CurrentConnectionIDs: Reports connection identifiers through the ConnectionManager state interface. It gives context for that service's connection model, rather than a complete list of HTTP sockets or proof that every control-session open and close produces a notification.
state_variables.DP.ResetVolumeAfter: Reports a settings-backed flag controlling restoration of volume after the relevant boot or playback path. It describes intended restoration behavior rather than the restored value itself. The flag should not be assumed to apply to every alarm, autoplay or interruption without its consumer context.
state_variables.renderingcontrol_status_schema: The fields on the diagnostics page for the volume and tone service. It is the player's internal view of channel volumes, mutes, EQ values, and flags, exposed for support and debugging.
state_variables.playstatemanager_schema: Shows the play-state manager's activity mask and its playback and information counts. Changes identify activity that started or stopped, rather than a detailed map of titles, rooms or queue positions. The associated crash-state file records this compact activity context and does not restore the music queue.
state_variables.alarm_status_schema: Reports scheduler mode, UTC and local time, and pending alarm entries with identity, type, recurrence and next activation times. Types include ordinary or expired alarms and voice-assistant or Muse timers. This is a scheduling snapshot, rather than proof that the selected audio is currently audible or that every pending entry will fire.
state_variables.zone_group_state_schema: Organizes a topology snapshot into groups with coordinator and member identities, plus player names, versions, network roles and selected feature state. Separate sections record vanished or quarantined devices with reasons and last-seen information. Consumers can distinguish known members from unavailable records; the snapshot does not guarantee immediate agreement across all players.
state_variables.zoneplayers_status_schema: Lists the players known to the reporting device with group membership, network state, discovery information, versions, compatibility and identity. Vanished-player entries retain departure reasons, elapsed time and selected battery context. This is the reporting player's census, rather than proof that every listed player is currently reachable.
state_variables.device_props_update_ids: The set of change-counters the device-properties service keeps. These version numbers tick when different aspects of the speaker's config change, so interested parties can tell what moved without comparing every field.
state_variables.update_info_schema: Shows automatic-update enablement, scheduler state, the configured window, upgrade-manager state, time pending and the active-device list. These fields help explain an update waiting for its opportunity to run. They do not themselves provide a complete installation history or prove that a pending update will finish.
state_variables.sounddevice_status_schema: Reports audio state per local zone, including unscaled, effective, deferred, ducked and overridden volume, mute, external-source volume, surround level and channel count. It allows diagnostics to compare selected control values with the state used by the output path. It is not a census of every player's physical sound level.
state_variables.replicated_netsettings_schema: Describes shared network configuration with update version and device identity, SonosNet enablement and frequency, network SSIDs and flags, and household, control, room or swap key identifiers. Current and backup key fields support the configuration lifecycle. Replication distributes this state, but the document alone does not guarantee that every member has applied the same settings or can join the network.
state_variables.vli_state_snapshot: Captures virtual-line-in source type, origin and seek times, stream byte offset, packet and frame position, account context, playing state and bitrate. Those values describe a session at the snapshot point and can support handoff or resumption. The snapshot is not itself proof that restoration or subsequent audio delivery succeeded.
state_variables.shares_schema: Lists configured music shares with path, credentials, identity and verified protocol information, plus index-display and sorting settings. A shorter status form reports a path and mount. Shared configuration tells players where to attempt library access; it does not prove that credentials remain valid, every share is mounted or indexing completed.
state_variables.device_props_extra_vars: Additional device-property fields the settings service carries beyond the standard set: the extra bits of speaker configuration reported alongside the usual name, LED, and button state.
state_variables.savedqueues_rsq_schema: Stores saved playlists as queue records with identifiers, curation data, track count and track URI or metadata entries. Root fields track update identity, version and the next identifier. Loading checks identifiers and counts and can reject corruption; migration updates service or account references. The file preserves playlist descriptions rather than audio, so a valid store can still contain unavailable items.
state_variables.services_xml_schema: Describes the music-service catalog with update version, schema version and entity tag, plus service identifiers, totals and presentation or endpoint information. Individual descriptors can specify polling, manifests, strings and container type. It identifies known integrations, separately from the user's account credentials or successful access to those services.
state_variables.userradio_schema: Stores favorite radio or content references with identity, title, URI and selected metadata such as type, description, room and play mode. The vocabulary includes stations, shows and broader favorite categories such as tracks, albums, playlists and audiobooks. These are saved references and preferences; the format does not guarantee that every item remains playable or establish one universal incremental-write strategy.
state_variables.zpinfo_schema: Reports player identity, software and hardware versions, manufacturing information, capabilities and network addressing. Related blocks expose play-mode settings, temperature history and hardware status. These fields help identify the reporting device and its configuration; capability flags and reported state should be distinguished from a live test of every advertised feature.
state_variables.netsettings_schema: Represents shared network configuration with SonosNet settings, known network SSIDs and flags, and current or backup household, control, room and swap key identifiers. Related JSON fields record network groups and key-generation time. This schema identifies the configuration and key families; the fields shown alone do not prove where every Wi-Fi password is stored or how each value is encrypted.
state_variables.avt_lastchange: Bundles transport state, source and track references, metadata, modes, error context and Sonos extension flags into one XML change document. The recovered emitter rebuilds the document from current values and fixed template fields rather than sending an independent notification for each variable. A consumer reads value attributes to reconstruct state; it is not a chronological list of only the fields that changed.
state_variables.zp_support_info: Wraps support information as titled items within a ZPSupportInfo document. The item structure lets collection tools organize diagnostic sections from the player. The wrapper alone does not define every section's contents or guarantee that a submission includes all devices and all available diagnostic data.
state_variables.zps_page: Shows update reports with system and target versions, player counts, hardware version, download duration, server address and error information. The reporting path checks response type and array size and can fail reading or renaming a report. This is status derived from update-manager results rather than proof that every displayed player has reached its target version.
state_variables.ht_input_session: Records a home-theater input session with correlation identity, total and playing durations, connection and content type, input rate, group-coordinator identity and start or end times. Forced-report and topology fields add context. These measurements describe a TV-audio session, rather than a complete dump of every decoder, HDMI or hardware state.

muse_resources.alarms: Lists, fetches, creates, updates and removes household alarm objects, with a separate operation to snooze an alarm for a group. Reported states distinguish pending, snoozed, firing and disabled alarms. Saving an alarm or receiving an operation result is separate from successfully playing its selected content at the scheduled time.
muse_resources.areas: Creates, lists, updates and removes household area objects. An area is part of the stored organization of the household, distinct from an active playback group. The recovered resource does not establish how a particular app presents areas or promise that it corresponds to a newer app migration.
muse_resources.audioClip: Requests loading or cancellation of an audio clip for a selected player. It provides a short-audio operation in the public API, rather than evidence that a clip is uploaded to every household speaker or always plays over existing audio. Eligibility, resource access and playback outcome belong to the clip implementation.
muse_resources.authorization: The sign-in and credential surface for the modern API, where API keys and authorization tokens are issued, presented, and checked. Every other resource group in the modern API trusts the credentials established here, so this is the foundation under the whole security model: get a valid credential here first, or nothing else will talk to you.
muse_resources.catalog: Translates music-service content identifiers individually or in batches within a service context. It connects an identifier to the corresponding catalog representation. These recovered operations are translation requests, rather than a complete set of folder-browsing or searching operations.
muse_resources.devices: Lists device information and manages registration lifecycle operations, including initiation, completion, refresh, transfer, status lookup and removal. Household, player and user context distinguish the affected registration. A registration request or listed device is separate from successful certificate installation, network reachability and playback readiness.
muse_resources.devicesExtended: Reads extended device status for a household. It is a separate resource from the basic device listing. The recovered operation establishes that extended status can be requested, but the resource name alone does not specify every returned field or guarantee that all device details are present.
muse_resources.diagnostics: Requests diagnostic submission, reads diagnostic metadata and reports submission status for a player. These operations participate in the diagnostic collection pipeline. A submission request does not guarantee a complete report from every household device, and the status must be checked separately.
muse_resources.effectiveSettings: Settings as the speaker actually applies them: the resolved result after defaults, household values, group values, and device-level overrides are merged into one answer. Reading 'the setting' here gives the value that governs real behavior rather than what some screen last typed, which is why automation and the app prefer this surface for checking current state.
muse_resources.entitlements: Reads entitlement data in household or user context. The data supplies input to feature and policy decisions, separately from a product's physical hardware capabilities. The recovered operations do not establish that every feature flag or regional rule is represented by this resource.
muse_resources.favorites: Reads household favorites and requests loading a favorite for a group. The recovered operations concern retrieving and using saved references. They do not themselves establish API operations for adding or deleting favorites, and loading a favorite is separate from successful playback.
muse_resources.groupVolume: Reads group volume and requests absolute or relative volume changes and mute changes. These operations address the group-level control rather than a single member's slider. Per-member application and current group state determine the result, so a request does not guarantee identical levels or simultaneous changes in every room.
muse_resources.groups: Lists groups, creates a group and requests replacement or modification of its membership. Household and group identities select the relevant scope. A membership request is distinct from the topology having settled and every member receiving synchronized audio.
muse_resources.hardwareStatus: Reads supported hardware state such as battery, Bluetooth, Ethernet, wireless, line-in, microphone switch, power-over-Ethernet, water sensor and wired-subwoofer status. It also includes paired-device actions and selected shutdown or ship-mode requests. The shared resource vocabulary spans products; an operation can require hardware this model does not have.
muse_resources.hdmi: Exposes HDMI status, EDID information and a power-cycle operation for a selected player. These functions inspect or act on the HDMI path where supported. Their presence in the shared API does not establish HDMI hardware on this optical-input model or a complete interface for every TV-audio setting.
muse_resources.history: Reads, posts, removes individual entries and clears household playback-history data. Entries carry content and playback context rather than copies of the audio. This is household history management, not proof that every audible event is recorded or that the local player alone supplies all history.
muse_resources.homeTheater: Reads or changes home-theater options, checks TV audio signal state and requests TV-related playback or power changes. It also lists and manages accessories and exposes swap-related information. These operations address configuration and lifecycle requests; model capabilities and current topology still determine which can succeed.
muse_resources.householdUpdate: Requests the start of a household software update and reads its rollout status. The associated status vocabulary distinguishes download, flash write, reboot, errors and completion. Starting the update is one milestone, while finishing all eligible devices is a later outcome reported separately.
muse_resources.households: Lists household objects, reads a selected household and its location, and requests name or location changes. The household identity supplies context for related player, group and service resources. A household-scoped operation can still affect particular members, so scope alone does not imply that every player changes.
muse_resources.info: Reads information associated with a selected player through the info resource. Returned descriptions can identify resources and content with names, metadata, images and service or account context where the implementation supplies them. The resource should not be reduced to a universal basic-device roster or assumed to return the same fields for every request.
muse_resources.ircontrol: Reads and changes infrared-control configuration for a player. It belongs to the remote-control setup and behavior described in the infrared records. The two recovered operations do not by themselves establish a complete learning sequence or guarantee that changed configuration has been saved and recognized by the hardware.
muse_resources.localContentLibrary: Lists, adds and removes music shares, requests reindexing and reads indexer status. Status distinguishes stages such as adding, reindexing, replication and deletion. These operations manage library access and maintenance, rather than a complete content-browsing API. Adding a share is separate from reaching it and indexing its files.
muse_resources.management: Requests reboot or factory reset of a selected player. Both are maintenance operations with consequences beyond changing one setting. The resource identifies these requests; its name and route inventory alone do not establish that every API call uses the same authorization rules or that accepting a request proves the reset completed.
muse_resources.musicServiceAccounts: Streaming-service accounts over the modern API: the JSON version of the account-management family, covering adding a service login, replacing credentials, setting a nickname, and removing an account. These are the routes behind the app's service account settings.
muse_resources.networkTest: Starts network tests, reads their results and includes an operation to temporarily disable networking. It separates requesting a test from retrieving its outcome. The recovered operation names do not specify every probe or prove that a result can conclusively attribute a playback failure to the network.
muse_resources.pinewood: Exposes remote-like controls under the Pinewood codename: directional navigation, back, home, settings, power, volume, mute, play toggle and resource loading. The operations describe a player-scoped control vocabulary. Their presence does not by itself identify every physical remote or prove that all functions apply to this product.
muse_resources.platformInternal: Internal platform routes: operations meant for Sonos's own components rather than apps. It's the back-channel surface of the modern API, used for system-level coordination between the player's own parts and Sonos's services.
muse_resources.playback: Controls a group's playback with play, pause, toggle, seek, skip and play-mode requests, and reads playback status. Separate loading operations handle containers, content, streams, track lists and line-in. Status distinguishes idle, buffering, paused and playing. A load or play request remains separate from resolving the content, passing source restrictions and producing audio.
muse_resources.playbackExtended: Reads extended playback status for a group. It is an additional status resource, not a recovered collection of extra session-control or source-management commands. The returned data must be interpreted separately from whether a later playback request succeeds.
muse_resources.playbackMetadata: Reads metadata status for group playback and sends a rating operation. Metadata supplies descriptive context for the selected content, while rating is a separate request whose accepted meaning depends on the source. The resource does not guarantee complete artwork or title data for every stream.
muse_resources.playbackSession: Creates, joins, rejoins, leaves or suspends playback sessions, and loads stream URLs or cloud queues into them. Other operations refresh a cloud queue, seek or skip to an item, with variants carrying additional context or item windows. Session membership and content loading are separate stages; requesting them does not prove the stream is available or all group members are playing.
muse_resources.playerVolume: Reads a player's volume and requests absolute or relative changes, mute, duck or unduck. Ducking changes temporary attenuation separately from the normal volume setting. The operations affect player control state, while hardware limits, grouping and active audio processing determine the resulting output.
muse_resources.playlists: Lists or reads playlist objects, posts playlist data and requests loading a playlist for a group. These operations use stored content references rather than uploading the audio itself. The recovered resource does not establish a delete operation, and loading a playlist is separate from playing every referenced item successfully.
muse_resources.positioning: Manages acoustic positioning sessions and measurements. Operations start or cancel a session, play a stimulus, exchange measurements, report session or device status, and read capabilities or stimulus tuning. This supports determining position from measured sound, rather than simply assigning a named surround role. Valid capability and measurement data are needed before a useful result can be inferred.
muse_resources.power: Requests a power-policy change for a selected player. The recovered resource is a policy-setting operation, rather than a full set of standby, sleep and power-status reads. Applying a policy and entering a particular power state are separate behaviors.
muse_resources.roomDetection: Starts or stops an acoustic signalling instance for a selected player. The underlying signal path uses a playback identifier and channel selection and allows only one signal at a time. This controls the chirp used for room detection; it does not itself return a completed identification or positioning result.
muse_resources.settings: General settings over the modern API: the player's configuration as readable and writable JSON settings rather than one command per knob. It's the consolidated settings surface the app prefers.
muse_resources.sleepTimer: Reads or configures a sleep timer for a group. The timer is intended to end or alter playback after its configured interval, separately from the current playback position. The operation inventory does not by itself specify every cancellation value or guarantee that a timer request is accepted in all transport states.
muse_resources.smartplay: Requests content for a household through the SmartPlay resource. The associated loader can use a response when a button trigger or empty transport needs content. This operation obtains a content choice; it does not establish how recommendations are selected or guarantee that loading and playback follow successfully.
muse_resources.soundSwap: Requests or triggers a swap for a selected player. The underlying controller checks source and topology eligibility and tracks the handoff through its own progress state. The public request is therefore separate from a completed transfer, and unsuitable audio or an active swap can prevent it.
muse_resources.svc: An internal service-level group: routes that don't fit a named resource, used for operations scoped to the API itself rather than to a thing like 'playback' or 'alarms'.
muse_resources.systemReporting: Reports product events, account-subscription information and firmware or software-download information. These operations identify particular reporting categories rather than a general transport for every health or usage record. Reporter configuration and submission policy still determine what is sent.
muse_resources.systemTime: Reads or sets time-zone information in household context. It manages the clock's zone configuration, rather than a complete interface for reading or manually setting the current UTC time. Applying the configuration and synchronizing the clock are separate steps.
muse_resources.time: Reads a player's relative-time value. That operation provides timing context rather than a calendar timestamp or time-zone configuration. The recovered resource should not be described as a complete replacement for the classic date and time getters.
muse_resources.timers: Creates and lists timers, pauses or resumes them, aborts them and changes duration by an absolute or relative request. This is a timer lifecycle exposed to clients, distinct from the internal maintenance-job scheduler. A created timer is not proof that its later action has completed.
muse_resources.trueplay: Reads or changes Trueplay configuration, reads status and performs speaker-presence or speaker-detection operations. It can reset a detected-speaker record or set the presence rate. These operations are parts of calibration configuration and observation, rather than proof that the API exposes every measurement and tuning step or that this model supports them all.
muse_resources.trueroom: Exposes room-correction adaptation, estimator configuration, calibration status, a success-tone operation and swap-input mute control. The recovered names identify the available operations. They do not establish a historical sequence in which Trueroom predates Trueplay, nor guarantee that requesting adaptation produces a valid calibration.
muse_resources.update: Checks for an update, requests the start of a software update and reads update status for a player. These are separate stages, with status needed to distinguish progress from completion or error. The operation list does not imply a separate client command for every download or flash-write step.

muse_resources.virtualRemoteControl: Sends a button-command request to a selected player. muse_resources.voice: Lists, creates, updates or removes voice accounts, creates an Amazon challenge and notifies the start of onboarding. muse_resources.zones: Reads and changes zone definitions, activates or deactivates zones, joins or unjoins them, and updates active-zone or member settings.
